products.name: trading_restriction
products.description: This association product represents the regulatory and compliance-driven restriction relationship between financial instruments and bank employees. It captures personal account dealing rules, insider trading prevention controls, and conflict-of-interest restrictions mandated by SEC Rule 10b-5, FINRA Rule 5280 (Personal Trading), MiFID II Article 19, and internal compliance policies. Each record links one instrument to one employee with restriction type, reason, effective dates, approval workflow status, and pre-clearance requirements. This is the authoritative source for pre-trade compliance checks, restricted list management, and audit trail for employee trading restrictions. Consumed by compliance monitoring, trade surveillance, and personal account dealing systems.. Existence Justification: In banking operations, employees can be restricted from trading multiple securities simultaneously due to material non-public information (MNPI) exposure, role-based conflicts (e.g., investment banking relationships, board memberships), or insider status. Conversely, each security can have multiple restricted employees at any given time based on their roles, project assignments, or information access. This is an operational compliance relationship actively managed by compliance officers through restricted lists, pre-clearance workflows, and trade surveillance systems.

attributes.name: trading_restriction_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the trading restriction record. Primary key for the association.

attributes.name: created_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: User ID of the compliance officer or system process that created the restriction record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the employee who is restricted from trading the instrument.

attributes.name: instrument_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the financial instrument that is subject to trading restrictions for the employee.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: User ID of the compliance officer who last modified the restriction record. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the restriction record. PENDING indicates awaiting compliance officer review. APPROVED indicates active restriction. REJECTED indicates restriction request denied. EXPIRED indicates restriction passed expiry_date. REVOKED indicates manual early termination. Drives pre-trade compliance logic.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the restriction record was created. Used for audit trail and regulatory examination.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the trading restriction becomes active and enforceable. Used for pre-trade compliance checks to determine if restriction applies to a proposed trade.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the trading restriction automatically expires and is no longer enforceable. Null for indefinite restrictions that require manual removal. Used for automated restriction lifecycle management.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp of the last modification to the restriction record. Used for audit trail and regulatory examination.

attributes.name: pre_clearance_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the employee must obtain explicit compliance approval before executing any trade in this instrument. True for high-risk scenarios (MNPI exposure, investment banking relationships). False for watch-list monitoring without pre-approval requirement. Drives pre-trade compliance workflow routing.

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific regulatory rule or internal policy that mandates this restriction (e.g., 'SEC Rule 10b-5', 'FINRA 5280', 'Internal Policy PAD-2023-01'). Used for regulatory examination and policy compliance reporting.

attributes.name: restriction_reason
attributes.description: Business justification for imposing the trading restriction. Examples include: 'Employee has MNPI due to M&A advisory role', 'Conflict of interest - employee on issuer board', 'Investment banking relationship', 'Insider status per Section 16', 'Research coverage restriction', 'Personal account dealing rule violation'. Used for audit trail and regulatory examination.

attributes.name: restriction_type
attributes.description: Classification of the trading restriction imposed on the employee for this instrument. BLACKOUT indicates temporary prohibition during material non-public information (MNPI) exposure. PRE_CLEARANCE_REQUIRED mandates approval before trading. PROHIBITED indicates permanent ban due to role-based conflicts. WATCH_LIST indicates heightened monitoring without prohibition. COOLING_OFF indicates post-transaction restriction period.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the system that originated the restriction (e.g., 'COMPLIANCE_PORTAL', 'TRADE_SURVEILLANCE', 'HR_SYSTEM'). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

products.name: constituent
products.description: This association product represents the membership relationship between a financial instrument and a benchmark index. It captures the operational reality that instruments are included in indices with specific weights, inclusion/exclusion dates, and rebalancing events. Each record links one instrument to one benchmark with attributes that exist only in the context of this index membership relationship. This is the authoritative source for index composition used by passive portfolio management, ETF basket construction, benchmark attribution, and index tracking operations.. Existence Justification: In banking operations, financial instruments are constituents of multiple benchmark indices simultaneously (e.g., Apple stock is in S&P 500, NASDAQ-100, MSCI World), and each index contains hundreds or thousands of instrument constituents. Index administrators actively manage constituent membership through scheduled rebalancing events, corporate action adjustments, and liquidity screens. Each instrument-benchmark pairing has unique relationship data including weight percentage, inclusion/exclusion dates, free-float factors, and rebalancing event history that belongs to neither the instrument nor the benchmark alone.

attributes.name: constituent_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this index constituent membership record. Primary key.

attributes.name: benchmark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the benchmark index that contains this instrument as a constituent

attributes.name: instrument_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the financial instrument that is a constituent member of the benchmark index

attributes.name: constituent_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this constituent membership record. Active constituents are included in index calculations; pending additions/removals reflect announced but not yet effective changes.

attributes.name: effective_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when this constituent record or weight change became effective. Critical for intraday index rebalancing and real-time index calculation.

attributes.name: exclusion_date
attributes.description: The effective date when this instrument was removed from the benchmark index. Null if the instrument is still an active constituent. Used for historical analysis and rebalancing event tracking.

attributes.name: free_float_factor
attributes.description: The free-float adjustment factor applied to this constituent for indices using free-float market capitalization weighting. Represents the proportion of shares available for public trading (excludes strategic holdings, government ownership, cross-holdings).

attributes.name: inclusion_date
attributes.description: The effective date when this instrument was added to the benchmark index. Critical for historical index composition reconstruction and performance attribution.

attributes.name: rebalancing_event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the event that triggered the inclusion, exclusion, or weight change for this constituent (e.g., scheduled quarterly rebalance, corporate action, market cap threshold breach, liquidity screen failure).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The system or data provider that published this constituent membership information (e.g., Bloomberg, MSCI, S&P Dow Jones Indices, FTSE Russell).

attributes.name: weight_percentage
attributes.description: The weight of this instrument within the benchmark index expressed as a percentage. Used for index tracking, replication, and attribution calculations. Weight calculation method depends on the benchmark's weighting scheme (market cap, free-float, equal-weight, etc.).

domains.name: trade
domains.description: Securities trading, order management, trade capture, execution, position management, P&L attribution, and post-trade processing for capital markets and trading book activities. Manages the full trade lifecycle from order entry through settlement, MTM valuation, trade confirmations, and FX/OTC derivative execution. Primary system of record aligned with Murex / Calypso.

products.name: order
products.description: Core master record for all trade orders entered into the Trading and Order Management System (Murex/Calypso). Captures the full order lifecycle from entry through execution including order type (market, limit, stop, IOC, FOK), asset class (equity, fixed income, FX, OTC derivative), side (buy/sell/short), quantity, price, order status, trader ID, desk, book, counterparty, venue, time-in-force, and origination channel. Supports parent/child order hierarchies for algorithmic and smart order routing. SSOT for trade order identity across capital markets.

attributes.name: trading_book_id
attributes.description: Reference to the trading book or portfolio where the order position will be held. Critical for position management, risk calculations, and regulatory capital requirements under FRTB (Fundamental Review of the Trading Book).

attributes.name: average_execution_price
attributes.description: Volume-weighted average price at which the order was executed. For partially filled orders, average of fills to date. Used for P&L calculation, transaction cost analysis, and client reporting. Expressed in order currency per unit.

attributes.name: cancellation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the order was cancelled. Null for active or filled orders. Used for order lifecycle analysis and operational metrics. Recorded in UTC.

attributes.name: capacity
attributes.description: Capacity in which the firm is acting for the order. Principal means trading for own account. Agency means acting as broker for client. Riskless principal means simultaneous offsetting trades. Required for regulatory reporting and best execution analysis.

attributes.name: commission_amount
attributes.description: Total commission charged for order execution. Includes broker fees, exchange fees, and clearing fees. Expressed in order currency. Used for revenue recognition, client billing, and transaction cost analysis.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the order record was first created in the database. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and operational monitoring. Recorded in UTC. Distinct from order_entry_timestamp which reflects business event time.

attributes.name: entry_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the order was entered into the trading system. Recorded in UTC with microsecond precision. Critical for transaction cost analysis, market abuse surveillance, and regulatory reporting under MiFID II clock synchronization requirements.

attributes.name: execution_strategy
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the algorithmic execution strategy applied to the order. Examples include VWAP, TWAP, implementation shortfall, liquidity-seeking, dark pool aggregation. Null for manual execution. Used for strategy performance analysis and best execution compliance.

attributes.name: execution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the order was fully executed. Null for unfilled or partially filled orders. Used for settlement date calculation (T+1, T+2) and performance measurement. Recorded in UTC.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the order automatically expires if not filled. Applicable for GTD (Good Till Date) orders. Null for Day, GTC, IOC, and FOK orders. System automatically cancels order at end of expiry date.

attributes.name: filled_quantity
attributes.description: Cumulative quantity executed to date. Updated as partial fills occur. When filled_quantity equals quantity, order status transitions to filled. Used to calculate remaining open quantity and order completion percentage.

attributes.name: instruction
attributes.description: Free-text field for special handling instructions or trader notes. May include client preferences, execution constraints, or operational notes. Not used for automated processing but valuable for audit trail and client service.

attributes.name: is_algorithmic
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order was generated or executed by an algorithmic trading system. True for algo orders, false for manual orders. Required for MiFID II algorithmic trading transparency and risk control reporting.

attributes.name: is_discretionary
attributes.description: Indicates whether the order was placed under discretionary authority where the firm has latitude in execution timing and price. True for discretionary orders, false for non-discretionary. Impacts regulatory reporting and best execution obligations.

attributes.name: last_update_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time of the most recent modification to the order record. Updated on status changes, partial fills, amendments, or cancellations. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: limit_price
attributes.description: Maximum price for buy orders or minimum price for sell orders. Only applicable for limit and stop-limit order types. Null for market orders. Expressed in currency per unit of the security.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp of the most recent update to the order record. Updated on any field change. Used for change data capture, audit trail, and data synchronization. Recorded in UTC.

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the order. Externally visible order reference used in confirmations, reports, and client communications. May follow desk-specific or system-specific numbering conventions.

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the order. Tracks progression from entry through execution or cancellation. Critical for order management, compliance monitoring, and operational reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new|pending|partially_filled|filled|cancelled|rejected|expired|suspended — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of order execution instruction. Market orders execute immediately at best available price. Limit orders execute only at specified price or better. Stop orders trigger at specified price. IOC (Immediate or Cancel) and FOK (Fill or Kill) define time-in-force behavior.

attributes.name: origination_channel
attributes.description: Channel through which the order was received. Electronic includes FIX protocol and API. Voice for phone orders. Algo for algorithmic trading. DMA (Direct Market Access) for client-routed orders. Client portal for self-service platforms. Used for channel analytics and operational efficiency measurement.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Total quantity of the security ordered. For equities, typically number of shares. For bonds, face value amount. For FX, base currency amount. For derivatives, number of contracts. Unit of measure depends on asset class and instrument type.

attributes.name: regulatory_trade_flag
attributes.description: Indicator for special regulatory treatment or reporting requirements. Examples include short sale indicator, large in scale (LIS), pre-trade transparency waiver, algorithmic trading flag. Used for regulatory reporting to FINRA, SEC, ESMA.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the order was rejected. Includes system validations (insufficient margin, invalid security), risk limit breaches, compliance blocks, or venue rejections. Null for non-rejected orders. Used for operational issue resolution and client communication.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the trade settles and securities and cash are exchanged. Calculated based on execution date and market convention (T+1 for US equities, T+2 for most securities). Critical for cash management and operational planning.

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: Direction of the trade order. Buy increases position, sell decreases position. Short sell creates negative position. Buy to cover closes short position. Critical for position management and P&L calculation.

attributes.name: stop_price
attributes.description: Trigger price for stop and stop-limit orders. Order becomes active when market price reaches this level. Null for market and limit orders. Used for risk management and automated trading strategies.

attributes.name: time_in_force
attributes.description: Duration for which the order remains active. Day orders expire at market close. GTC (Good Till Cancelled) remains active until filled or cancelled. IOC (Immediate or Cancel) executes immediately or cancels. FOK (Fill or Kill) must fill completely or cancel. GTD (Good Till Date) expires on specified date.

products.name: execution
products.description: Transactional record of each individual fill or partial fill against a trade order. Captures execution price, executed quantity, execution venue (exchange, ECN, OTC), execution timestamp, counterparty BIC/LEI, broker, commission, execution type (full/partial), and market microstructure data. Supports T+1 settlement initiation and best-execution regulatory reporting (MiFID II, SEC Rule 606). One order may have multiple executions.

attributes.name: gross_trade_value

attributes.name: instrument_type

attributes.name: liquidity_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this execution added liquidity to the market (maker), removed liquidity (taker), or was routed. Affects exchange fee rebates and best-execution analysis.

attributes.name: market_microstructure_indicator
attributes.description: Classification of the market microstructure where the execution occurred: lit exchange, dark pool, systematic internaliser, over-the-counter (OTC), or request-for-quote (RFQ). Required for MiFID II best-execution reporting.

attributes.name: net_trade_value
attributes.description: Total value of the execution after all commissions and fees. Calculated as gross_trade_value ± commission_amount ± exchange_fee ± clearing_fee. Denominated in execution_currency.

attributes.name: price
attributes.description: The price per unit at which this execution was filled. Used to calculate gross trade value and for Mark-to-Market (MTM) valuation.

attributes.name: reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique reference number for this execution, typically assigned by the trading venue or broker. Used for trade confirmations and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: Total amount to be settled on settlement_date, denominated in settlement_currency. Includes FX conversion if settlement_currency differs from execution_currency.

attributes.name: settlement_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the trade will settle. May differ from execution_currency if FX conversion is required.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the trade is scheduled to settle. Calculated as execution_timestamp + settlement cycle (e.g., T+1 for equities, T+2 for bonds). Critical for liquidity and collateral management.

attributes.name: trade_reporting_flag

attributes.name: trade_reporting_timestamp

attributes.name: trade_side

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.name: venue
attributes.description: Name or code of the trading venue where the execution occurred (e.g., NYSE, NASDAQ, LSE, OTC, ECN). Critical for best-execution reporting under MiFID II and SEC Rule 606.

attributes.name: venue_mic_code
attributes.description: Four-character ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code (MIC) for the execution venue. Standardized venue identifier for regulatory reporting.

products.name: capture
products.description: Authoritative trade booking record and single system of record in the trading platform (Murex/Calypso). Represents the confirmed, booked trade after execution, capturing trade date, value date, settlement date, notional amount, price/rate, accrued interest, trade currency, settlement currency, counterparty LEI, legal entity, trading book, and booking status. Supports all asset classes and product types including cash equities, bonds, IRS, CDS, FX spot/forward/swap/NDF, OTC options, equity swaps, and swaptions with product-type-specific attributes (e.g., UTI/USI for OTC derivatives, currency pair/forward points for FX, fixed/floating legs for swaps). Maintains full amendment and versioning history as lifecycle events on the trade record, including amendment type (economic amendment, administrative correction, novation, compression), amended fields with before/after values, amendment reason, approval workflow status, approver, amendment timestamp, and regulatory re-reporting flags for EMIR/Dodd-Frank/MiFID II. Each amendment creates a versioned snapshot preserving the complete audit trail. SSOT for the confirmed trade event, its full amendment audit trail, and all product types across capital markets.

attributes.name: maturity_date

attributes.name: notional_amount

attributes.name: portfolio_code

attributes.name: settlement_date

attributes.name: trade_amount

attributes.name: trade_date

attributes.name: trade_reference_number

attributes.name: trade_timestamp

attributes.name: trade_version
attributes.description: Sequential version number incremented with each amendment or lifecycle event. Version 1 represents the original trade; subsequent versions capture economic amendments, administrative corrections, novations, or compressions.

attributes.name: trading_book
attributes.description: The trading book or portfolio to which the trade is assigned. Used for P&L attribution, risk limits, and FRTB boundary determination between trading book and banking book.

attributes.name: usi

attributes.name: uti

attributes.name: value_date

products.name: trade_position
products.description: Real-time and end-of-day position record per trading book, instrument, and legal entity. Tracks long/short quantity, average cost, market value, unrealized P&L, realized P&L, accrued income, dirty/clean price, and Greek sensitivities (DV01, delta, gamma, vega, theta). Supports intraday position keeping, risk limit monitoring, regulatory capital calculations (FRTB), and serves as the base record for MTM revaluation and P&L attribution. Updated on each trade capture event, corporate action adjustment, and MTM revaluation cycle. Maintains position history for end-of-day snapshots enabling T-1 comparison and position break investigation.

attributes.name: accrued_income
attributes.description: The accrued interest, dividends, or coupon income earned but not yet received on the position.

attributes.name: average_cost
attributes.description: The weighted average cost per unit at which the position was acquired. Used for realized P&L calculation.

attributes.name: base_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO currency code of the reporting entity's base currency for P&L and risk reporting.

attributes.name: base_currency_market_value

attributes.name: base_currency_unrealized_pnl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Base Currency Unrealized Profit and Loss (P&L)

attributes.name: delta

attributes.name: dirty_price
attributes.description: The price of the instrument including accrued interest. Used for fixed income securities.

attributes.name: dv01
attributes.business_glossary_term: Dollar Value of One Basis Point (DV01)
attributes.description: The dollar change in position value for a one basis point change in interest rates. Key risk sensitivity metric for fixed income positions.

attributes.name: fx_rate

attributes.name: gamma

attributes.name: market_price

attributes.name: market_value

attributes.name: position_date
attributes.description: The business date for which this position snapshot is recorded. Represents the end-of-day position as of this date.

attributes.name: position_status
attributes.description: The current lifecycle status of the position. Open positions are actively managed, closed positions have been fully liquidated.

attributes.name: position_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise timestamp when this position record was captured or updated. Used for intraday position keeping and real-time risk monitoring.

attributes.name: position_type

attributes.name: quantity

attributes.name: quantity_unit

attributes.name: realized_pnl
attributes.description: The cumulative realized profit or loss from closed or partially closed positions during the current period.

attributes.name: rho
attributes.description: The sensitivity of the position value to changes in the risk-free interest rate. Greek for interest rate sensitivity.

attributes.name: rwa_amount
attributes.description: The risk-weighted asset amount allocated to this position for regulatory capital calculations under Basel III.

attributes.name: settlement_date

attributes.name: theta
attributes.description: The rate of change of the position value with respect to the passage of time (time decay). Key Greek for options positions.

attributes.name: unrealized_pnl

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.name: valuation_source

attributes.name: var_amount

attributes.name: vega
attributes.description: The sensitivity of the position value to changes in implied volatility. Key Greek for options positions.

attributes.name: theta_pnl

attributes.name: total_pnl

attributes.name: trading_pnl

attributes.description: P&L component attributable to changes in implied volatility (vega sensitivity).

products.name: settlement_instruction
products.description: Settlement instruction record generated post-trade for delivery versus payment (DVP), free of payment (FOP), or FX settlement. Captures settlement date, settlement amount, settlement currency, IBAN/SWIFT BIC of custodian, CSD/ICSD (DTC, Euroclear, Clearstream), settlement status (pending, matched, settled, failed), settlement agent, and nostro account. attributes.name: compression_cycle_id
attributes.description: Primary key for compression_cycle

attributes.name: approval_deadline_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time by which participants must approve or reject compression results. Applicable only when approval is required.

attributes.name: approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether participant approval is required before finalizing compression results. If true, participants must explicitly accept results before settlement.

attributes.name: asset_class
attributes.description: The asset class category for which this compression cycle is executed. Determines the type of derivatives being compressed.

attributes.name: base_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code representing the base currency for notional amounts and cash flows in this compression cycle.

attributes.name: booking_entity
attributes.description: Legal entity under which the compressed and replacement trades are booked. Important for regulatory capital and legal entity reporting.

attributes.name: business_unit
attributes.description: Internal business unit or trading desk responsible for managing this compression cycle, such as rates trading, credit trading, or central risk management.

attributes.name: cash_settlement_amount
attributes.description: Total net cash amount to be settled as a result of the compression, expressed in the base currency. Represents economic adjustments required to maintain portfolio equivalence.

attributes.name: clearing_house
attributes.description: Name of the central counterparty clearing house facilitating the compression cycle, such as LCH, CME, ICE Clear, or Eurex Clearing.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or contextual information about the compression cycle.

attributes.name: compressed_notional_amount
attributes.description: Total gross notional amount eliminated through compression, expressed in the base currency. Represents the reduction in notional exposure.

attributes.name: compression_algorithm_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the compression algorithm or methodology used for this cycle. Important for audit trail and reproducibility.

attributes.name: compression_methodology
attributes.description: Detailed description of the compression methodology applied, including algorithm type, optimization constraints, and calculation approach.

attributes.name: compression_rate_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of notional amount successfully compressed relative to the total submitted notional. Key performance indicator for compression efficiency.

attributes.name: compression_service_provider
attributes.description: Third-party service provider or platform facilitating the compression cycle, such as TriOptima, Quantile, or internal bank compression desk.

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who created this compression cycle record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this compression cycle record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: cycle_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the compression cycle, used for external reference and reporting.

attributes.name: cycle_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label for the compression cycle, typically describing the scope or purpose of the cycle.

attributes.name: cycle_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the compression cycle. Draft indicates initial setup, scheduled means planned for future execution, open allows participant submissions, in_progress indicates active processing, completed means successfully finished, cancelled indicates termination before completion, and failed indicates unsuccessful execution.

attributes.name: cycle_type
attributes.description: Classification of the compression cycle based on the methodology and scope. Bilateral involves two counterparties, multilateral involves multiple counterparties, portfolio compression reduces notional across a portfolio, tear-up eliminates offsetting positions, novation replaces existing trades, and termination closes out positions.

attributes.name: execution_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the compression algorithm completes processing and final results are available.

attributes.name: execution_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the compression algorithm begins processing submitted trades and calculating optimal compression results.

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the primary regulatory jurisdiction governing this compression cycle.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified this compression cycle record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this compression cycle record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: legal_documentation_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the legal documentation governing this compression cycle, such as ISDA protocol adherence letters, bilateral agreements, or clearing house rulebooks.

attributes.name: optimization_objective
attributes.description: Primary goal of the compression algorithm. Maximize notional reduction prioritizes largest gross notional elimination, minimize cash payments reduces settlement amounts, minimize replacement trades reduces new trade count, and balanced optimizes across multiple objectives.

attributes.name: participant_count
attributes.description: Total number of distinct counterparties or legal entities participating in this compression cycle.

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Specific product type within the asset class being compressed, such as interest rate swaps, credit default swaps, equity options, FX forwards, or commodity futures.

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compression cycle requires regulatory reporting to authorities such as trade repositories under EMIR, Dodd-Frank, or MiFID II.

attributes.name: remaining_notional_amount
attributes.description: Total gross notional amount remaining after compression, expressed in the base currency. Calculated as submitted notional minus compressed notional.

attributes.name: risk_tolerance_level
attributes.description: Risk appetite setting for the compression cycle. Conservative maintains strict economic equivalence, moderate allows minor deviations within tolerance, and aggressive maximizes compression with higher tolerance for economic changes.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The business date on which the compressed trades are settled and the original trades are terminated or novated.

attributes.name: submission_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the compression cycle closes for participant submissions. No further trade nominations are accepted after this time.

attributes.name: submission_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the compression cycle opens for participant submissions and trade nominations.

attributes.name: submitted_notional_amount
attributes.description: Total gross notional amount of all trades submitted for compression, expressed in the base currency.

attributes.name: tolerance_threshold_amount
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable cash payment or economic deviation that participants are willing to accept to achieve compression, expressed in the base currency.

attributes.name: total_compressed_trades
attributes.description: Total number of trades successfully compressed or eliminated as a result of this compression cycle.

attributes.name: total_replacement_trades
attributes.description: Total number of new replacement trades created as a result of the compression to maintain economic equivalence.

attributes.name: total_submitted_trades
attributes.description: Total number of trades submitted by all participants for inclusion in this compression cycle.

attributes.name: previous_compression_cycle_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on compression_cycle (previous_compression_cycle_id)

attributes.name: legal_entity_identifier_party_a
attributes.description: The 20-character ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier for Party A to this ISDA Master Agreement.

attributes.name: legal_entity_identifier_party_b
attributes.description: The 20-character ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier for Party B (the counterparty) to this ISDA Master Agreement.

attributes.name: minimum_transfer_amount
attributes.description: The minimum amount of collateral that must be transferred in any single collateral movement under the Credit Support Annex (CSA).

attributes.name: multibranch_party_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether either party is designated as a Multibranch Party, allowing multiple offices to enter into transactions under this agreement.

attributes.name: netting_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether close-out netting is permitted under this agreement, allowing offsetting of obligations upon termination.

attributes.name: notification_time
attributes.description: The deadline time by which collateral call notifications must be sent under the Credit Support Annex.

attributes.name: payment_netting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether payment netting is enabled, allowing offsetting of payment obligations due on the same date in the same currency.

attributes.name: regulatory_regime
attributes.description: The primary regulatory framework applicable to derivatives traded under this agreement (e.g., Dodd-Frank, EMIR, MiFID II).

attributes.name: setoff_applicable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether setoff rights are included, allowing parties to offset amounts owed under this agreement against other obligations.

attributes.name: specified_entities
attributes.description: List or description of specified entities (subsidiaries, affiliates) whose credit events may trigger provisions under this agreement.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: The date on which the ISDA Master Agreement terminates or was terminated. Nullable for open-ended agreements.

attributes.name: threshold_amount
attributes.description: The minimum exposure amount below which collateral is not required to be posted under the Credit Support Annex (CSA).

attributes.name: trade_reporting_party
attributes.description: The party responsible for reporting derivative transactions to trade repositories under regulatory requirements.

attributes.name: valuation_agent
attributes.description: The party or entity responsible for determining mark-to-market valuations of derivative positions under this agreement.

attributes.name: valuation_time
attributes.description: The specified time of day (and timezone) at which valuations are performed for collateral and close-out calculations.

attributes.name: waiting_period_days
attributes.description: The number of days that must elapse after a potential event of default before it becomes an actual event of default.

domains.name: investment
domains.description: Investment banking advisory services including M&A, IPO underwriting, DCF valuation, debt and equity capital markets origination, syndicated lending mandates, and corporate finance. Manages deal pipelines, pitch books, mandate agreements, transaction structures, fee arrangements, and tombstone records.

products.name: deal
products.description: Core master entity representing an investment banking deal or transaction mandate. Captures the full lifecycle from origination through closing, including deal type (M&A buy-side/sell-side, ECM, DCM, LBO, restructuring), stage progression (origination, pitch, mandate, execution, pricing, closing, post-closing), deal size, target enterprise value, expected fee, mandate date, closing date, status, originating banker, pipeline probability, and key milestone dates. Serves as the primary anchor entity for all investment domain relationships — mandate, valuation, offering, syndication, tombstone, fee arrangement, regulatory filing, and deal participants all reference this entity.

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the investment banking deal or transaction mandate. Primary key for the deal entity, referenced by all downstream investment domain entities including mandate, valuation, offering, syndication, tombstone, and fee arrangement.

attributes.name: alco_meeting_id

Real process: secured financing structures in leveraged buyouts, asset-back

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: Investment banking deals must be booked to specific legal entities for regulatory capital calculation, financial statement consolidation, and tax reporting. Core requirement for Basel III, IFRS 10 con

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.channel. Business justification: Investment deals are originated through specific banking channels (branch, digital, RM). Deal capture systems track origination channel for revenue attribution, channel profitability analysis, and reg

attributes.name: regulatory_exam_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_exam. Business justification: Regulatory examiners review deal files during BSA/AML, Reg W, capital markets exams. Deal documentation is primary evidence source. Examiners trace deals to verify compliance with securities laws and

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: Investment banking deals require stress testing under CCAR/DFAST regulatory scenarios to assess capital impact, deal viability under adverse conditions, and regulatory approval requirements. Essential

attributes.name: target_industry_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.industry_code. Business justification: Industry classification drives sector concentration limits, credit portfolio segmentation, CECL modeling, and league table rankings. Target_industry_sector is denormalized industry name.

attributes.name: team_lead_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the senior banker or managing director designated as the execution team lead for the deal. May differ from the coverage banker; responsible for day-to-day deal execution and client management during the transaction.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; Internal Deal Governance Policy

attributes.name: actual_closing_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the transaction legally closed and was completed. Populated upon deal closure; used for revenue recognition, tombstone generation, and post-deal performance analysis.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 — Revenue Recognition; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: announcement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the transaction was publicly announced to the market. Relevant for M&A and ECM transactions; triggers regulatory disclosure obligations and market impact analysis.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation FD; SEC Rule 135; FINRA Rule 5250

attributes.name: complexity
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the deal's structural and execution complexity, used for resource allocation, staffing decisions, and risk committee escalation thresholds. Assessed at origination and updated as deal structure evolves.
attributes.references: Internal Deal Governance Policy; FINRA Rule 4511

attributes.name: confidentiality_level
attributes.description: Information barrier and confidentiality classification of the deal. STRICTLY_CONFIDENTIAL deals trigger Chinese Wall protocols, restricted list management, and information barrier controls to prevent insider trading.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-5; FINRA Rule 3110; MAR (Market Abuse Regulation); FCA SYSC

attributes.name: counterparty_name
attributes.description: Name of the counterparty in the transaction (e.g., target company in M&A buy-side, acquirer in sell-side, co-underwriter in ECM/DCM). Stored as a descriptive field for deal context; may not yet be a registered client in the CRM system.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the deal record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides audit trail for record creation; used for data lineage, SOX compliance, and pipeline aging calculations.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302 and 404; BCBS 239 — Data Lineage; FINRA Rule 4511

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the deal size, enterprise value, and fees are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency pipeline reporting and FX conversion to reporting currency.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 — Currency Codes; FASB ASC 830 — Foreign Currency

attributes.name: deal_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier assigned to the deal at origination, used in pitch books, mandate letters, and client communications. Typically follows the investment bank's internal deal numbering convention (e.g., IB-2024-00123).

attributes.name: deal_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description of the deal structure, strategic rationale, and key transaction terms. Used in pitch books, deal committee memos, and tombstone records. Contains sensitive deal information subject to information barrier controls.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Regulation S-K Item 101

attributes.name: deal_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or working title of the deal, often referencing the target company or project codename (e.g., 'Project Falcon — Acquisition of XYZ Corp'). Used in internal pipeline reporting and pitch book headers.

attributes.name: deal_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the deal record. ACTIVE indicates the deal is in progress; CLOSED_WON indicates successful completion; CLOSED_LOST or WITHDRAWN indicates the deal did not proceed. Used for pipeline management and revenue forecasting.

attributes.name: deal_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investment banking transaction by strategic category. Drives workflow, fee structure, and regulatory treatment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: M&A_BUY_SIDE|M&A_SELL_SIDE|ECM|DCM|LBO|RESTRUCTURING|SYNDICATED_LENDING|LEVERAGED_FINANCE|PROJECT_FINANCE|SPIN_OFF — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: expected_closing_date
attributes.description: Projected date on which the transaction is expected to close or complete. Used for pipeline probability weighting, revenue forecasting, and resource scheduling. Updated as deal progresses through execution stages.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 303; FINRA Rule 4511

attributes.name: expected_fee_amount
attributes.description: The estimated total advisory or underwriting fee expected to be earned upon deal completion, expressed in the deal currency. Used for revenue pipeline forecasting, banker incentive compensation, and ALCO revenue planning.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 — Revenue Recognition; FINRA Rule 2010

attributes.name: fee_rate_bps
attributes.description: The advisory or underwriting fee expressed as a rate in basis points (BPS) of the deal size or enterprise value. Standard investment banking fee metric; used for benchmarking against market comparables and mandate negotiation.

attributes.name: is_cross_border
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the transaction involves parties or assets in more than one country. Triggers additional regulatory review, FATCA/CRS reporting obligations, and cross-border M&A regulatory approval tracking.
attributes.references: FATCA; CRS (Common Reporting Standard); OCC Cross-Border Guidelines; CFPB

attributes.name: is_public_company
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the target or issuer is a publicly listed company. Determines applicability of SEC disclosure requirements, public M&A rules (e.g., Williams Act), and public company audit standards.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Exchange Act of 1934; SEC Regulation M-A; Williams Act

attributes.name: lob_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the investment banking line of business responsible for the deal (e.g., M&A Advisory, Equity Capital Markets, Debt Capital Markets, Leveraged Finance, Restructuring). Used for P&L attribution and management reporting.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; Internal LOB Taxonomy; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: mandate_date
attributes.description: The date on which the client formally awarded the mandate to the bank, typically evidenced by a signed engagement letter or mandate agreement. Triggers formal deal execution resourcing and fee accrual commencement.

attributes.name: origination_date
attributes.description: The date on which the deal opportunity was first identified and entered into the pipeline system. Marks the start of the deal lifecycle and is used for pipeline aging analysis and banker performance attribution.

attributes.name: pipeline_probability_pct
attributes.description: Estimated probability (0.00–100.00%) that the deal will successfully close, assigned by the coverage banker and reviewed by deal committee. Used to compute probability-weighted revenue in pipeline forecasting and ALCO reporting.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 — Revenue Recognition; Internal Pipeline Management Policy

attributes.name: pitch_date
attributes.description: The date on which the formal pitch or proposal was presented to the client. Marks the transition from origination to active pursuit; used for pipeline conversion rate analysis and banker activity tracking.

attributes.name: pricing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the transaction was priced (applicable to ECM and DCM transactions). For IPOs and bond issuances, this is the date the final offer price or coupon is set; triggers T+1 or T+2 settlement obligations.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 15c6-1 (T+1 Settlement); FINRA Rule 11810; SEC Regulation S

attributes.name: rationale
attributes.description: Summary of the strategic rationale for the transaction from the client's perspective (e.g., market expansion, synergy realization, capital structure optimization). Used in deal committee presentations and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 101; FASB ASC 805

attributes.name: region_code
attributes.description: Geographic region responsible for the deal coverage and execution (Americas, EMEA, Asia-Pacific). Used for regional P&L attribution, pipeline reporting, and regulatory jurisdiction mapping.
attributes.references: Internal Geographic Taxonomy; BCBS Basel III Pillar 3

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_required
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the transaction requires regulatory approval (e.g., antitrust/HSR filing, CFIUS review, FCA approval, ECB notification). Triggers compliance workflow and deal timeline adjustment.
attributes.references: HSR Act; CFIUS (50 U.S.C. § 4565); EU Merger Regulation; FCA MAR

attributes.name: restricted_list_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the deal has triggered placement of the target or issuer on the bank's restricted trading list, preventing proprietary trading and research publication. Enforces information barrier compliance.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-5; FINRA Rule 3110; MAR Article 18 — Insider Lists

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: The total transaction size or notional value of the deal (e.g., total equity raised for ECM, total debt issued for DCM, total consideration for M&A). Distinct from enterprise value; represents the actual capital markets transaction amount.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 2210; FASB ASC 606

attributes.name: source_system_deal_ref
attributes.description: The deal identifier as recorded in the originating system of record (e.g., Murex deal ID, Loan IQ deal number, or internal CRM opportunity ID). Enables lineage tracing and reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and operational systems.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 — Internal Controls; BCBS BCBS 239 — Data Lineage

attributes.name: subtype
attributes.description: Further granular classification within the deal type. For ECM: IPO, Follow-On, Rights Issue, SPAC. For DCM: Investment Grade Bond, High Yield Bond, Convertible Note. For M&A: Strategic, Financial Sponsor. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IPO|FOLLOW_ON|RIGHTS_ISSUE|SPAC|IG_BOND|HY_BOND|CONVERTIBLE|STRATEGIC_MA|FINANCIAL_SPONSOR — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: target_company_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the target company in M&A transactions, or the issuer name in ECM/DCM transactions. Used in tombstone records, regulatory filings, and deal marketing materials.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 2210; FASB ASC 805

attributes.name: target_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the target company's or issuer's primary jurisdiction of incorporation. Used for cross-border deal classification, regulatory jurisdiction determination, and geographic pipeline reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; FATCA; CRS (Common Reporting Standard); OCC Cross-Border Guidelines

attributes.name: target_enterprise_value
attributes.description: The estimated total enterprise value of the target company or transaction, expressed in the deal currency. Used as the primary sizing metric for M&A transactions, LBO analysis, and DCF valuation benchmarking. Basis for fee calculation in many mandate structures.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 805 — Business Combinations; BCBS Basel III

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to the deal record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change data capture, audit trail maintenance, and detecting stale pipeline records.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302 and 404; BCBS 239 — Data Lineage; FINRA Rule 4511

products.name: investment_mandate
products.description: Formal mandate agreement record capturing the engagement between the bank and a client for a specific investment banking transaction. Records mandate type (exclusive, co-advisor, bookrunner, co-manager), mandate letter date, engagement scope, exclusivity period, termination rights, governing law, and signatory details. Distinct from the deal entity — a mandate is the contractual authorization to execute a deal.

attributes.name: investment_mandate_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the investment banking mandate record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: counterparty_rating_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.counterparty_rating. Business justification: Mandates require counterparty ratings for client onboarding, KYC/AML compliance verification, engagement risk assessment, and credit authority determination. Essential for conflict checks and regulato

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the lead investment banking coverage officer or relationship banker responsible for originating and managing this mandate.

attributes.name: engagement_channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.channel. Business justification: Client mandates for advisory services are signed through specific channels. MiFID II and Dodd-Frank require tracking client engagement channel for suitability and best execution compliance. Mandate ma

attributes.name: governing_law_jurisdiction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.jurisdiction. Business justification: Governing law jurisdiction required for legal enforceability assessment, netting opinion validation, and dispute resolution framework per ISDA Master Agreement standards.

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: Mandates are executed by specific bank legal entities (signatory to engagement letter). Required for revenue recognition under ASC 606/IFRS 15, legal liability tracking, and regulatory reporting of ad

attributes.name: margin_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to collateral.margin_agreement. Business justification: Investment banking mandates for derivatives and structured products reference CSA/margin agreements governing collateral terms. Real process: ISDA master agreement negotiation, collateral schedule doc

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the corporate or institutional client that has engaged the bank under this mandate. Represents the counterparty granting the mandate.

attributes.name: bank_signatory_name
attributes.description: Full name of the authorized bank representative who executed the mandate letter on behalf of the bank. Required for legal enforceability and audit trail.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-4; Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302

attributes.name: client_signatory_name
attributes.description: Full name of the authorized client representative who executed the mandate letter on behalf of the client entity. Required for legal enforceability and Know Your Customer (KYC) documentation.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-4; FinCEN KYC Requirements; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: client_signatory_title
attributes.description: Job title or designation of the client signatory (e.g., Chief Financial Officer, Managing Director) confirming their authority to bind the client entity under the mandate.

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the mandated transaction was successfully completed and closed (e.g., IPO pricing date, M&A closing date, bond settlement date). Triggers final fee recognition and tombstone eligibility.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-4; IFRS 15 — Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: confidentiality_level
attributes.description: Information barrier and confidentiality classification of the mandate. 'wall_crossed' indicates that specific individuals have been brought over the wall and are subject to information barrier restrictions under Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) and SEC insider trading rules.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation FD; Market Abuse Regulation (MAR); FINRA Rule 4511; Internal Information Barrier Policy

attributes.name: conflict_check_status
attributes.description: Status of the bank's internal conflict of interest review for this mandate. Mandates cannot be activated until conflicts are cleared or formally waived per Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) policy.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2010; SEC Rule 10b-5; MiFID II Article 23 — Conflicts of Interest; Internal GRC Policy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the mandate record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under SOX and SEC Rule 17a-4.
attributes.references: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302; SEC Rule 17a-4; FINRA Rule 4511

attributes.name: deal_size_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the estimated or target transaction size. Used for fee calculation, pipeline reporting, and capital markets analytics.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 — Currency Codes; BCBS Reporting Standards

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_mechanism
attributes.description: Contractually agreed mechanism for resolving disputes arising under the mandate agreement (e.g., litigation in courts, arbitration under ICC/LCIA rules, mediation).
attributes.references: ISDA Master Agreement; Internal Legal Policy

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the mandate becomes binding and the bank is authorized to commence advisory or underwriting activities on behalf of the client.
attributes.references: ISDA Master Agreement Framework; Internal Investment Banking Policy

attributes.name: engagement_scope
attributes.description: Narrative description of the services the bank is mandated to provide, including advisory scope, underwriting obligations, distribution responsibilities, and any carve-outs or limitations agreed in the mandate letter.

attributes.name: estimated_deal_size
attributes.description: Estimated gross transaction value or deal size as agreed at mandate signing. Used for pipeline valuation, fee estimation, and Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) modelling. Expressed in deal_size_currency.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110 — Underwriting Compensation; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: exclusivity_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the exclusivity period. After this date, the client may engage competing advisors unless the mandate is renewed or the exclusivity is extended.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation M-A; Internal M&A Policy

attributes.name: exclusivity_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the exclusivity period during which the client is contractually restricted from engaging other advisors for the same transaction.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation M-A; Internal M&A Policy

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the mandate agreement expires if the transaction has not been completed. Nullable for open-ended mandates. Distinct from the exclusivity end date.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; Internal Investment Banking Policy

attributes.name: fee_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which mandate fees (retainer, success fee, minimum fee) are denominated and payable. May differ from deal_size_currency for cross-border transactions.

attributes.name: governing_law_state
attributes.description: State or province within the governing law jurisdiction (e.g., New York, England and Wales) where sub-national law applies. Relevant for US and federal jurisdictions.
attributes.references: ISDA Master Agreement; Internal Legal Policy

attributes.name: industry_sector_code
attributes.description: Four-digit Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) or Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) code representing the client's primary industry sector. Used for sector-based pipeline analytics and coverage team assignment.
attributes.references: SEC SIC Code Classification; MSCI/S&P GICS Standard

attributes.name: investment_mandate_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the mandate agreement. Drives pipeline reporting, fee accrual eligibility, and deal team resource allocation. Valid states: draft (under negotiation), active (signed and in force), suspended (temporarily paused), terminated (cancelled before completion), completed (transaction closed), lapsed (exclusivity expired without execution).
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; Internal Investment Banking Policy

attributes.name: is_exclusive
attributes.description: Indicates whether the mandate grants the bank exclusive advisory rights for the transaction, preventing the client from engaging competing advisors during the exclusivity period.

attributes.name: kyc_status
attributes.description: Current Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) due diligence status for the client under this mandate. Mandates cannot proceed without approved KYC per Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and FinCEN requirements.
attributes.references: FinCEN KYC Requirements; Bank Secrecy Act (BSA); FATCA; AML/CFT Standards — BCBS

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the mandate record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for change data capture, audit trail, and regulatory record-keeping.
attributes.references: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302; SEC Rule 17a-4; FINRA Rule 4511

attributes.name: league_table_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this mandate and its associated transaction qualify for submission to investment banking league table rankings (e.g., Bloomberg, Dealogic, Thomson Reuters). Drives competitive positioning analytics.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210; Dealogic / Bloomberg League Table Methodology

attributes.name: letter_date
attributes.description: Date on which the mandate letter was formally signed and executed by both the bank and the client. This is the principal business event date establishing the contractual engagement.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511 — Books and Records; SEC Rule 17a-4

attributes.name: lob_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the investment banking Line of Business (LOB) responsible for this mandate (e.g., IBD — Investment Banking Division, ECM — Equity Capital Markets, DCM — Debt Capital Markets, M&A, SYND — Syndicated Lending, CORP_FIN — Corporate Finance).
attributes.references: Internal LOB Taxonomy; FINRA Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: mandate_type
attributes.description: Classification of the bank's role under the mandate agreement. Determines fee entitlement, exclusivity rights, and regulatory disclosure obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: exclusive_advisor|co_advisor|bookrunner|co_manager|lead_manager|arranger — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110 — Underwriting Compensation; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: minimum_fee_amount
attributes.description: Minimum guaranteed fee payable to the bank regardless of final transaction size, providing a floor on advisory compensation. Expressed in deal_size_currency.

attributes.name: pitch_book_reference
attributes.description: Document management system reference or identifier for the pitch book or information memorandum presented to the client prior to mandate award. Supports audit trail and deal origination tracking.

attributes.name: reference
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned to the mandate, used in client correspondence, pitch books, and regulatory filings. Format: LOB-MND-YYYY-NNNNNNNN.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the mandated transaction requires regulatory approval (e.g., antitrust clearance, SEC registration, FCA approval) before completion. Triggers compliance workflow and timeline management.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FCA Listing Rules; EU Merger Regulation; OCC Guidance

attributes.name: retainer_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fixed upfront or periodic retainer fee payable by the client to the bank upon mandate signing, independent of transaction completion. Expressed in deal_size_currency.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110 — Underwriting Compensation; Internal Fee Policy

attributes.name: success_fee_bps
attributes.description: Contingent success fee expressed in Basis Points (BPS) of the final transaction value, payable upon successful completion of the mandated transaction. Drives revenue recognition and Profit and Loss (PnL) attribution.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Fee Policy

attributes.name: tail_period_months
attributes.description: Number of months following mandate termination or expiry during which the bank retains the right to a success fee if the transaction is completed with a counterparty introduced during the mandate period.

attributes.name: target_company_name
attributes.description: Name of the target company or issuer in the transaction (e.g., acquisition target in M&A, issuer in an IPO or bond offering). May be confidential prior to public announcement.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation M-A; FINRA Rule 4511; Market Abuse Regulation (MAR)

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the mandate was formally terminated prior to transaction completion, if applicable. Populated only when status is 'terminated'. Distinct from expiry_date (natural end) and completion_date (successful close).
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; Internal Investment Banking Policy

attributes.name: termination_rights
attributes.description: Description of the contractual termination rights available to either party, including notice periods, termination for convenience clauses, material adverse change (MAC) provisions, and tail fee obligations upon termination.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-4; Internal Legal Policy

attributes.name: tombstone_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the completed transaction is eligible for tombstone advertisement publication, subject to client consent and regulatory requirements. Tombstones are used for marketing and league table submissions.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210 — Communications with the Public; Internal Marketing Policy

attributes.name: transaction_type
attributes.description: Category of the investment banking transaction covered by this mandate (e.g., Initial Public Offering (IPO), Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) buy-side, Debt Capital Markets (DCM)). Drives workflow, fee structure, and regulatory treatment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ipo|follow_on|m_and_a_buy_side|m_and_a_sell_side|debt_capital_markets|equity_capital_markets|syndicated_loan|restructuring — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 5110; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) — Capital Markets Guidance

products.name: transaction_structure
products.description: Master entity defining the financial and legal structure of an investment banking transaction. Captures structure type (merger, acquisition, carve-out, spin-off, IPO, follow-on, rights issue, bond issuance, syndicated loan), consideration type (cash, stock, mixed), financing mix, leverage ratio, pro forma capital structure, regulatory approvals required, and structural conditions. Supports DCF valuation and deal execution planning.

attributes.name: transaction_structure_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the investment banking transaction structure record. Primary key for this entity in the Silver Layer lakehouse.

attributes.name: aml_case_id

attributes.name: collateral_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to collateral.collateral_asset. Business justification: Transaction structures specify collateral packages securing debt tranches in LBOs, secured bond offerings, and asset-backed financings.
