attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.country. Business justification: Target country determines country risk premium in WACC calculation, sovereign credit rating impact, and regulatory approval timeline for valuation scenarios.

attributes.name: transaction_structure_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.transaction_structure. Business justification: Valuations and fairness opinions are performed to support specific transaction structures (e.g., DCF valuation for a proposed merger structure). While investment_valuation has deal_id, one deal can ha

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the valuation or fairness opinion was formally approved by the designated investment committee or approval authority. Marks the transition from in_review to approved status and is a key compliance milestone.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 14a-9; Internal Investment Banking Governance Policy

attributes.name: board_presentation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the valuation analysis or fairness opinion was formally presented to the client's board of directors. Required for fairness opinion compliance documentation and proxy statement disclosure. Distinct from the valuation date.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; Delaware General Corporation Law

attributes.name: conflict_check_status
attributes.description: Status of the investment bank's internal conflict of interest review for this valuation engagement. FINRA Rule 5150 requires disclosure of material relationships between the advisor and the parties to the transaction. Cleared indicates no material conflicts; conflict_identified requires disclosure or recusal.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 2010

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when this valuation record was first created in the investment banking platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance record-keeping under SEC Rule 17a-4 and FINRA recordkeeping requirements.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-4; FINRA Rule 4511; SOX Section 802

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all monetary valuation figures (enterprise value, equity value, implied multiples) are expressed. Typically USD for US transactions but may vary for cross-border M&A.

attributes.name: delivery_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the valuation analysis or fairness opinion letter was formally delivered to the client or their board of directors. Marks the transition to delivered status and is referenced in the engagement letter and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: enterprise_value_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the enterprise value range derived from the valuation analysis, expressed in the deal currency. The EV range reflects sensitivity analysis across key assumptions such as WACC and terminal growth rate.

attributes.name: enterprise_value_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the enterprise value range derived from the valuation analysis, expressed in the deal currency. Enterprise Value represents the total value of the business including debt and excluding cash. Used for deal pricing and fairness opinion conclusions.

attributes.name: equity_value_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the implied equity value range, calculated by deducting net debt from the enterprise value high. Used in conjunction with shares outstanding to derive implied per-share value ranges for board presentations and proxy filings.

attributes.name: equity_value_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the implied equity value range, calculated by deducting net debt from the enterprise value low. Represents the value attributable to equity holders and is used to derive implied share price ranges for M&A and IPO pricing.

attributes.name: ev_ebitda_multiple_high
attributes.business_glossary_term: Enterprise Value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) Multiple High
attributes.description: Upper bound of the implied EV/EBITDA multiple derived from the valuation range. Together with the low multiple, defines the EV/EBITDA range used in board presentations, fairness opinion analyses, and investment committee materials.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; FINRA Rule 5150

attributes.name: ev_ebitda_multiple_low
attributes.business_glossary_term: Enterprise Value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) Multiple Low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the implied EV/EBITDA multiple derived from the valuation range, calculated as enterprise value low divided by the target company's EBITDA. Used to benchmark the valuation against comparable company trading multiples and precedent transaction multiples.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; FINRA Rule 5150

attributes.name: forecast_period_years
attributes.description: Number of years in the explicit cash flow forecast period used in the DCF or LBO model. Typically 5 to 10 years for investment banking valuations. Determines the horizon over which detailed financial projections are modeled before applying the terminal value.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: implied_share_price_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the implied per-share equity value derived from the equity value high divided by fully diluted shares outstanding. Together with the low, defines the implied share price range disclosed in fairness opinion proxy materials.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: implied_share_price_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the implied per-share equity value derived from the equity value low divided by fully diluted shares outstanding. Used in fairness opinion analyses to compare the implied price range against the proposed transaction consideration.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; FASB ASC 820

attributes.name: is_fairness_opinion
attributes.description: Indicates whether this valuation record constitutes a formal fairness opinion (True) or an internal valuation analysis (False). Fairness opinions carry additional regulatory obligations under SEC Rule 14a-9 and FINRA Rule 5150, including board presentation and proxy disclosure requirements.

attributes.name: ltm_ebitda
attributes.description: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (EBITDA) for the last twelve months (LTM) period used as the primary financial metric in the valuation analysis. Denominator for EV/EBITDA multiple calculations and key input to DCF normalization.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; SEC Regulation S-X; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: material_relationship_disclosure
attributes.description: Narrative description of any material relationships between the investment bank and the parties to the transaction that must be disclosed in the fairness opinion letter or proxy statement, as required by FINRA Rule 5150. Includes prior advisory mandates, lending relationships, and equity holdings.

attributes.name: methodology
attributes.description: Primary valuation methodology applied in this analysis. Common investment banking methodologies include Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), Leveraged Buyout (LBO), Comparable Company Analysis, Precedent Transaction Analysis, Sum-of-Parts (SOTP), Net Asset Value (NAV), Dividend Discount Model (DDM), and Asset-Based valuation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DCF|LBO|comparable_company|precedent_transaction|sum_of_parts|NAV|dividend_discount|asset_based — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; IFRS 13; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: model_file_reference
attributes.description: Document management system reference or file path to the underlying financial model (Excel/Python workbook) supporting this valuation. Enables auditors and reviewers to trace the valuation conclusion back to the source model and assumptions.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 17a-4; Internal Model Risk Management Policy

attributes.name: net_debt
attributes.description: Total financial debt less cash and cash equivalents of the target company as of the valuation date, used to bridge from enterprise value to equity value. A negative net debt (net cash) position increases equity value relative to enterprise value.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; IFRS 13; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: opinion_conclusion
attributes.description: The formal conclusion of the fairness or solvency opinion as rendered by the investment bank. Applicable when is_fairness_opinion is True. The conclusion is disclosed in the proxy statement or offering document and is subject to SEC and FINRA scrutiny.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; Delaware General Corporation Law

attributes.name: opinion_type
attributes.description: Classification of the formal opinion rendered, applicable when is_fairness_opinion is True. Fairness opinions address whether consideration is fair from a financial point of view; solvency opinions address the target's ability to meet obligations post-transaction; valuation opinions provide a point estimate of value; adequacy opinions address whether consideration is adequate.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; Delaware General Corporation Law

attributes.name: pe_multiple_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of the implied Price-to-Earnings (P/E) multiple derived from the equity value range. Together with the low multiple, defines the P/E range used in fairness opinion analyses and investment committee presentations.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; SEC Rule 14a-9

attributes.name: pe_multiple_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of the implied Price-to-Earnings (P/E) multiple derived from the equity value range divided by the target company's net income. Used as a cross-check valuation metric, particularly relevant for IPO pricing and public M&A transactions.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; SEC Rule 14a-9

attributes.name: reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the valuation engagement, used in client deliverables, pitch books, and regulatory filings. Follows the format VAL-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: Internal Investment Banking Engagement Numbering Standard

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the SEC, FINRA, or other regulatory filing (e.g., proxy statement, S-1, Form 8-K) in which this fairness opinion or valuation is disclosed. Enables traceability between the internal valuation record and public regulatory filings.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; SEC Schedule 14A; FINRA Rule 5150

attributes.name: secondary_methodology
attributes.description: Secondary or cross-check valuation methodology used to triangulate the primary valuation result. Investment banking practice typically employs multiple methodologies to establish a valuation range. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DCF|LBO|comparable_company|precedent_transaction|sum_of_parts|NAV|dividend_discount|asset_based — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; IFRS 13; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: shares_outstanding
attributes.description: Fully diluted shares outstanding of the target company as of the valuation date, including common shares, in-the-money options, warrants, and convertible securities on a treasury stock method basis. Used to derive implied per-share equity value.

attributes.name: target_company_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the company being valued or the target of the M&A transaction. Captured directly on the valuation record for reporting and audit purposes, as the target may not be an existing client in the customer master.

attributes.name: terminal_growth_rate
attributes.description: Perpetuity growth rate applied in the DCF terminal value calculation, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.025 for 2.5%). Represents the assumed long-term sustainable growth rate of the target company's free cash flows beyond the explicit forecast period.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards

attributes.name: transaction_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investment banking transaction for which this valuation is being performed. Determines the applicable regulatory requirements, fee structures, and valuation standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MA_buyside|MA_sellside|IPO|secondary_offering|debt_issuance|leveraged_buyout|restructuring|spin_off — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEC Rule 14a-9; FINRA Rule 5150; IASB IFRS 3

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording the most recent modification to this valuation record. Used for change tracking, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-4; FINRA Rule 4511; SOX Section 802

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The as-of date on which the valuation analysis is anchored. All market data, financial projections, and comparable benchmarks are referenced as of this date. Critical for fairness opinion compliance and deal pricing.

attributes.name: valuation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the valuation record, tracking progression from initial draft through internal review, committee approval, client delivery, and potential supersession or withdrawal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|in_review|approved|delivered|superseded|withdrawn — promote to reference product if additional states are required]

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the valuation model, incremented each time the analysis is materially revised (e.g., updated financial projections, revised WACC, new comparable set). Enables version control and audit trail for deal pricing decisions.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; Internal Investment Banking Model Risk Policy

attributes.name: wacc
attributes.description: Weighted Average Cost of Capital expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.085 for 8.5%) used as the discount rate in DCF valuation. Reflects the blended cost of equity and debt financing, adjusted for the target company's capital structure and risk profile.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 820; CFA Institute Valuation Standards; BCBS Basel III

products.name: fee_arrangement
products.description: Master entity capturing the fee structure, economics, and all payment events for investment banking mandates. Records fee type (retainer, success fee, underwriting spread, advisory fee, break fee, tail fee), fee basis (fixed, percentage, tiered), fee amount, payment milestones, fee sharing with co-advisors, revenue recognition schedule, and individual fee payment event details including event type (retainer payment, success fee trigger, closing fee, break fee), event date, invoiced amount, received amount, payment status, reconciliation reference, and revenue recognition date. Critical for IB revenue management, P&L attribution, banker compensation, and finance reconciliation.
products.reference: IB Fee Letter / Advisory Fee Agreement

attributes.name: fee_arrangement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the fee arrangement record in the investment banking mandate fee management system. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: aml_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.aml_case. Business justification: Fee structures examined in AML cases to detect potential bribery, kickbacks, or unusual payment patterns indicating illicit activity. Compliance reviews fee arrangements for FCPA violations, conflicts

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.cost_center. Business justification: Fee revenue is attributed to cost centers for P&L reporting, banker compensation calculations, and management reporting. Replaces denormalized cost_center_code. Required for segment reporting under IF

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investment banking deal or transaction (e.g., M&A transaction, IPO, syndicated loan) associated with this fee arrangement.

attributes.name: engagement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audit.engagement. Business justification: Fee arrangements are audited for revenue recognition compliance, conflict of interest management, regulatory adherence, internal policy compliance, and appropriateness of fee structures relative to se

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.gl_account. Business justification: Investment banking fees are posted to specific GL accounts for revenue recognition. Replaces denormalized gl_account_code with proper FK to enable drill-down from financial statements to deal-level fe

attributes.name: investment_mandate_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investment banking mandate (M&A, IPO, DCF advisory, debt/equity capital markets) to which this fee arrangement belongs.

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: Fee revenue must be recognized in specific legal entity's financial statements for GAAP/IFRS compliance, tax reporting, and regulatory capital calculations. Essential for revenue_recognition_date post

attributes.name: managed_portfolio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to wealth.managed_portfolio. Business justification: Investment banking fees for HNW individuals are sometimes paid from or tracked against wealth management portfolios. Real business process: fee billing coordination between investment banking and weal

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the corporate or institutional client (counterparty) for whom the investment banking services are being rendered under this fee arrangement.

attributes.name: primary_fee_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the lead investment banker (Managing Director or Director) responsible for originating and managing the mandate. Used for banker compensation, league table credit, and performance attribution.
attributes.references: Internal IB Compensation Policy; FINRA Registration Requirements

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee arrangement received final internal approval. Part of the SOX-compliant audit trail for revenue recognition and mandate governance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal IB Governance Policy

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Internal approval workflow status for the fee arrangement, reflecting sign-off by IB management, finance, and legal prior to client engagement. Required for SOX compliance and revenue recognition.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal IB Governance Policy; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: arrangement_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric reference code for the fee arrangement, used in client-facing engagement letters, mandate agreements, and finance reconciliation. Format: FA-{LOB}-{YEAR}-{SEQUENCE}.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Revenue Management Policy

attributes.name: arrangement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the fee arrangement. Draft: under negotiation; Active: binding and in effect; Suspended: temporarily paused; Terminated: cancelled before completion; Completed: all fees settled; Expired: lapsed without completion.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; Internal IB Revenue Recognition Policy

attributes.name: bank_fee_share_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total fee retained by this bank after co-advisor fee sharing. Equals 100% minus co_advisor_fee_sharing_pct for simple two-party splits, or the bank's specific allocation in multi-party syndicates.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Syndicate Revenue Sharing Policy

attributes.name: break_fee_amount
attributes.description: The contractual fee payable to the bank if the deal is terminated by the client before completion. Compensates the bank for work performed and opportunity cost.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Mandate Agreement Template

attributes.name: co_advisor_fee_sharing_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total fee to be shared with co-advisors or syndicate members on the mandate. Used for fee split calculations and revenue attribution in multi-bank advisory or underwriting syndicates.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; IASB IFRS 15; Internal Syndicate Revenue Sharing Policy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this fee arrangement record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the fee arrangement is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Governs all monetary amounts on this record.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; IASB IAS 21 — Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates

attributes.name: deal_value_basis
attributes.description: The transaction or deal value (e.g., enterprise value, equity value, issuance proceeds) used as the basis for computing percentage-based fees. Critical for success fee and underwriting spread calculations.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; IASB IFRS 15

attributes.name: dispute_description
attributes.description: Description of the fee dispute raised by the client, including the disputed amount and grounds for dispute. Populated when payment_status is 'disputed'. Used for legal and collections management.
attributes.references: Internal Legal and Collections Policy; FINRA Dispute Resolution Rules

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee arrangement becomes legally binding and operative, typically aligned with the mandate agreement execution date.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: engagement_letter_ref
attributes.description: The document reference number of the signed engagement letter or mandate agreement that governs this fee arrangement. Used for legal and compliance audit trail.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Legal Document Management Policy

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee arrangement ceases to be operative. Nullable for open-ended arrangements. Tail fee provisions may extend beyond this date.

attributes.name: fee_amount
attributes.description: The gross base fee amount in the arrangement currency. For fixed-basis arrangements, this is the total contractual fee. For percentage-basis arrangements, this is the computed fee amount once the deal value is known. Used for P&L attribution and revenue recognition.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: fee_basis
attributes.description: The computational basis on which the fee is calculated. Fixed: flat dollar amount; Percentage: applied to transaction value or deal size; Tiered: percentage varies by deal size bracket; Blended: combination of fixed and percentage; Minimum Plus Percentage: floor amount plus variable component.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers; FASB ASC 606

attributes.name: fee_rate_bps
attributes.description: The fee rate expressed in basis points (BPS) applied to the transaction or deal value for percentage-basis fee arrangements. One basis point equals 0.01%. Used in underwriting spread and advisory fee calculations.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; IASB IFRS 15; Internal IB Pricing Policy

attributes.name: fee_type
attributes.description: Classification of the fee by its commercial nature within the investment banking mandate. Retainer: periodic engagement fee; Success Fee: contingent on deal close; Underwriting Spread: difference between issue price and proceeds; Advisory Fee: M&A or capital markets advisory; Break Fee: payable on deal termination; Tail Fee: post-termination success fee within tail period.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 601; IASB IFRS 15

attributes.name: fee_waiver_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the business reason for waiving or reducing the contractual fee, required for management approval and audit trail when payment_status is 'waived'. Null when no waiver applies.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal IB Revenue Management Policy; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: The accounts receivable invoice number issued to the client for fees due under this arrangement. Links to the AR module in the General Ledger system (Oracle Financials / SAP S4HANA) for payment tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal AR Policy; IASB IFRS 15

attributes.name: invoiced_amount
attributes.description: The total fee amount invoiced to the client under this arrangement. May differ from fee_amount due to adjustments, credits, or partial invoicing.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: lob_code
attributes.description: The Line of Business (LOB) code identifying the investment banking division responsible for this fee arrangement (e.g., M&A Advisory, ECM, DCM, Leveraged Finance, Syndicated Lending).
attributes.references: Internal IB Revenue Management Policy; CCAR/DFAST LOB Segmentation

attributes.name: minimum_fee_amount
attributes.description: The contractual floor fee amount guaranteed to the bank regardless of deal size or outcome, applicable for tiered or minimum-plus-percentage fee basis arrangements.

attributes.name: payment_due_date
attributes.description: The contractual date by which the client must remit payment for the invoiced fee. Used for AR aging, collections management, and overdue fee tracking.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; Internal AR Collections Policy

attributes.name: payment_received_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee payment was actually received from the client. Used for cash reconciliation, days-sales-outstanding (DSO) calculation, and revenue recognition confirmation.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: payment_status
attributes.description: Current payment collection status for the fee arrangement. Pending: invoice issued, payment not yet due; Partially Paid: partial receipt; Paid: fully settled; Overdue: past due date; Waived: fee forgiven; Disputed: client has raised a dispute.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; Internal AR Collections Policy; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: received_amount
attributes.description: The total fee amount actually received from the client as of the most recent payment event. Used for cash reconciliation, outstanding receivables tracking, and revenue recognition confirmation.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: reconciliation_reference
attributes.description: The payment or wire transfer reference number used to match the received fee payment to the invoice in the GL/AR system. Supports finance reconciliation and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Finance Reconciliation Policy; SWIFT Payment Standards

attributes.name: retainer_amount
attributes.description: The periodic retainer fee amount payable by the client during the engagement period, typically monthly or quarterly. May be credited against the success fee upon deal close.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Revenue Policy

attributes.name: retainer_creditable
attributes.description: Indicates whether retainer payments made during the engagement are creditable (offset) against the success fee upon deal completion. True = retainer amounts reduce the success fee payable.

attributes.name: retainer_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which retainer fee payments are due from the client during the engagement period.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; Internal IB Engagement Letter Standards

attributes.name: revenue_recognition_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee revenue is recognized in the General Ledger per the applicable revenue recognition method (IFRS 15 / ASC 606). Critical for period-end financial close and P&L attribution.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: revenue_recognition_method
attributes.description: The accounting method applied to recognize revenue from this fee arrangement per IFRS 15 / ASC 606. Point in Time: recognized at deal close; Over Time: recognized ratably over engagement period; Milestone Based: recognized upon achievement of defined milestones; Contingent: deferred until contingency resolved.
attributes.references: IASB IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: tail_period_months
attributes.description: The number of months following termination or expiry of the mandate during which the bank retains the right to a success fee if the client completes a transaction with a party introduced by the bank.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Mandate Agreement Template

attributes.name: tombstone_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fee arrangement is associated with a completed transaction eligible for tombstone publication (deal announcement). True = deal closed and fee earned; used for league table credit and marketing purposes.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal IB Marketing Policy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this fee arrangement record was most recently modified. Audit trail field for change tracking, data lineage, and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Data Governance Policy

products.name: investment_syndication
products.description: Master entity for syndicated lending and capital markets syndication activities. Captures syndication type (primary syndication, secondary sell-down, club deal), total facility size, bank's hold amount, target sell-down amount, syndication status, bookrunner role, co-arranger list, syndication launch date, and pricing flex. Supports loan syndication desk operations and CLO/ABS structuring activities.

attributes.name: investment_syndication_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the syndicated lending or capital markets syndication record. Primary key for the syndication master entity.
attributes.references: Loan Syndication and Trading Association (LSTA); Finastra Fusion Loan IQ

attributes.name: alco_meeting_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.alco_meeting. Business justification: Large syndication commitments requiring balance sheet capacity are escalated to ALCO for approval. Business process: ALCO governance over credit and liquidity risk from syndications ensures alignment

attributes.name: aml_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.aml_case. Business justification: Syndicated loan participants screened for sanctions/AML risk. Large cash movements and cross-border syndications trigger transaction monitoring. Compliance reviews syndication structures for layering,

attributes.name: capital_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.capital_plan. Business justification: Syndication pipeline affects projected credit RWA and capital ratios. Business process: capital stress testing includes syndication exposures in baseline and adverse scenarios to assess capital adequa

attributes.name: collateral_pledge_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to collateral.pledge. Business justification: Syndicated loans are secured by collateral pledges documented in security agreements. Real process: secured credit facility documentation, lien perfection filings, intercreditor agreements in syndicat

attributes.name: counterparty_rating_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.counterparty_rating. Business justification: Syndication participants require credit ratings for underwriting decisions, allocation sizing, pricing determination, and regulatory capital calculation. Essential for credit approval and risk-adjuste

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent investment banking deal or mandate under which this syndication is structured. Links syndication activity to the originating deal pipeline.
attributes.references: Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LSTA Market Practice

attributes.name: engagement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audit.engagement. Business justification: Syndication activities are audited for credit risk assessment, regulatory capital treatment, fee sharing compliance, documentation standards, and underwriting risk management. Critical for capital mar

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the credit facility or loan facility being syndicated. Ties the syndication record to the underlying credit agreement in the loan origination system.
attributes.references: Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LMA (Loan Market Association)

attributes.name: funding_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.funding_plan. Business justification: Large syndications require dedicated funding plans to ensure the bank can honor underwriting commitments. Business process: treasury funding planning coordinates with capital markets to pre-arrange fu

attributes.name: governing_law_jurisdiction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.jurisdiction. Business justification: Governing law jurisdiction determines loan enforceability, netting opinion requirements, and intercreditor agreement framework for syndicated lending transactions.

attributes.name: holiday_calendar_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.holiday_calendar. Business justification: Holiday calendar required for business day convention application, payment date calculation, and interest accrual period determination per ISDA definitions and LMA standards.

attributes.name: investor_fund_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.fund. Business justification: Institutional funds are major participants in syndicated loan and debt markets as lenders/investors. Real business process: syndication book-building, investor allocation management, and relationship

attributes.name: liquidity_position_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.liquidity_position. Business justification: Syndicated facilities impact bank liquidity positions through commitment drawdowns and funding requirements. Business process: liquidity risk management tracks syndication exposures in LCR/NSFR regula

attributes.name: marketing_channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.channel. Business justification: Loan syndications are marketed through specific channels - institutional sales desks, digital loan platforms (LoanIQ, SyndTrak), RM networks. Syndicate desks track marketing channel for lender reach a

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the borrower or obligor entity for whom the syndicated facility is being arranged. Core party reference for the syndication transaction.
attributes.references: Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LSTA; LMA

attributes.name: rate_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.rate_benchmark. Business justification: Reference rate benchmark required for IBOR transition (LIBOR→SOFR), interest accrual calculations, hedge accounting documentation, and LMA/LSTA loan documentation standards.

attributes.name: actual_selldown_amount
attributes.description: The amount actually distributed to third-party lenders at close of syndication. May differ from target_selldown_amount due to market conditions, pricing flex, or investor demand shortfall.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; IFRS 9

attributes.name: arrangement_fee_amount
attributes.description: The total arrangement fee earned by the bank for structuring and executing the syndication, expressed in deal currency. Recognized as fee income upon close per IFRS 15 / FASB ASC 606.
attributes.references: IFRS 15; FASB ASC 606; LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: asset_class
attributes.description: Broad asset class of the syndicated instrument: leveraged_loan, investment_grade, Collateralized Loan Obligation (CLO), Asset-Backed Security (ABS), Mortgage-Backed Security (MBS), or project_finance. Drives regulatory capital treatment and investor eligibility.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III; SEC Regulation AB; FRTB

attributes.name: bank_hold_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the total facility that the arranging bank intends to retain on its own balance sheet after syndication. Reflects the bank's final hold position and drives RWA and capital consumption calculations.
attributes.references: OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance; BCBS Basel III; LSTA Market Practice

attributes.name: bookrunner_role
attributes.description: The bank's role in the syndication as bookrunner or arranger: sole_bookrunner, joint_bookrunner, co_bookrunner, mandated_lead_arranger (MLA), or lead_arranger. Determines fee entitlement and decision-making authority in the syndicate.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; Finastra Fusion Loan IQ

attributes.name: close_date
attributes.description: The date on which the syndication was formally closed and the credit agreement was executed with the final lender group. Corresponds to the effective date of the facility.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; FASB ASC 310

attributes.name: co_arranger_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of co-arranger bank names or BIC codes participating in the syndication alongside the bookrunner. Captures the arranger group composition for tombstone records, fee sharing, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; SWIFT BIC Standard

attributes.name: commitment_deadline
attributes.description: The deadline by which prospective lenders must submit their commitments during the bookbuilding phase. Drives the syndication desk's investor outreach timeline.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the syndication record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides audit trail for record origination and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; FASB ASC 310; Finastra Fusion Loan IQ Audit Trail

attributes.name: credit_rating_moodys
attributes.description: The Moody's Investors Service credit rating assigned to the syndicated facility or borrower at the time of syndication (e.g., Ba1, B2, Caa1). Used alongside S&P rating for dual-rating requirements in leveraged loan markets.
attributes.references: Moody's Investors Service; BCBS Basel III; SEC Rule 17g-5

attributes.name: credit_rating_sp
attributes.description: The Standard & Poor's credit rating assigned to the syndicated facility or the borrower at the time of syndication (e.g., BB+, B, CCC). Drives investor eligibility, pricing, and regulatory capital treatment.
attributes.references: S&P Global Ratings; BCBS Basel III IRB Approach; SEC Rule 17g-5

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the syndicated facility (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Governs all monetary amounts on this syndication record.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; SWIFT; BIS Foreign Exchange Committee

attributes.name: documentation_standard
attributes.description: The market documentation standard used for the syndicated loan agreement: LMA (Loan Market Association — EMEA), LSTA (Loan Syndication and Trading Association — US), APLMA (Asia Pacific), or bespoke. Governs transferability, voting thresholds, and secondary market conventions.
attributes.references: LMA Standard Documentation; LSTA Credit Agreement; APLMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: esg_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the syndicated facility is structured as an ESG-linked loan or sustainability-linked loan (SLL), where pricing is tied to the borrower's ESG performance targets. Supports green finance reporting and investor ESG mandates.
attributes.references: LMA Green Loan Principles; LMA Sustainability-Linked Loan Principles; ICMA Green Bond Principles

attributes.name: facility_type
attributes.description: The structural type of the syndicated credit facility: term_loan_a (amortizing, bank-held), term_loan_b (institutional, bullet), revolving_credit (RCF), bridge_loan (short-term acquisition financing), or delayed_draw (DDTL). Determines investor base and secondary market liquidity.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; Finastra Fusion Loan IQ

attributes.name: flex_amount_bps
attributes.description: The magnitude of the pricing flex applied, expressed in basis points. Positive value indicates widening; negative value indicates tightening. Captures the delta between initial price talk and final pricing.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines

attributes.name: launch_date
attributes.description: The date on which the syndication was formally launched to the market, i.e., when the information memorandum and term sheet were distributed to prospective lenders.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: league_table_credit
attributes.description: Determines how this syndication is credited in investment banking league tables: full_credit (sole bookrunner), pro_rata (shared among joint bookrunners), or no_credit (co-arranger only). Drives competitive ranking and business development reporting.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Standards; LSTA

attributes.name: lender_count
attributes.description: The total number of lenders in the final syndicate at close. Indicates syndication breadth and diversification of the lender group; used in post-deal analytics and tombstone records.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: leveraged_loan_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the syndicated facility meets the OCC/Fed/FDIC definition of a leveraged loan (typically total debt/EBITDA > 4x or borrower rated below investment grade). Triggers enhanced regulatory scrutiny and reporting under interagency leveraged lending guidance.
attributes.references: OCC/Fed/FDIC Leveraged Lending Guidance (2013); BCBS Basel III; Federal Reserve SR 13-3

attributes.name: mandate_date
attributes.description: The date on which the borrower formally awarded the syndication mandate to the arranging bank(s). Marks the start of the syndication process and triggers fee accrual.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: oid_bps
attributes.description: The original issue discount expressed in basis points, representing the upfront discount to par at which the loan is issued to lenders. Common in leveraged loan syndications; impacts lender yield and borrower all-in cost.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; IRS OID Rules (IRC §1272); FASB ASC 835-30

attributes.name: oversubscription_amount
attributes.description: The amount by which investor commitments exceeded the target syndication amount during bookbuilding. A positive value indicates strong market demand; used for pricing flex decisions and greenshoe allocation.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines

attributes.name: pricing_date
attributes.description: The date on which final pricing (spread, OID, fees) was determined and communicated to lenders. Marks the transition from bookbuilding to allocation in the syndication lifecycle.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; FINRA TRACE

attributes.name: pricing_flex_type
attributes.description: Indicates the direction of pricing flex applied during bookbuilding: tightened (spread reduced due to oversubscription), held (no change), flexed_wider (spread increased due to weak demand), oid_added, oid_increased, or structure_changed. Key indicator of market reception.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines; OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance

attributes.name: purpose_code
attributes.description: The stated purpose of the syndicated facility: acquisition_finance, leveraged_buyout (LBO), refinancing, general_corporate, capital_expenditure (capex), or working_capital. Used for regulatory classification, OCC leveraged lending identification, and portfolio analytics.
attributes.references: OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance (2013); BCBS Basel III; LSTA Market Practice

attributes.name: reference
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned to the syndication transaction, used in deal communications, tombstones, and regulatory filings. Corresponds to the deal reference in Loan IQ.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation

attributes.name: spread_bps
attributes.description: The credit spread over the reference rate expressed in basis points (BPS) at which the syndicated facility is priced. Core pricing parameter for lender economics and secondary market trading.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; ISDA

attributes.name: syndication_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the syndication process: mandate_awarded (bank selected as arranger), launched (syndication formally opened to market), bookbuilding (collecting lender commitments), priced (spread and terms finalized), closed (facility fully allocated), withdrawn (deal pulled from market), failed (insufficient demand). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mandate_awarded|launched|bookbuilding|priced|closed|withdrawn|failed|post_close — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines

attributes.name: syndication_type
attributes.description: Classification of the syndication structure: primary_syndication (initial distribution to lender group), secondary_sell_down (post-close transfer of hold), club_deal (small bilateral group), best_efforts (no underwriting commitment), underwritten (bank commits full amount). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: primary_syndication|secondary_sell_down|club_deal|best_efforts|underwritten|participation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines; OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance

attributes.name: target_selldown_amount
attributes.description: The target amount the bank aims to distribute to third-party lenders through the syndication process. Equals total_facility_amount minus bank_hold_amount at deal inception; may be revised during bookbuilding.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Syndicated Loan Guidelines; OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance

attributes.name: tenor_months
attributes.description: The contractual tenor of the syndicated facility expressed in months from the close date to final maturity. Key parameter for duration risk, regulatory capital, and investor suitability assessment.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; BCBS Basel III

attributes.name: tombstone_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the bank has received borrower consent to publicize this transaction in a tombstone announcement. Required before any deal announcement in pitch books, league tables, or press releases.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; SEC Regulation FD

attributes.name: total_facility_amount
attributes.description: Gross size of the syndicated credit facility or capital markets transaction in the deal currency. Represents the full commitment amount before any sell-down or hold reduction.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; IFRS 9; FASB ASC 310

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent update to the syndication record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver layer ETL pipeline and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Finastra Fusion Loan IQ Audit Trail; Databricks Delta Lake CDC

attributes.name: upfront_fee_bps
attributes.description: The upfront participation fee paid to lenders expressed in basis points of their commitment. Incentivizes early commitment during bookbuilding and is a key component of lender all-in yield.
attributes.references: LSTA Market Practice; LMA Standard Documentation; FASB ASC 310-20

products.name: syndication_allocation
products.description: Transactional line-item record capturing the allocation of syndicated loan or bond tranches to individual investor or lender participants. Records participant institution, allocated amount, participation percentage, commitment type (firm, soft), allocation date, settlement date, participation agreement reference, and fee share. Child of syndication — enables the syndication desk to manage investor books, track commitments, finalize allocations for primary syndication and secondary sell-down, and reconcile with settlement systems.

attributes.name: syndication_allocation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each syndication allocation line-item record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this transactional line entity.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ Syndication Module

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent investment banking deal or mandate record. Links the syndication allocation back to the originating M&A, DCF, or capital markets advisory deal in the deal pipeline.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; Investment Banking Deal Management

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.gl_account. Business justification: Syndication participations create loan assets on balance sheet that must be posted to specific GL accounts for financial reporting and regulatory capital (RWA) calculation. Replaces denormalized gl_ac

attributes.name: investment_syndication_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the parent syndication deal or tranche header record. Links this allocation line to the overarching syndicated loan or bond facility from which it is derived.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ Syndication Module

attributes.name: org_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal syndication desk or business unit responsible for managing this allocation. Used for PnL attribution, revenue allocation, and line-of-business (LOB) reporting.
attributes.references: Core Banking System — Temenos T24 / FIS Profile; General Ledger and Financial Accounting System — Oracle Financials / SAP S4HANA

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investor or lender institution receiving this allocation. Identifies the counterparty bank, fund, or institutional investor participating in the syndicated facility.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards

attributes.name: rate_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.rate_benchmark. Business justification: Reference rate type links to rate_benchmark for participant-specific pricing, IBOR fallback provisions, and interest payment calculations per participation agreement.

attributes.name: tranche_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific tranche of the syndicated facility being allocated (e.g., Term Loan A, Term Loan B, Revolving Credit Facility). A syndication may have multiple tranches with separate allocation books.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines

attributes.name: actual_settlement_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which settlement was completed for this allocation. May differ from the scheduled settlement date due to failed settlements, late funding, or operational delays. Used for settlement reconciliation and SLA monitoring.
attributes.references: Payment Processing Hub — ACI Worldwide / Volante; LSTA Settlement Standards; Federal Reserve Regulation CC

attributes.name: allocated_amount
attributes.description: The principal monetary amount of the syndicated loan or bond tranche allocated to this participant institution. Represents the participant's share of the total facility commitment in the deal currency.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; IFRS 9; FASB ASC 310

attributes.name: allocation_date
attributes.description: The business date on which the syndication desk formally allocated this tranche amount to the participant institution. Marks the principal real-world event time for this allocation line-item.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards; LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines

attributes.name: allocation_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this allocation line, as generated by the Loan IQ syndication module or the syndication desk. Used in participant confirmation notices, participation agreements, and settlement instructions.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards

attributes.name: allocation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of this syndication allocation line. Tracks progression from indicative interest through firm commitment, final allocation, settlement, and any post-close transfers or cancellations.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards

attributes.name: allocation_type
attributes.description: Classifies whether this allocation is part of the primary syndication (initial distribution), a secondary sell-down (post-close transfer of risk), a formal loan transfer, or a sub-participation arrangement. Determines accounting treatment and regulatory capital impact.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards; FASB ASC 860 Transfers and Servicing; IFRS 9

attributes.name: arrangement_fee_amount
attributes.description: The upfront arrangement or structuring fee allocated to this participant as part of the syndication economics. Paid by the borrower and distributed among arrangers and participants per the fee letter.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LMA Fee Letter Standards; FASB ASC 310-20 Loan Origination Fees

attributes.name: booking_entity_code
attributes.description: The legal entity code of the bank's booking entity that holds this allocation on its balance sheet. Critical for regulatory capital reporting, FATCA/CRS entity-level reporting, and intercompany reconciliation in multi-entity banking groups.
attributes.references: Regulatory Reporting Platform — AxiomSL / Wolters Kluwer OneSumX; FATCA IRS Regulations; CRS OECD Standard; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: commitment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the participant institution submitted its commitment (firm or soft) to participate in the syndication. Precedes the allocation date and is used to track the book-building timeline.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines

attributes.name: commitment_type
attributes.description: Nature of the participant's commitment to the allocation. Firm commitments are legally binding; soft commitments are indicative and subject to withdrawal; sub-underwrite and underwrite indicate risk-taking obligations; best_efforts indicates no guaranteed take-down.
attributes.references: LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Credit Risk Framework

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this syndication allocation record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; General Ledger and Financial Accounting System — Oracle Financials / SAP S4HANA; FDIC Record Retention Requirements

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the allocated amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Determines the settlement currency and FX conversion requirements for cross-border syndications.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SWIFT BIC Standards; Federal Reserve System FX Guidelines

attributes.name: ead_amount
attributes.description: The exposure at default (EAD) for this allocation, representing the expected outstanding balance at the time of default. Includes drawn amounts plus estimated undrawn commitments for revolving facilities. Core input to ECL and RWA calculations.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III IRB Approach; IFRS 9 ECL; FASB CECL ASC 326; Risk Management Platform — SAS Risk Management / Moody's RiskAuthority

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this allocation becomes legally binding and the participant's obligations under the participation agreement commence. Aligns with the facility closing date or drawdown date.
attributes.references: LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards; Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which this allocation commitment expires if not settled or transferred. Applicable to revolving credit facilities and unfunded commitments where the participant's obligation has a defined end date.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; BCBS Basel III Credit Risk

attributes.name: fee_share_pct
attributes.description: The participant's proportional share of total syndication fees expressed as a decimal percentage. Used to calculate the participant's entitlement to arrangement, participation, and agency fees distributed from the fee pool.
attributes.references: LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards; Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ

attributes.name: ftp_rate
attributes.description: The internal Funds Transfer Pricing (FTP) rate applied to this allocation for internal profitability measurement and ALCO reporting. Used by the Treasury function to allocate the cost of funds and liquidity premium to the originating business line.
attributes.references: ALCO Asset-Liability Management Framework; Treasury and Liquidity Management — FTP Policy; BCBS IRRBB

attributes.name: hold_amount
attributes.description: The final amount the participant intends to retain on its own balance sheet after any secondary sell-down. Represents the net retained exposure post-syndication and is used for RWA and capital adequacy calculations.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; BCBS Basel III; OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance; CCAR/DFAST Stress Testing

attributes.name: instrument_type
attributes.description: The type of debt instrument being allocated to the participant. Determines the applicable documentation standard (LMA/LSTA), interest calculation convention, and regulatory capital treatment under Basel III.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; BCBS Basel III; FASB ASC 310

attributes.name: interest_spread_bps
attributes.description: The credit spread in basis points (BPS) over the reference rate (e.g., SOFR, EURIBOR) applicable to this participant's allocation. Determines the participant's interest income on the allocated commitment.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; ISDA SOFR Fallback Protocol; BCBS Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB)

attributes.name: is_agent_bank
attributes.description: Indicates whether the participant institution is also acting as the facility agent or security agent for the syndicated loan. The agent bank administers payments, waivers, and amendments on behalf of the lender group.
attributes.references: LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards; Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ

attributes.name: is_lead_arranger
attributes.description: Indicates whether the participant institution is acting as lead arranger or bookrunner for this syndication. Lead arrangers have additional obligations including book-building, documentation, and agent responsibilities.
attributes.references: LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards

attributes.name: lgd_pct
attributes.description: The loss given default (LGD) estimate for this allocation expressed as a decimal percentage of the exposure at default (EAD). Used in ECL provisioning under IFRS 9/CECL and regulatory capital calculations under the IRB approach.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III IRB Approach; IFRS 9 ECL; FASB CECL ASC 326; Risk Management Platform — SAS Risk Management / Moody's RiskAuthority

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for syndication desk commentary, special conditions, or exceptions associated with this allocation. May include investor-specific terms, waiver notes, or documentation exceptions agreed during the book-building process.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines

attributes.name: participant_role
attributes.description: Role of the participant institution in the syndication structure. Determines fee entitlement, voting rights, and reporting obligations. Lead arrangers and bookrunners typically receive higher arrangement fees.
attributes.references: LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards

attributes.name: participation_agreement_ref
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the executed participation agreement between the arranger and the participant institution governing the terms of this allocation. Used for legal documentation reconciliation.
attributes.references: LMA Loan Market Association Standard Participation Agreement; LSTA Participation Agreement

attributes.name: participation_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee paid to the participant institution for joining the syndication, typically expressed as basis points (BPS) on the allocated commitment. Distinct from the arrangement fee paid to the lead arranger.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; LMA Fee Letter Standards; FASB ASC 310-20

attributes.name: participation_pct
attributes.description: The participant institution's pro-rata share of the total syndicated facility expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 0.125000 = 12.5%). Used to calculate pro-rata distributions of interest, fees, and principal repayments.
attributes.references: LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; LSTA Syndicated Loan Market Standards; Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ

attributes.name: pd_rating
attributes.description: The probability of default (PD) assigned to the participant or the underlying borrower for this allocation, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.005 = 0.5%). Used in ECL calculations under IFRS 9/CECL and IRB capital models.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III IRB Approach; IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss (ECL); FASB CECL ASC 326; Risk Management Platform — SAS Risk Management / Moody's RiskAuthority

attributes.name: regulatory_capital_approach
attributes.description: The Basel III regulatory capital approach applied to this allocation for RWA calculation: Standardized Approach (SA), Foundation Internal Ratings-Based (IRB), or Advanced IRB. Determines the methodology used in CCAR/DFAST stress testing submissions.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Capital Framework; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST; OCC Capital Adequacy Standards; Regulatory Reporting Platform — AxiomSL

attributes.name: rwa_amount
attributes.description: The risk-weighted asset (RWA) amount attributable to this allocation, calculated under the Basel III Standardized Approach (SA) or Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) approach. Used for capital adequacy reporting under CCAR/DFAST and CET1 ratio calculations.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Capital Framework; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST; OCC Capital Adequacy Standards; Regulatory Reporting Platform — AxiomSL / Wolters Kluwer OneSumX

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which funds are expected to be transferred from the participant to the agent bank, completing the settlement of this allocation. Used for liquidity planning, RTGS scheduling, and reconciliation with the Payment Processing Hub.
attributes.references: Payment Processing Hub — ACI Worldwide / Volante; RTGS Settlement Standards; LSTA T+1 Settlement Convention; Federal Reserve Regulation CC

attributes.name: syndication_market
attributes.description: The market segment classification of the syndicated facility. Investment grade and leveraged loans have different documentation standards, pricing conventions, and regulatory capital treatments. Used for portfolio segmentation and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance (2013); BCBS Basel III; LSTA Leveraged Loan Market Standards; LMA Investment Grade Loan Standards

attributes.name: tombstone_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this allocation qualifies for inclusion in the deal tombstone record, which publicly commemorates the completed transaction. Tombstone eligibility is typically limited to lead arrangers, bookrunners, and significant participants above a minimum threshold.
attributes.references: Investment Banking Deal Management; LMA Syndicated Lending Guidelines; FINRA Public Disclosure Rules

attributes.name: underwrite_amount
attributes.description: The amount of the facility that the participant has underwritten (i.e., committed to take onto its own balance sheet if the syndication is not fully subscribed). May differ from the final allocated amount after sell-down.
attributes.references: Loan Origination System — Finastra Fusion Loan IQ; BCBS Basel III Capital Framework; OCC Leveraged Lending Guidance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this syndication allocation record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change data capture (CDC), ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; FDIC Record Retention Requirements; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer CDC Standards

products.name: underwriting
products.description: Master entity representing the bank's underwriting commitment for equity or debt capital markets transactions. Captures commitment type (firm commitment, best efforts, standby), underwritten amount, underwriting spread, over-allotment option (greenshoe), commitment date, pricing date, settlement date, and syndicate role (lead bookrunner, joint bookrunner, co-manager). Tracks the bank's risk exposure during the underwriting period.

attributes.name: underwriting_id
attributes.description: Primary key for underwriting

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.fund. Business justification: Institutional funds are cornerstone investors in underwritten equity and debt offerings, often receiving anchor allocations. Real business process: pre-marketing to anchor investors, allocation manage

attributes.name: booking_branch_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.branch. Business justification: Underwriting commitments for municipal bonds, regional offerings, or private placements are booked through specific branch locations (regional/community banking underwriting desks). Required for branc

attributes.name: capital_markets_offering_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.offering. Business justification: Underwriting commitments are made for specific capital markets offerings. While both underwriting and offering reference deal_id, one deal can have multiple offerings (e.g., primary offering + greensh

attributes.name: capital_ratio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.capital_ratio. Business justification: Underwriting commitments consume regulatory capital (RWA) and impact CET1 ratios. Business process: capital planning and CCAR stress testing include capital markets pipeline exposures in RWA projectio

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to collateral.collateral_asset. Business justification: Underwritten securities (ABS, MBS, covered bonds) are backed by collateral pools that must be tracked for prospectus disclosure and investor reporting. Real process: asset-backed securities issuance,

Direct regulatory filing obligation under Securities Act. Compliance tracks filing status, acknowledgments, and amendments

attributes.name: credit_exposure_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.credit_exposure. Business justification: Underwriting commitments generate credit exposure to issuers requiring capital allocation, limit monitoring, and regulatory capital calculation. Links underwriting transactions to EAD and RWA for Base

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent investment banking deal or transaction for which this underwriting commitment is being made. Links to the deal pipeline entity.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hr.employee. Business justification: Underwriting commitments require a responsible banker for risk ownership, capital allocation approval, and P&L attribution. Regulatory capital frameworks (Basel III) and internal risk management requi

attributes.name: engagement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audit.engagement. Business justification: Underwriting commitments are major audit subjects for risk exposure assessment, capital adequacy calculation, regulatory compliance (SEC registration), revenue recognition, and stabilization activity

attributes.name: funding_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.funding_plan. Business justification: Underwriting commitments may require pre-arranged funding capacity to ensure settlement capability. Business process: treasury coordinates with capital markets to ensure funding availability for under

attributes.name: instrument_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to security.instrument. Business justification: Underwriting commitments are for specific securities, not just issuers. Required for inventory risk management, stabilization trading, greenshoe exercise, settlement instructions, and fee calculation

attributes.name: issuer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the corporate or sovereign issuer (client) on whose behalf the bank is underwriting the securities offering.

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: Underwriting commitments create contingent liabilities that must be tracked by legal entity for regulatory capital (market risk, underwriting risk), financial statement disclosure (IAS 37), and legal

attributes.name: liquidity_position_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.liquidity_position. Business justification: Underwriting commitments create contingent liquidity obligations tracked in liquidity stress scenarios. Business process: regulatory liquidity reporting (LCR/NSFR) includes underwriting exposures as p

attributes.name: market_risk_position_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.market_risk_position. Business justification: Underwriting commitments create market risk positions (inventory risk, price risk, spread risk) requiring VaR calculation, hedging strategies, and trading desk risk limits. Essential for capital marke

attributes.name: reference_instrument_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.instrument_classification. Business justification: Security type classification drives FRTB book assignment, IFRS 9 classification, regulatory capital treatment, and Volcker Rule compliance for underwriting inventory.

attributes.name: reference_instrument_identifier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.instrument_identifier. Business justification: Instrument identifier (ISIN/CUSIP) required for securities master data, trade confirmation matching, regulatory reporting (MiFID II, Dodd-Frank), and settlement instructions.

attributes.name: regulatory_exam_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_exam. Business justification: Underwriting practices reviewed in SEC, FINRA exams for compliance with securities laws, disclosure requirements, Reg M stabilization rules, and allocation fairness. Examiners trace underwriting commi

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.jurisdiction. Business justification: Regulatory jurisdiction determines prospectus requirements (SEC S-1, EU Prospectus Regulation), underwriting agreement enforceability, and securities law compliance framework.

attributes.name: agreement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the formal underwriting agreement between the bank (and co-underwriters) and the issuer was executed. This is the legally binding contract governing the terms of the underwriting commitment.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933 Section 11; FINRA Rule 5110; ISDA Framework

attributes.name: bank_allocation_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total offering size allocated to this bank as its underwriting commitment share within the syndicate. Determines the bank's proportional fee entitlement and risk exposure.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Syndicate Management Standard

attributes.name: book_runner_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the bank is acting as a bookrunner (lead or joint) for this offering, responsible for managing the order book during the book-building process. True if the bank has bookrunner responsibilities; False for co-manager or selling group roles.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Syndicate Role Classification Standard

attributes.name: commitment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the bank formally committed to underwrite the offering, typically coinciding with the signing of the mandate letter or underwriting agreement. Marks the start of the bank's underwriting risk exposure period.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Deal Lifecycle Standard

attributes.name: commitment_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this underwriting commitment, used in mandate letters, syndicate agreements, and regulatory filings. Format: LOB-UW-YYYY-NNNNNN.

attributes.name: commitment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the underwriting commitment. Mandated: bank has received the mandate; Active: commitment is live during the offering period; Priced: pricing has been set; Closed: transaction has settled; Withdrawn: issuer withdrew the offering; Terminated: commitment cancelled prior to pricing.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Lifecycle Management Standard

attributes.name: commitment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the underwriting commitment structure. Firm commitment means the bank purchases all securities and resells them; best efforts means the bank sells as much as possible without guaranteeing the full amount; standby is used in rights offerings; all-or-none requires full subscription or cancellation; mini-max sets a minimum threshold.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; IOSCO Principles

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this underwriting commitment record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS BCBS 239 Data Governance; Internal Audit Trail Standard

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the underwritten amount and all fee fields on this commitment (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, JPY). Required for multi-currency reporting and FX (Foreign Exchange) risk management.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; BCBS Basel III; IFRS 9

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the SEC registration statement became effective, permitting the public sale of securities. For Rule 144A transactions, this is the date the offering memorandum was finalized.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933 Section 8; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: expected_fee_revenue
attributes.description: The bank's expected gross fee revenue from this underwriting commitment, calculated as the bank's allocated underwriting spread applied to its committed underwriting amount. Used for revenue forecasting, deal profitability analysis, and RAROC (Risk-Adjusted Return on Capital) calculations.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition; IFRS 15; Internal FTP (Funds Transfer Pricing) Standard

attributes.name: fee_bps
attributes.description: The portion of the underwriting spread allocated as the underwriting fee, expressed in basis points. Compensates syndicate members for bearing the underwriting risk during the offering period.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508

attributes.name: greenshoe_option_amount
attributes.description: The maximum additional amount (in base currency) that the underwriters may purchase from the issuer under the over-allotment (greenshoe) option, typically up to 15% of the base offering size. Exercised to stabilize the aftermarket price. Named after the Green Shoe Manufacturing Company, the first company to use this mechanism.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-7; Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: greenshoe_option_flag
