attributes.description: Indicates whether an over-allotment (greenshoe) option has been granted to the underwriters in this transaction. True if a greenshoe option exists; False if no over-allotment option is included.

attributes.name: league_table_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transaction qualifies for inclusion in investment banking league table rankings (e.g., Bloomberg, Dealogic, Thomson Reuters). Transactions may be excluded due to size thresholds, role limitations, or issuer type restrictions.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Standards; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: lock_up_period_days
attributes.description: The number of days following the offering during which existing shareholders and insiders are contractually prohibited from selling their shares. Typically 90 or 180 days for IPOs. Relevant for aftermarket risk management and secondary trading restrictions.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; NYSE/NASDAQ Listing Standards

attributes.name: management_fee_bps
attributes.description: The portion of the underwriting spread allocated as the management fee, expressed in basis points. Compensates the lead manager(s) for structuring, due diligence, and transaction management responsibilities.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508

attributes.name: mandate_letter_date
attributes.description: The date on which the issuer formally awarded the underwriting mandate to the bank via a signed mandate letter. Precedes the commitment date and marks the formal engagement of the bank as underwriter.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Investment Banking Mandate Management Standard

attributes.name: offering_price
attributes.description: The final public offering price per unit (share or bond face value) at which securities are sold to investors. For equity, expressed as price per share; for debt, expressed as a percentage of par value. Determined at pricing date.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 501; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: offering_size
attributes.description: The total gross proceeds of the offering at the offering price, representing the full transaction size including any greenshoe option if exercised. Distinct from underwritten_amount which reflects only the bank's committed portion.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 501; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: offering_type
attributes.description: Classification of the securities offering structure. IPO (Initial Public Offering) is the first public sale; follow-on is a subsequent equity offering; 144A is a private placement to qualified institutional buyers; Reg S covers offshore offerings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ipo|follow_on|secondary|rights_offering|private_placement|144a|reg_s|block_trade — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933 Rule 144A; Regulation S; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: pricing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the final offering price and size are determined through the book-building process. Marks the end of the primary underwriting risk period for firm commitment transactions as the spread is locked in.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; FINRA Rule 5110; IOSCO Principles

attributes.name: prospectus_type
attributes.description: The type of SEC registration statement or offering document filed for this transaction. S-1 is the standard IPO registration; S-3 is for seasoned issuers; F-1 is for foreign private issuers; 424B is the final prospectus; offering memorandum is used for 144A/Reg S private placements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: s1|f1|s3|s11|424b|offering_memorandum|prospectus_supplement|base_prospectus — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933; SEC Forms S-1, S-3, F-1; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: roadshow_start_date
attributes.description: The date on which the investor roadshow commenced for this offering. The roadshow is the marketing period during which management presents to institutional investors prior to pricing.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 5110; Internal Deal Lifecycle Standard

attributes.name: rwa_amount
attributes.description: The Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) amount attributable to this underwriting commitment, calculated per Basel III standardized or internal ratings-based (IRB) approach. Drives capital charge allocation and CET1 (Common Equity Tier 1) consumption reporting.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Capital Framework; OCC Capital Adequacy Standards; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST

attributes.name: sec_file_number
attributes.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) file number assigned to the registration statement for this offering (e.g., 333-XXXXXX for Securities Act registrations). Used for regulatory tracking and EDGAR cross-referencing.
attributes.references: SEC Securities Act of 1933 Section 8; SEC EDGAR Filing System

attributes.name: selling_concession_bps
attributes.description: The portion of the underwriting spread allocated as the selling concession, expressed in basis points. Paid to dealers and selling group members for distributing securities to end investors.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the securities are delivered to investors and proceeds are remitted to the issuer. Typically T+1 for US equity offerings and T+2 or T+3 for debt. Marks the completion of the underwriting commitment.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 15c6-1 (T+1 Settlement); FINRA Rule 11860; DTCC Settlement Standards

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this underwriting commitment record originated (e.g., MUREX or CALYPSO for trading/deal capture, DEALOGIC for deal tracking, LOAN_IQ for syndicated lending mandates). Required for data lineage and ETL reconciliation.
attributes.references: BCBS BCBS 239 Data Aggregation and Reporting Principles; Internal Data Lineage Standard

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: The native primary key or record identifier of this underwriting commitment in the originating operational system of record (e.g., Murex deal ID, Calypso transaction ID, Dealogic deal reference). Enables bi-directional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the source system.
attributes.references: BCBS BCBS 239 Data Aggregation and Reporting Principles; Internal Data Lineage Standard

attributes.name: spread_bps
attributes.description: The total underwriting spread expressed in basis points (BPS), representing the difference between the price paid to the issuer and the public offering price. This is the primary revenue metric for the underwriting commitment and is split among syndicate members per the fee allocation agreement.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K Item 508; IOSCO Principles

attributes.name: stabilization_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the bank is acting as stabilizing manager for this offering, authorized to conduct price stabilization transactions in the aftermarket to support the offering price. True if the bank has stabilization responsibilities.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-7; EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) Article 5; FCA Stabilisation Rules

attributes.name: syndicate_role
attributes.description: The bank's role within the underwriting syndicate. Lead bookrunner has primary responsibility for book building and allocation; joint bookrunner shares that responsibility; co-manager has a smaller participation; selling group members distribute but do not underwrite. Determines fee economics and regulatory obligations.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; IOSCO Principles for Secondary Markets

attributes.name: tombstone_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a tombstone advertisement has been published for this completed transaction. Tombstones are formal announcements of completed capital markets transactions and serve as marketing credentials for the bank's league table rankings.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Investment Banking Marketing Standard

attributes.name: underwritten_amount
attributes.description: The gross principal amount (in base currency) that the bank has committed to underwrite for this transaction. For firm commitment deals, this represents the bank's maximum financial exposure prior to distribution. Key input for RWA (Risk-Weighted Assets) and capital charge calculations under Basel III.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Capital Framework; SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this underwriting commitment record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, data lineage, and incremental ETL (Extract Transform Load) processing.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS BCBS 239 Data Governance; Internal Audit Trail Standard

products.name: investment_investor_order
products.description: Transactional record capturing individual investor orders received during the bookbuilding process for ECM and DCM transactions. Records investor name, order type (strike, limit, step), order size, price limit, order date and time, order status (active, filled, cancelled), allocation received, and investor tier classification. Enables bookrunner to manage the order book and determine final pricing and allocation.
products.reference: Bookbuilding Order / Investor Indication of Interest

attributes.name: investment_investor_order_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each investor order record in the bookbuilding order book. Primary key for the investor_order data product.

attributes.name: aml_alert_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.aml_alert. Business justification: Large or unusual investor orders trigger transaction monitoring alerts (structuring, layering patterns, rapid turnover). AML surveillance systems flag orders exceeding thresholds or exhibiting suspici

attributes.name: branch_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.branch. Business justification: Investor orders in capital markets offerings placed through branch locations (retail IPO participation, regional institutional desks) require branch tracking for regulatory reporting (SEC Rule 15c2-8,

attributes.name: capital_markets_offering_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.offering. Business justification: Investor orders are placed during bookbuilding for a specific capital markets offering. While investor_order has deal_id, one deal can have multiple offerings. Orders must reference the specific offer

attributes.name: coverage_assignment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the sales professional or relationship manager who solicited or managed this investor order on behalf of the bookrunner. Used for sales credit attribution, commission calculation, and investor relationship tracking.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4512; SEC Rule 17a-3; MiFID II Article 25

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent capital markets transaction (ECM or DCM deal) for which this investor order was submitted during the bookbuilding process.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hr.employee. Business justification: Investor orders require a covering banker for relationship credit attribution, order dispute resolution, and regulatory best execution reporting (MiFID II). Capital markets operations track which bank

attributes.name: instrument_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to security.instrument. Business justification: Investor orders in offerings are for specific instruments. Required for order book management, allocation algorithms, settlement file generation, and post-IPO position reconciliation. Complements exis

attributes.name: investor_geography_country_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.country. Business justification: Investor geography required for Reg S/144A eligibility determination, geographic allocation analysis, and cross-border securities offering compliance.

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investment bank or syndicate member acting as bookrunner who received and recorded this investor order. In syndicated deals, multiple bookrunners may collect orders from different investor segments.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the institutional or retail investor entity that submitted this order. Links to the investor master record for KYC and AML compliance purposes.

attributes.name: sanctions_screening_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.sanctions_screening_event. Business justification: Every investor order must be screened against OFAC/sanctions lists before allocation. Mandatory compliance control for capital markets offerings. Screening event records match status, disposition, and

attributes.name: settlement_account_deposit_account_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Settlement Account Deposit Account Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to account.deposit_account. Business justification: Capital markets investor orders settle cash through specific deposit accounts. Settlement operations require validated account linkage for payment processing, reconciliation, and regulatory reporting

attributes.name: allocation_amount
attributes.description: Total monetary value of the allocation received by the investor, calculated as allocation_size multiplied by allocation_price. Represents the investor's financial commitment to the transaction. Used for settlement, fee calculation, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles

attributes.name: allocation_price
attributes.description: The final deal price per share or per unit at which the investor's allocation was confirmed. Typically the IPO offer price or bond issue price. Used for settlement and P&L attribution.
attributes.references: IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: allocation_size
attributes.description: The number of shares or face value amount actually allocated to the investor following the bookrunner's allocation decision at deal pricing. Zero if the order was not filled. Compared against order_size to determine fill ratio.
attributes.references: IOSCO Principles for IPO Bookbuilding; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation M

attributes.name: allocation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the allocation decision was communicated to the investor following deal pricing. Marks the transition from bookbuilding to allocation phase. Used for settlement timeline tracking (T+1, T+2).
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation M; T+1 Settlement Rule

attributes.name: cancellation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the investor cancelled or withdrew the order from the book. Null if the order was not cancelled. Used for demand attrition analysis and bookbuilding audit trail.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-3; MiFID II Article 25

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this investor order record was first captured and persisted in the order management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes. May differ from order_timestamp if there is a processing lag.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-3; FINRA Rule 4511; SOX Section 802

attributes.name: custodian_name
attributes.description: Name of the custodian bank or prime broker responsible for holding the allocated securities on behalf of the investor. Used for settlement instruction routing and corporate trust/custody services coordination.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17f-1; FINRA Rule 4311; Corporate Trust and Custody Services standards

attributes.name: demand_multiple
attributes.description: Ratio of the investor's order size to the investor's expected or target allocation, indicating the degree of oversubscription at the individual investor level. Used by the bookrunner to assess investor conviction and calibrate allocation decisions.

attributes.name: greenshoe_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this investor order is eligible to be filled from the overallotment (greenshoe) option, allowing the bookrunner to allocate up to 15% additional shares beyond the base offering size to cover excess demand.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation M Rule 104; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Rule 10b-7

attributes.name: investor_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the investor or institution placing the order. Used for order book management, allocation decisions, and regulatory reporting. May represent an institutional fund, asset manager, or individual investor.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4512; SEC Rule 17a-3; GDPR Article 4; FATCA

attributes.name: investor_tier
attributes.description: Classification of the investor by tier, which influences allocation priority and deal economics. 'anchor' investors commit pre-IPO with lock-up; 'cornerstone' investors receive guaranteed allocations; 'institutional' covers qualified institutional buyers (QIBs); 'retail' covers individual investors; 'strategic' covers corporate or government investors with strategic interest.
attributes.references: IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles; SEC Rule 144A; FINRA Rule 5110; Hong Kong SFC Listing Rules

attributes.name: investor_type
attributes.description: Categorization of the investor by institutional type. Drives regulatory treatment, allocation policy, and suitability assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: asset_manager|hedge_fund|pension_fund|sovereign_wealth|insurance|bank|family_office|retail|corporate|endowment — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: MiFID II Article 4; SEC Rule 144A; FINRA Rule 4512; IOSCO Principles

attributes.name: is_anchor_investor
attributes.description: Indicates whether this investor has been designated as an anchor investor for the transaction, committing to a pre-IPO allocation with a lock-up period. Anchor investors receive guaranteed allocations in exchange for early commitment and price support.
attributes.references: IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles; Hong Kong SFC Listing Rules; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: is_covered_short
attributes.description: Indicates whether the investor's order includes a covered short sale component, typically associated with the greenshoe/overallotment option exercise. Relevant for stabilization and price support analysis post-IPO.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation M Rule 104; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Rule 10b-21

attributes.name: kyc_status
attributes.description: Current KYC/AML compliance status of the investor at the time of order submission. 'approved' indicates KYC checks passed; 'pending' indicates checks in progress; 'failed' indicates KYC not satisfied (order cannot be filled); 'exempt' indicates regulatory exemption applies. Mandatory for AML compliance under BSA and FATCA.
attributes.references: BSA; FATCA; FinCEN CDD Rule; FINRA Rule 3310; OCC AML Guidelines

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this investor order record, including status changes, order amendments, or allocation updates. Supports audit trail and change tracking requirements.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-3; FINRA Rule 4511; SOX Section 802

attributes.name: lock_up_period_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days the investor is contractually restricted from selling the allocated securities following the deal closing date. Applicable primarily to anchor and cornerstone investors. Zero or null if no lock-up applies.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 144; FINRA Rule 5110; IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles

attributes.name: order_amendment_count
attributes.description: Number of times the investor has amended this order during the bookbuilding period (e.g., size increases, price limit changes). Tracks investor conviction and demand evolution. Used for bookbuilding analytics and investor behavior analysis.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-3; MiFID II Article 25

attributes.name: order_channel
attributes.description: The channel through which the investor submitted the order to the bookrunner. 'electronic' covers order management system portals; 'voice' covers telephone orders; 'email' covers written email instructions; 'roadshow' covers orders placed during investor roadshow meetings; 'bloomberg' covers Bloomberg order management system submissions.
attributes.references: MiFID II Article 25; FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Rule 17a-3

attributes.name: order_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the investor order is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for FX conversion and cross-border deal management.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; ISDA; MiFID II; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: order_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the investor submitted the order during the bookbuilding period. Used for day-level reporting and analysis of demand build-up over the bookbuilding timeline.

attributes.name: order_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing additional instructions, conditions, or commentary provided by the investor or the sales coverage team regarding this order. May include special allocation requests, investment rationale, or bookrunner observations.

attributes.name: order_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this investor order, used for communication between the bookrunner and the investor during the bookbuilding process. Corresponds to the order ticket number in the Trading and Order Management System (e.g., Murex/Calypso).

attributes.name: order_size
attributes.description: The total number of shares (for ECM) or face value amount (for DCM) that the investor has requested in this order. Represents the gross demand submitted by the investor before any allocation decision.
attributes.references: IOSCO Principles for IPO Bookbuilding; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the investor order within the bookbuilding process. 'active' indicates the order is live in the book; 'filled' indicates full allocation received; 'partially_filled' indicates partial allocation; 'cancelled' indicates investor withdrew the order; 'expired' indicates the order lapsed at book close.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Regulation M; IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles

attributes.name: order_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone) at which the investor submitted the order to the bookrunner. This is the principal real-world business event timestamp for the order, critical for time-priority allocation and regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 17a-3; FINRA Rule 4511; MiFID II Article 25

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the investor order by pricing instruction: 'strike' (accept final IPO/deal price), 'limit' (maximum price the investor will pay), 'step' (tiered quantity at different price levels), 'capped' (maximum size cap), 'uncapped' (no size restriction). Drives bookrunner pricing and allocation logic.
attributes.references: IOSCO Principles for IPO Bookbuilding; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: price_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the price limit is expressed. May differ from order_currency in cross-border transactions where the security is priced in a different currency than the order denomination.

attributes.name: price_limit
attributes.description: The maximum price per share or per unit that the investor is willing to pay for a limit order. Null for strike orders where the investor accepts the final deal price. Used by the bookrunner to determine price sensitivity and construct the demand curve.
attributes.references: IOSCO Bookbuilding Principles; FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation M

attributes.name: regulatory_category
attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the investor order under applicable securities law. 'qib' = Qualified Institutional Buyer under SEC Rule 144A; 'reg_s' = offshore investor under SEC Regulation S; 'retail' = retail investor under applicable prospectus rules; 'employee' = employee share plan participant; 'directed' = directed share program recipient.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 144A; SEC Regulation S; FINRA Rule 5110; EU Prospectus Regulation

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational system of record from which this investor order was originated or captured. Supports data lineage and ETL audit trail in the Databricks Silver Layer. Typical sources include Murex, Calypso, iPreo (bookbuilding platform), Dealogic, Bloomberg OMS, or manual entry.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS 239 Data Lineage Principles

attributes.name: step_price_1
attributes.description: First price level for a step order, representing the price at which the investor commits to the quantity specified in step_size_1. Applicable only for order_type = 'step'. Null for non-step orders.

attributes.name: step_price_2
attributes.description: Second price level for a step order, representing the price at which the investor commits to the quantity specified in step_size_2. Null for non-step orders or step orders with only one tier.

attributes.name: step_size_1
attributes.description: Quantity (shares or face value) the investor will take at step_price_1 in a step order. Represents the first tier of a tiered demand schedule. Null for non-step orders.

attributes.name: step_size_2
attributes.description: Quantity (shares or face value) the investor will take at step_price_2 in a step order. Represents the second tier of a tiered demand schedule. Null for non-step orders.

products.name: tombstone
products.description: Master record for deal tombstones — the official commemorative records of completed investment banking transactions — and all associated league table credit claims. Captures transaction name, deal type, deal value, closing date, client name, banks role, co-advisors, and for each league table submission: provider (Dealogic, Bloomberg, Refinitiv), product category (M&A, ECM, DCM, Loans), credit amount, credit methodology, submission date, accepted credit, ranking period, dispute status, and publication status. Used for league table submissions, competitive positioning analysis, market share tracking, marketing materials, and deal track record management.

attributes.name: tombstone_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the tombstone record representing a completed investment banking transaction commemorative record.

attributes.name: capital_markets_offering_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.offering. Business justification: Tombstones for capital markets transactions should reference the specific offering. Not all tombstones are for offerings (M&A tombstones exist), so this FK is nullable. When tombstone commemorates a c

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent deal or mandate record in the investment banking deal pipeline from which this tombstone was generated.
attributes.references: Internal Investment Banking Deal Management Standard

attributes.name: deal_value_local_currency_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Deal Value Local Currency Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: Local currency required for tombstone publication, league table credit calculation, and deal value reporting in both local and USD terms.

attributes.name: industry_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.industry_code. Business justification: Industry sector required for sector-specific league table rankings, industry expertise demonstration, and tombstone publication with sector classification.

attributes.name: instrument_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to security.instrument. Business justification: Tombstones commemorate deals that create securities. Links tombstone to instrument for deal term verification (size, pricing) against instrument master data, league table dispute resolution, and marke

attributes.name: investment_mandate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to investment.mandate. Business justification: Tombstones commemorate completed deals that had formal mandate agreements. tombstone.mandate_reference (STRING) should be replaced with FK to mandate.mandate_id to enable retrieval of full mandate det

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: League table credits and tombstone publications must be attributed to the specific legal entity that executed the transaction for regulatory reporting (MiFID II transaction reporting), marketing compl

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary client (issuer, acquirer, or borrower) for whom the investment banking transaction was executed.

attributes.name: publication_channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.channel. Business justification: Tombstone publication and client approval occurs through specific channels (email via digital, physical presentation at branch, RM delivery). Marketing and compliance teams track publication channel f

attributes.name: accepted_credit_amount_usd
attributes.description: The USD credit amount formally accepted by the league table provider after review and any dispute resolution. May differ from the claimed credit_amount_usd if the provider applies a different methodology or partially accepts the submission.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: advisory_fee_usd
attributes.description: Total advisory or underwriting fee earned by the bank on the transaction, expressed in USD. Used for revenue recognition, profitability analysis, and fee benchmarking. Classified as confidential as it represents commercially sensitive deal economics.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers; IFRS 15; SEC Regulation S-K; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 302

attributes.name: announcement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investment banking transaction was publicly announced to the market, as reported to regulators and disclosed in press releases.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation FD; FINRA Rule 5250; FSB Disclosure Standards

attributes.name: bank_role
attributes.description: The role of the bank in the transaction as it appears on the tombstone and is used for league table credit assignment. Determines the credit methodology applied (e.g., full credit for Sole Advisor, pro-rata for Joint Bookrunner). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Sole Advisor|Joint Advisor|Lead Manager|Joint Bookrunner|Co-Manager|Arranger|Underwriter|Syndication Agent|Administrative Agent — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: bookrunner_allocation_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total deal allocated to this bank as bookrunner, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 33.3333 for one-third share). Used in bookrunner credit methodology to calculate the bank's proportional league table credit amount.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: client_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the primary client (issuer, acquirer, target, or borrower) as it appears on the tombstone advertisement and in league table submissions.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 2210; KYC (Know Your Customer) Standards

attributes.name: closing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the investment banking transaction was legally completed and all conditions precedent were satisfied. This is the primary business event date used for league table credit assignment and tombstone publication.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 1.01; FINRA; FSB Transaction Reporting Standards

attributes.name: co_advisor_names
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of co-advisors, co-managers, or joint bookrunners participating in the transaction alongside the bank. Used for competitive intelligence, league table credit sharing analysis, and tombstone advertisement content.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: coverage_banker_name
attributes.description: Full name of the senior investment banker or managing director responsible for the client relationship and transaction execution. Used for deal attribution, performance management, and pitch book preparation.
attributes.references: Internal HR and Performance Management Policy; FINRA Registration Requirements

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the tombstone record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides audit trail for record creation and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 302 and 404; GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: credit_amount_usd
attributes.description: The USD dollar amount of league table credit claimed by the bank for this transaction submission. Calculated based on the credit methodology (e.g., full deal value for sole advisor, pro-rata share for joint bookrunners). This is the primary metric used to determine league table rankings.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: credit_methodology
attributes.description: The credit allocation methodology applied to calculate the bank's league table credit amount. 'Full Credit' = 100% of deal value; 'Pro-Rata' = deal value divided equally among all bookrunners; 'Equal Credit' = each bookrunner receives full deal value credit; 'Bookrunner Credit' = credit based on bookrunner allocation percentage.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: deal_value_local
attributes.description: Total transaction value expressed in the original deal currency (local currency) before conversion to USD. Used for regional league table submissions and local market reporting.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: deal_value_usd
attributes.description: Total transaction value in US dollars as reported for league table credit purposes. For M&A, this is the enterprise value or equity value of the target. For ECM/DCM, this is the total proceeds raised. For syndicated loans, this is the total facility size. Used as the primary monetary measure for competitive positioning and market share analysis.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K; FINRA Rule 5110; Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: Narrative description of the reason for the league table credit dispute, including the basis of the challenge (e.g., incorrect role classification, deal value discrepancy, closing date eligibility, credit methodology disagreement).
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Dispute Resolution Guidelines; Bloomberg League Table Dispute Resolution Guidelines

attributes.name: dispute_status
attributes.description: Status of any dispute raised against the league table credit submission. 'no_dispute' = credit accepted without challenge; 'disputed' = credit challenged by a competitor or the provider; 'under_review' = provider is reviewing the dispute; 'resolved' = dispute settled; 'rejected' = credit claim rejected by provider.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Dispute Resolution Guidelines; Bloomberg League Table Dispute Resolution Guidelines; Refinitiv League Table Dispute Resolution Guidelines

attributes.name: fee_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the advisory fee was contractually agreed and invoiced (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). May differ from deal_currency for cross-border transactions.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FASB ASC 606; IFRS 15

attributes.name: fx_rate_to_usd
attributes.description: Exchange rate applied to convert the deal value from local currency to USD at the time of closing, used for standardized league table credit calculations across currencies.
attributes.references: BIS FX Standards; Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology

attributes.name: is_cross_border
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction involves parties from different countries (True) or is a domestic transaction (False). Cross-border transactions may qualify for separate geographic league table categories and require additional regulatory disclosures.
attributes.references: Dealogic Cross-Border League Table Methodology; FINRA; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: is_tombstone_client_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client has formally approved the tombstone advertisement content and publication (True) or approval is still pending (False). Client approval is required before tombstone publication per standard investment banking practice and FINRA communications rules.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210 — Communications with the Public; Internal Marketing Compliance Policy

attributes.name: league_table_product_category
attributes.description: Product category under which the transaction is submitted for league table credit. M&A = Mergers and Acquisitions advisory; ECM = Equity Capital Markets; DCM = Debt Capital Markets; Loans = Syndicated Lending. A single transaction may be submitted under multiple categories.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology; FINRA

attributes.name: league_table_provider
attributes.description: Name of the league table data provider to which this credit submission is made. Each provider has distinct credit methodologies and product category definitions. Dealogic, Bloomberg, and Refinitiv (LSEG) are the primary providers used for investment banking competitive positioning.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv (LSEG) League Table Methodology

attributes.name: lob_code
attributes.description: Internal code identifying the Line of Business (LOB) within investment banking that originated and executed the transaction (e.g., 'IBD-MA' for M&A Advisory, 'IBD-ECM' for Equity Capital Markets, 'IBD-DCM' for Debt Capital Markets, 'IBD-LF' for Leveraged Finance).
attributes.references: Internal LOB Taxonomy; CCAR (Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review) LOB Reporting; DFAST (Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing) Reporting

attributes.name: number_of_co_advisors
attributes.description: Total count of co-advisors or joint bookrunners on the transaction. Used to determine pro-rata league table credit allocation methodology when credit is shared equally among all bookrunners.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: publication_date
attributes.description: Date on which the tombstone advertisement was formally published in marketing materials, pitch books, or public media. Used for deal track record management and marketing compliance.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210 — Communications with the Public; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: publication_status
attributes.description: Current publication lifecycle status of the tombstone advertisement. 'draft' = tombstone content being prepared; 'approved' = client and internal sign-off obtained; 'published' = tombstone publicly released in marketing materials; 'suppressed' = publication withheld at client request; 'archived' = historical record retained for deal track record.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210 — Communications with the Public; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Marketing Compliance Policy

attributes.name: ranking_period
attributes.description: The calendar period for which the league table credit is claimed and ranked (e.g., 'Q1 2024', 'H1 2024', 'FY 2024', 'YTD 2024'). Determines which league table publication the credit will appear in.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: ranking_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the league table ranking period for which this credit submission applies. The transaction closing date must fall within the ranking period start and end dates to be eligible for credit.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: ranking_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the league table ranking period for which this credit submission applies. Used to determine eligibility of the transaction closing date within the ranking window.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Methodology; Refinitiv League Table Methodology

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the league table credit claim was submitted to the provider (Dealogic, Bloomberg, or Refinitiv) for inclusion in the ranking period.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Submission Guidelines; Bloomberg League Table Submission Guidelines; Refinitiv League Table Submission Guidelines

attributes.name: target_company_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the target company in M&A transactions, or the issuer in ECM/DCM transactions. Distinct from client_name which represents the bank's primary client (e.g., the acquirer). Null for transactions where there is no distinct target entity.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation M-A; FINRA Rule 5250; M&A Transaction Disclosure Standards

attributes.name: target_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the target company's or issuer's country of incorporation or primary operations. Used for geographic league table submissions (e.g., EMEA M&A, Asia-Pacific ECM) and cross-border transaction analysis.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3 Country Codes; Dealogic Geographic League Table Methodology

attributes.name: tombstone_description
attributes.description: Full narrative text of the tombstone advertisement as approved for publication, describing the transaction, the bank's role, and the deal highlights. Used in pitch books, marketing materials, and deal track record databases.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210 — Communications with the Public; SEC Regulation S-K; Internal Marketing Compliance Policy

attributes.name: transaction_name
attributes.description: Official marketing name or title of the completed investment banking transaction as it appears on the tombstone advertisement (e.g., 'Acquisition of XYZ Corp by ABC Inc').
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210 — Communications with the Public; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the tombstone record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, data lineage, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 302 and 404; GDPR Article 5 — Data Integrity; Internal Data Governance Policy

products.name: coverage_assignment
products.description: Master entity tracking the assignment of investment banking coverage bankers to client relationships and industry sectors. Records coverage banker, client entity, sector (TMT, healthcare, energy, financials, industrials), geography, coverage role (primary, secondary, sector specialist), assignment dates, and deal origination attribution. Supports banker accountability, client relationship management, and revenue attribution for the IB division.
products.reference: IB Coverage Model / Client Coverage Assignment

attributes.name: coverage_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each investment banking coverage assignment record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: channel_relationship_manager_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.relationship_manager. Business justification: Coverage assignments in investment banking ARE relationship manager assignments - linking investment banker (employee) to client (party) for revenue attribution, client interaction tracking, and cross

attributes.name: client_mandate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to wealth.client_mandate. Business justification: Coverage bankers in investment banking coordinate with wealth management mandates for the same client, ensuring holistic relationship management. Real business process: cross-LOB client coverage coord

attributes.name: counterparty_rating_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.counterparty_rating. Business justification: Coverage assignments require current counterparty ratings for relationship management, credit decision authority, and client tier classification. Essential for determining banker approval limits and e

attributes.name: geographic_region_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.geographic_region. Business justification: Geographic region required for regional coverage team structure, P&L attribution, and management reporting of client coverage by region.

attributes.name: industry_code_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the industry sector classification (e.g., TMT, Healthcare, Energy, Financials, Industrials) under which this coverage assignment is organized. Links to the sector reference product.

attributes.name: kyc_review_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.kyc_review. Business justification: Coverage bankers responsible for ensuring client KYC is current. Assignment triggers KYC review cycle based on client tier, risk rating, and regulatory requirements. Compliance tracks which coverage a

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the corporate or institutional client entity being covered. Links to the client/counterparty master record used for KYC and CRM purposes.

attributes.name: primary_coverage_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the investment banking coverage banker (relationship manager or sector specialist) assigned to the client. Links to the banker/employee master record.

attributes.name: tertiary_coverage_approved_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the senior officer (e.g., Head of Coverage, Group Head) who approved this coverage assignment. Supports governance, audit trail, and segregation of duties requirements under SOX.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal IB Governance Policy

attributes.name: universe_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audit.audit_universe. Business justification: Coverage assignments (banker-client relationships) are auditable entities for conflict management, KYC compliance, relationship governance, and coverage model effectiveness. Tracked in audit universe

attributes.name: aml_risk_rating
attributes.description: The Anti-Money Laundering (AML) risk rating assigned to the client entity for this coverage relationship. Determines the frequency and depth of enhanced due diligence (EDD) reviews required. Sourced from the AML/Financial Crime system.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA; FATF Recommendations; OCC AML Guidelines; NICE Actimize / Oracle Financial Crime

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the coverage assignment was formally approved by the designated approving officer. Part of the governance audit trail for IB coverage decisions.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal IB Governance Policy

attributes.name: assignment_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the coverage assignment, used in pitch books, mandate letters, and CRM systems to uniquely reference this banker-client relationship.

attributes.name: assignment_date
attributes.description: The business event date on which the coverage assignment decision was formally made and recorded, which may differ from the effective_from_date if there is a future-dated assignment.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the coverage assignment. Active indicates the banker is currently covering the client; transferred indicates ownership has moved to another banker; terminated indicates the relationship has ended.

attributes.name: banker_title
attributes.description: The seniority title of the assigned coverage banker at the time of assignment (e.g., Analyst, Associate, Vice President, Director, Managing Director). Relevant for deal origination credit allocation and client relationship governance.
attributes.references: Internal HR / IB Seniority Framework; FINRA Rule 1210

attributes.name: client_tier
attributes.description: Strategic tier classification of the client within the IB coverage model, reflecting the client's revenue potential and strategic importance to the bank (e.g., Tier 1 = top global corporates, Tier 3 = emerging/developing relationships).

attributes.name: coverage_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes recorded by the coverage banker or coverage manager regarding the client relationship, strategic priorities, or special circumstances of this assignment. Contains sensitive business development information.

attributes.name: coverage_office
attributes.description: The physical office or booking center from which the coverage banker operates (e.g., New York, London, Hong Kong). Used for regulatory jurisdiction assignment and internal cost allocation.
attributes.references: Internal IB Geographic Coverage Model; OCC; PRA

attributes.name: coverage_role
attributes.description: The functional role of the assigned banker in the client coverage model. Primary bankers own the overall relationship; secondary bankers provide support; sector and product specialists contribute domain expertise. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: primary|secondary|sector_specialist|product_specialist|co_coverage|advisory — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Internal IB Coverage Policy; FINRA Rule 2010

attributes.name: coverage_team_name
attributes.description: Name of the investment banking coverage team or group responsible for this assignment (e.g., 'Global TMT Coverage', 'Healthcare Investment Banking'). Supports team-level performance reporting and deal pipeline management.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The date on which the coverage assignment became effective and the banker formally assumed responsibility for the client relationship. Used for revenue attribution and accountability tracking.
attributes.references: Internal IB Coverage Policy; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: effective_until_date
attributes.description: The date on which the coverage assignment is scheduled to end or was terminated. Null for open-ended assignments. Used for historical coverage analysis and transition planning.

attributes.name: geography_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the primary country of the client entity for this coverage assignment. Used for regulatory jurisdiction mapping and cross-border compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; FATCA; CRS (Common Reporting Standard)

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this coverage assignment is currently active. Derived from assignment_status but maintained as an explicit field to support efficient filtering in analytics queries and reporting dashboards without requiring status string comparisons.

attributes.name: is_lead_coverage
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this banker is the designated lead coverage officer for the client relationship. Only one banker per client should have this flag set to True at any given time. Drives primary accountability and escalation routing.

attributes.name: is_sector_specialist
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the assigned banker is acting in a sector specialist capacity rather than a generalist relationship management role. Sector specialists provide deep industry expertise and are typically engaged on specific transaction types.

attributes.name: kyc_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the client's KYC documentation expires and must be renewed. Coverage bankers are alerted prior to this date to initiate KYC refresh. Supports AML compliance and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA; FATCA; OCC KYC Guidelines; FATF Recommendations

attributes.name: kyc_status
attributes.description: Current Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance status for the client entity under this coverage assignment. Coverage bankers are responsible for ensuring KYC is current before engaging in transactions. Drives AML and regulatory compliance workflows.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA (Bank Secrecy Act); FATCA; CRS; OCC KYC Guidelines; FATF Recommendations

attributes.name: last_client_interaction_date
attributes.description: The most recent date on which the coverage banker had a documented interaction with the client (meeting, call, pitch presentation). Used for CRM activity monitoring and relationship health assessment.

attributes.name: lob_name
attributes.description: The investment banking Line of Business (LOB) associated with this coverage assignment, indicating the primary product focus area (e.g., M&A Advisory, Equity Capital Markets (ECM), Debt Capital Markets (DCM), Leveraged Finance, Syndicated Lending). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: M&A_advisory|ECM|DCM|leveraged_finance|syndicated_lending|restructuring|corporate_finance — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Internal IB LOB Taxonomy; SEC; FINRA

attributes.name: mandate_count
attributes.description: The number of active IB mandates (M&A, IPO, DCM, etc.) currently associated with this coverage assignment at the time of record. Provides a snapshot of deal pipeline depth for this banker-client relationship.
attributes.references: Internal IB Deal Pipeline Management Policy

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this coverage assignment, at which point the assignment may be renewed, transferred, or terminated. Supports coverage governance and banker accountability cycles.

attributes.name: origination_credit_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of deal origination credit allocated to this banker for revenue attribution purposes. Multiple bankers may share credit across a single client relationship; percentages across all active assignments for a client should sum to 100. Used in RAROC and banker performance measurement.
attributes.references: Internal IB Revenue Attribution Policy; FINRA

attributes.name: pitch_book_count
attributes.description: The number of pitch books or marketing presentations delivered to this client under this coverage assignment. Tracks business development activity intensity and supports pipeline conversion analysis.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this coverage assignment record was first created in the data platform. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this coverage assignment record was last modified in the data platform. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, SCD processing, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: relationship_since_date
attributes.description: The date on which the bank first established a formal investment banking relationship with this client entity. Distinct from the coverage assignment effective date; reflects the longevity of the overall client relationship.
attributes.references: Internal CRM Policy; KYC Onboarding Records

attributes.name: revenue_attribution_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of total client-generated IB revenue attributed to this specific coverage assignment. Distinct from origination_credit_pct as it may reflect ongoing relationship management credit rather than deal origination credit alone.
attributes.references: Internal IB Revenue Attribution Policy; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: sector_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the industry sector under which this coverage assignment is classified (e.g., TMT, Healthcare, Energy, Financials, Industrials). Aligns with GICS sector taxonomy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: TMT|healthcare|energy|financials|industrials|consumer|real_estate|utilities|materials — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GICS (Global Industry Classification Standard) / MSCI; FINRA

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this coverage assignment record was sourced (e.g., CRM platform, IB deal management system). Supports data lineage and ETL reconciliation in the lakehouse.

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: The native primary key or record identifier of this coverage assignment in the originating operational system of record. Enables traceability from the Silver Layer back to the source system for audit and reconciliation.

attributes.name: sub_sector_name
attributes.description: More granular sub-sector classification within the primary sector (e.g., within TMT: Software, Semiconductors, Media; within Healthcare: Pharma, MedTech, Biotech). Supports specialist banker routing and deal origination attribution.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the coverage assignment was terminated or transferred. Populated only when assignment_status is terminated or transferred. Distinct from effective_until_date which may be a planned end date.

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Reason code explaining why the coverage assignment was terminated or transferred. Supports workforce planning, client retention analysis, and coverage continuity management.

products.name: deal_participant
products.description: Association entity capturing all parties involved in an investment banking deal — including the client, target company, acquirer, co-advisors, legal counsel, auditors, regulators, and other deal counterparties. Records participant role, institution name, engagement start date, engagement end date, and conflict check status. Enables deal team management and conflict of interest screening.

attributes.name: deal_participant_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each deal participant record in the investment banking deal association entity. Primary key for the deal_participant table.

attributes.name: counterparty_rating_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.counterparty_rating. Business justification: Deal participants require credit ratings for conflict checks, engagement decisions, syndicate formation, and fee arrangement structuring. Standard practice to assess participant creditworthiness befor

attributes.name: deal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investment banking deal (M&A, IPO, DCF, debt/equity capital markets, syndicated lending) to which this participant is associated.

attributes.name: kyc_review_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.kyc_review. Business justification: Each deal participant requires KYC due diligence before engagement. Compliance tracks which participant record triggered or is associated with each KYC review cycle. Participant onboarding cannot proc

attributes.name: lei_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.lei_registry. Business justification: LEI code required for EMIR/Dodd-Frank trade reporting, counterparty due diligence, and legal entity identification in syndication and capital markets transactions.

attributes.name: primary_deal_party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the institution or counterparty entity representing the participating organization (e.g., client, co-advisor, legal counsel, auditor, regulator).

attributes.name: sanctions_screening_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.sanctions_screening_event. Business justification: All deal counterparties, advisors, and participants must be screened against OFAC/sanctions lists before engagement. Regulatory requirement pre-mandate execution. Screening event records match status,

attributes.name: agreed_fee_amount
attributes.description: Contractually agreed fee amount payable to or by this participant for their role in the deal, expressed in the deal currency. For success fees, this represents the agreed percentage or fixed amount at deal close.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; ASC 606; IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

attributes.name: bic_code
attributes.description: SWIFT Bank Identifier Code (BIC) of the participating institution, used for SWIFT messaging, payment settlement, and cross-border transaction identification in investment banking deal communications.
attributes.references: ISO 9362; SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication); BIC Standard

attributes.name: conflict_check_date
attributes.description: Date on which the conflict of interest screening was last performed or updated for this participant. Used to ensure checks are current and within required review cycles.
attributes.references: OCC Conflict of Interest Guidelines; FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 17j-1

attributes.name: conflict_check_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting the outcome of the conflict of interest review, including nature of any identified conflict, waiver rationale, or escalation details. Maintained for regulatory audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: OCC Conflict of Interest Guidelines; FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 17j-1

attributes.name: conflict_check_status
attributes.description: Status of the conflict of interest screening performed for this participant relative to the deal. Values: pending (check not yet initiated), cleared (no conflict found), conflict_identified (potential conflict detected), waived (conflict acknowledged and waived with appropriate approvals), escalated (referred to compliance committee).
attributes.references: OCC Conflict of Interest Guidelines; FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 17j-1; FSB Principles for Sound Compensation Practices

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this deal participant record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides audit trail for record origination.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 404; FINRA Rule 4511; Internal Audit Standard

attributes.name: deal_team_lead
attributes.description: Indicates whether this participant is designated as the lead institution or lead advisor for their role in the deal (e.g., lead left bookrunner, lead financial advisor). True = lead; False = co-participant or supporting role.
attributes.references: Investment Banking Deal Hierarchy Standard; FINRA Rule 5110

attributes.name: engagement_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the participant's engagement in the deal formally concluded, either through deal close, withdrawal, termination, or completion of advisory mandate. Null if engagement is ongoing.

attributes.name: engagement_letter_date
attributes.description: Date on which the formal engagement letter was signed between the bank and this participant, establishing the legal basis for the advisory or service relationship within the deal.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; Investment Banking Engagement Protocol

attributes.name: engagement_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the participant formally commenced engagement in the deal, typically aligned with the execution of a mandate letter, engagement letter, or non-disclosure agreement (NDA).

attributes.name: fee_arrangement_type
attributes.description: Type of fee arrangement agreed with this participant: retainer (periodic fixed fee), success_fee (contingent on deal close), hourly (time-based billing), fixed (lump sum), or no_fee (pro bono or regulatory participant). Drives revenue recognition and deal economics.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: fee_basis_points
attributes.description: Fee expressed in basis points (BPS) as a proportion of the total deal value, applicable for success fees and underwriting fees in capital markets transactions. One basis point equals 0.01%.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Investment Banking Fee Standard; BPS (Basis Points) Convention

attributes.name: fee_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the agreed fee amount is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency deal fee tracking and FX (Foreign Exchange) conversion.

attributes.name: information_barrier_group
attributes.description: Identifier of the information barrier (Chinese Wall) group to which this participant has been assigned, controlling access to material non-public information (MNPI) about the deal. Used for insider trading prevention and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-5; FINRA Rule 5280; MAR (Market Abuse Regulation); OCC Information Barrier Guidelines

attributes.name: institution_type
attributes.description: Classification of the type of institution participating in the deal: investment_bank, commercial_bank, law_firm, accounting_firm, regulator, private_equity, or hedge_fund. Supports deal team composition analysis and conflict screening. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: investment_bank|commercial_bank|law_firm|accounting_firm|regulator|private_equity|hedge_fund — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 4511; SEC Regulation S-K; Investment Banking Deal Taxonomy

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the primary legal jurisdiction under which the participating institution is incorporated or regulated. Used for cross-border deal structuring and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; FATCA; CRS (Common Reporting Standard); Basel Committee on Banking Supervision

attributes.name: kyc_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent KYC (Know Your Customer) review was completed for this participant. Used to track review currency and trigger periodic refresh cycles per AML compliance requirements.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA; OCC KYC Guidelines; FATF Recommendations; FATCA

attributes.name: kyc_status
attributes.description: Current KYC (Know Your Customer) due diligence status for the participating institution. Ensures AML (Anti-Money Laundering) and BSA (Bank Secrecy Act) compliance before the institution is permitted to participate in deal activities.
attributes.references: FinCEN BSA (Bank Secrecy Act); FATCA; CRS (Common Reporting Standard); OCC KYC Guidelines; FATF Recommendations

attributes.name: league_table_credit
attributes.description: Indicates whether this participant is eligible to receive league table credit for this deal in industry rankings (e.g., Bloomberg, Dealogic, Thomson Reuters). True = eligible for credit; False = excluded from league table attribution.
attributes.references: Dealogic League Table Methodology; Bloomberg League Table Rules; Thomson Reuters Investment Banking Rankings

attributes.name: mandate_letter_ref
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the mandate letter or engagement letter governing this participant's involvement in the deal. Links to the formal contractual document establishing scope, fees, and obligations.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; SEC Regulation S-K; Investment Banking Mandate Management Standard

attributes.name: nda_executed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) has been executed with this participant prior to sharing confidential deal information. True = NDA in place; False = NDA not yet executed.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation FD; FINRA Rule 4511; Investment Banking Deal Protocol

attributes.name: nda_execution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) was formally executed between the bank and this deal participant. Null if NDA has not been executed.

attributes.name: participant_category
attributes.description: High-level classification grouping participant roles into: principal (client, target, acquirer), advisor (financial advisor, legal counsel, auditor, co-advisor), regulatory (regulator, compliance body), or support (escrow agent, trustee, paying agent).
attributes.references: Investment Banking Deal Taxonomy; SEC Regulation S-K

attributes.name: participant_ref_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this participant engagement within the deal, used in mandate letters, pitch books, and tombstone records for cross-system identification.
attributes.references: Investment Banking Operations Standard; FINRA Rule 4511

attributes.name: participant_role
attributes.description: Functional role of the participant in the investment banking deal. Common roles include: client, target, acquirer, co-advisor, financial advisor, legal counsel, auditor, underwriter, syndicate member, regulator, escrow agent, trustee, fairness opinion provider. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: client|target|acquirer|co_advisor|financial_advisor|legal_counsel|auditor|underwriter|syndicate_member|regulator|escrow_agent|trustee|fairness_opinion_provider — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Regulation M; ISDA Master Agreement

attributes.name: participant_side
attributes.description: Indicates which side of the transaction the participant represents: buy_side (acquirer/investor), sell_side (target/issuer), neutral (independent advisor, auditor, fairness opinion), or regulatory (governing body). Critical for conflict of interest screening.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5150; SEC Rule 10b-5; OCC Conflict of Interest Guidelines

attributes.name: participant_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the participant's engagement in the deal: active (currently engaged), withdrawn (voluntarily exited), terminated (engagement ended by counterparty), completed (deal closed with participant fulfilling role), suspended (engagement paused pending resolution).
attributes.references: Investment Banking Lifecycle Management Standard; FINRA Rule 4511

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: Business email address of the primary contact person at the participating institution. Used for deal communications, document distribution, and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; CCPA; Investment Banking Deal Management Standard

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: Full name of the primary contact person at the participating institution responsible for deal communications and execution. Captured for deal team management and correspondence tracking.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; CCPA; Investment Banking Deal Management Standard

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: Direct phone number of the primary contact person at the participating institution for deal-related communications.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this participant's involvement in the deal requires specific regulatory approval (e.g., antitrust clearance, CFIUS review, FCA approval). True = regulatory approval required; False = no specific approval required.
attributes.references: SEC Merger Review; DOJ/FTC Antitrust Guidelines; CFIUS; FCA; PRA; EBA

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_status
attributes.description: Current status of any required regulatory approval for this participant's deal involvement: not_required, pending (application submitted), approved (clearance received), rejected (approval denied), or conditional (approved with conditions).
attributes.references: SEC Merger Review; DOJ/FTC Antitrust Guidelines; CFIUS; FCA; PRA; EBA; BCBS

attributes.name: syndicate_rank
attributes.description: Numeric ranking of this participant within the deal syndicate or advisory group, where 1 indicates the lead/senior position. Used for tombstone ordering, fee allocation, and league table credit attribution in capital markets transactions.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 5110; Investment Banking Syndicate Management Standard; Dealogic League Table Methodology

attributes.name: tombstone_credit_line
attributes.description: The exact credit line text to be used for this participant in the deal tombstone advertisement, specifying the institution name and role as it should appear in the published announcement.
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210; Investment Banking Tombstone Convention

attributes.name: tombstone_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this participant's involvement should be included in the deal tombstone advertisement published upon deal completion. True = eligible for tombstone credit; False = excluded (e.g., confidential participants, regulatory bodies).
attributes.references: FINRA Rule 2210; SEC Regulation S-K; Investment Banking Tombstone Convention

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this deal participant record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, data lineage, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 404; FINRA Rule 4511; Internal Audit Standard

attributes.name: wall_cross_date
attributes.description: Date on which this participant was formally 'wall-crossed' — i.e., brought over the information barrier and made aware of material non-public information (MNPI) about the deal. Critical for insider trading compliance and information barrier management.
attributes.references: SEC Rule 10b-5; FINRA Rule 5280; MAR (Market Abuse Regulation); OCC Information Barrier Guidelines

attributes.name: withdrawal_reason
attributes.description: Reason for the participant's withdrawal or termination from the deal, if applicable. Captures business rationale such as conflict of interest, regulatory objection, commercial disagreement, or deal collapse. Populated only when participant_status is withdrawn or terminated.
attributes.references: Investment Banking Deal Management Standard; FINRA Rule 4511

The primary ECM/DCM transaction record.

products.name: deal_participation
products.description: This association product represents the participation relationship between parties and investment banking deals. It captures the role, engagement timeline, conflict status, fee arrangements, and syndicate positioning for each party involved in a deal. Each record links one party to one deal with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific engagement.. Existence Justification: Investment banking deals inherently involve multiple parties in various roles (client, target, advisors, lenders, underwriters, legal counsel), and each party participates in multiple deals over time. The business actively manages deal participation as a distinct operational entity, tracking role-specific data such as engagement dates, conflict status, NDA execution, fee arrangements, and syndicate positioning that cannot be stored on either party or deal alone.

products.name: deal_broker_participation
products.description: This association product represents the participation relationship between brokers and investment banking deals. It captures the syndicate structure for each deal, recording which brokers participate in what capacity (bookrunner, co-manager, selling group member), their economic share, and their syndicate ranking. Each record links one broker to one deal with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific deal participation.. Existence Justification: Investment banking deals are executed through syndicates where multiple brokers participate in different capacities (bookrunner, lead manager, co-manager, selling group). Each broker participates in multiple deals over time. The syndicate structure is an operational business entity that investment bankers actively manage during deal execution, with specific data about each broker's role, economic participation, fee allocation, and tombstone positioning that cannot be stored on either the broker or deal entity alone.

attributes.name: deal_broker_participation_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the broker participating in the deal syndicate

attributes.name: broker_role
attributes.description: The specific role the broker plays in this deal syndicate. Bookrunner leads the transaction, lead managers have significant responsibility, co-managers participate in distribution, selling group members assist with placement. Drives fee allocation and tombstone positioning.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
