attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Capital Framework; Federal Reserve CCAR Capital Ratio Projections; OCC DFAST RWA Guidance

attributes.name: scenario_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the stress scenario within the regulatory program or internal stress framework (e.g., CCAR-2024-SA, DFAST-2024-ADV, ICAAP-2024-BL). Used as the business key for cross-system referencing in AxiomSL/OneSumX.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Instructions; OCC DFAST Guidance; BCBS Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: scenario_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the macroeconomic and financial conditions assumed under the stress scenario, including the economic story, key assumptions, and the nature of the shock being modeled.
attributes.references: BCBS Stress Testing Principles (2018); Federal Reserve SR 12-7 Stress Testing Guidance

attributes.name: scenario_horizon_quarters
attributes.description: The projection horizon of the stress scenario expressed in quarters. Standard CCAR/DFAST horizon is 9 quarters (13 quarters for certain programs). Determines the length of the macroeconomic variable path and the stress run projection period.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR 9-Quarter Projection Requirement; OCC DFAST Guidance

attributes.name: scenario_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the stress scenario (e.g., '2024 CCAR Severely Adverse', '2024 DFAST Adverse', 'Internal Recession Scenario Q1-2024'). Used in regulatory submissions, board presentations, and risk reporting.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Instructions; OCC DFAST Guidance

attributes.name: scenario_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the stress scenario per regulatory and internal taxonomy. 'baseline' = expected/central economic path; 'adverse' = moderate stress; 'severely_adverse' = severe recession/crisis conditions; 'reverse_stress' = scenario designed to cause failure; 'exploratory' = ad-hoc sensitivity analysis.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Severely Adverse Scenario Definition; BCBS Stress Testing Principles; EBA Stress Test Methodology

attributes.name: scenario_source
attributes.description: The originating authority or institution that published or defined the stress scenario. 'federal_reserve' = Fed-prescribed CCAR/DFAST scenario; 'occ' = OCC-prescribed scenario; 'eba' = European Banking Authority; 'pra' = Prudential Regulation Authority; 'internal' = bank-developed scenario; 'imf' = IMF FSAP scenario; 'bis' = BIS/BCBS scenario. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: federal_reserve|occ|fdic|eba|pra|internal|imf|bis — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed); OCC; FDIC; EBA; PRA; BCBS; IMF FSAP

attributes.name: scenario_type
attributes.description: Classification of the primary risk driver modeled in the scenario. 'macroeconomic' = GDP/unemployment/inflation shocks; 'market_risk' = interest rate/FX/equity shocks; 'credit_risk' = credit spread/default rate shocks; 'liquidity' = funding/liquidity stress; 'operational' = operational risk events; 'combined' = multi-risk-factor scenario; 'idiosyncratic' = firm-specific stress. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: macroeconomic|market_risk|credit_risk|liquidity|operational|combined|idiosyncratic — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Stress Testing Principles (2018); Federal Reserve SR 12-7; FRTB Stress Scenario Requirements

attributes.name: scenario_vintage
attributes.description: The publication or reference vintage of the scenario, typically expressed as a year (e.g., '2024') or year-quarter (e.g., '2024Q1'). Identifies the cycle in which the scenario was issued by the regulator or approved internally. Critical for tracking scenario evolution across CCAR/DFAST cycles.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Annual Cycle; OCC DFAST Annual Cycle

attributes.name: short_term_rate_shock_bps
attributes.description: The shock to short-term interest rates (e.g., 3-month Treasury, Fed Funds Rate) applied under this scenario, expressed in basis points (BPS). Used in NII/NIM stress testing and ALM analysis. Positive = rate increase; negative = rate decrease.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Interest Rate Variable Definitions; BCBS Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) Standards; ALCO Framework

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this stress scenario record was sourced (e.g., 'AXIOMSL', 'ONESUMX', 'SAS_RISK', 'MOODYS_RA'). Supports data lineage tracking and ETL reconciliation in the lakehouse.
attributes.references: AxiomSL Regulatory Reporting Platform; Wolters Kluwer OneSumX; SAS Risk Management; Moody's RiskAuthority

attributes.name: unemployment_rate_shock_pct
attributes.description: The peak unemployment rate assumed under this stress scenario, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 12.50 for 12.5% peak unemployment). A primary macroeconomic driver for consumer credit loss models in CCAR/DFAST stress testing.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Macroeconomic Variable Definitions; OCC DFAST Scenario Variables

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this stress scenario record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance in the lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Audit Trail Requirements; BCBS Stress Testing Governance; Federal Reserve Data Integrity Standards

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the stress scenario, incremented each time the scenario parameters are materially revised. Version 1 = initial approved version. Supports scenario versioning, change management, and audit trail requirements under model risk governance.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7 Model Risk Management; OCC Model Risk Guidance; BCBS Stress Testing Governance

products.name: stress_test_run
products.description: Stress test execution record capturing results of a specific stress scenario applied to a portfolio or enterprise. Captures run date, scenario reference, portfolio scope, stressed capital ratios (CET1, Tier 1, Total Capital), stressed RWA, stressed ECL, stressed NII/NIM impact, LCR/NSFR impact, and regulatory submission metadata. Primary output for CCAR/DFAST regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: stress_test_run_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each stress test execution record. Primary key for the stress_test_run data product.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Stress Testing Principles; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Framework

attributes.name: alco_meeting_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.alco_meeting. Business justification: Stress test results are presented to ALCO meetings for capital action decisions, dividend policy, and balance sheet management. Regulatory requirement under Federal Reserve SR 12-7 and Dodd-Frank Act

attributes.name: currency_id
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this stress test run record (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). All stressed financial metrics are expressed in this currency.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; Federal Reserve CCAR Reporting Instructions

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: Stress test runs (CCAR/DFAST) are executed at legal entity or consolidated group level for regulatory submissions. Results must be attributed to specific legal entities for capital planning and regula

attributes.name: regulatory_exam_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_exam. Business justification: Stress test results are reviewed during CCAR/DFAST exams. Examiners validate methodology, assumptions, and capital adequacy. Banks track which stress test runs were reviewed in each exam for documenta

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Reference to the stress scenario definition applied in this run, identifying the macroeconomic or idiosyncratic shock parameters (e.g., severely adverse, adverse, baseline).
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Scenario Definitions; DFAST Macroeconomic Scenarios

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the stress test results were formally approved by the designated governance authority. Null if pending approval.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Federal Reserve CCAR Capital Plan Rule

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the senior risk officer or governance body (e.g., ALCO, CRO) that approved the stress test results prior to regulatory submission or management reporting.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Capital Plan Rule; BCBS Corporate Governance Principles for Banks

attributes.name: as_of_date
attributes.description: The reference balance sheet date from which the stress test projects forward. All starting positions (exposures, capital, liquidity) are measured as of this date.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Capital Plan Rule; DFAST Reporting Instructions

attributes.name: capital_action_restriction_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this stress test result triggered restrictions on capital distributions (dividends, share buybacks) under the stress capital buffer framework or CCAR objection process.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve Stress Capital Buffer Rule (Regulation Y); CCAR Capital Plan Rule

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this stress test run record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Basel III Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: executed_by
attributes.description: The name or system identifier of the team, user, or automated process that initiated and executed this stress test run. Used for governance and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; OCC Model Risk Management Guidance (SR 11-7)

attributes.name: irb_approach_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Internal Ratings-Based (IRB) approach was used for credit risk RWA calculation in this stress test run. If False, the Standardized Approach (SA) was applied.
attributes.references: Basel III IRB Framework (BCBS); OCC Capital Adequacy Rules; Federal Reserve Advanced Approaches Rule

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the risk model suite (PD/LGD/EAD, market risk, liquidity models) used to generate the stress test results. Critical for model governance, backtesting, and regulatory model validation.
attributes.references: OCC Model Risk Management Guidance (SR 11-7); Federal Reserve CCAR Model Risk Standards

attributes.name: portfolio_scope_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the portfolio or sub-portfolio subjected to this stress test run (e.g., 'ENTERPRISE', 'COMMERCIAL_LENDING', 'TRADING_BOOK', 'RETAIL_MORTGAGE'). Defines the boundary of exposure included.
attributes.references: BCBS Stress Testing Principles; Federal Reserve CCAR Capital Plan Rule

attributes.name: projection_end_date
attributes.description: The final date of the stress projection horizon, calculated as as_of_date plus the stress horizon. Defines the terminal point for all stressed capital and liquidity metrics.

attributes.name: regulatory_outcome
attributes.description: The regulatory determination resulting from this stress test submission. 'no_objection' and 'pass' indicate capital plan approval; 'objection' or 'fail' require remediation. 'pending' indicates awaiting regulatory response.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Capital Plan Rule; Dodd-Frank Act Section 165(i)

attributes.name: regulatory_program
attributes.description: The regulatory or internal program under which this stress test was conducted. CCAR (Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review) and DFAST (Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing) are US Fed programs; ICAAP/ILAAP are internal capital/liquidity adequacy processes; EBA_ST and PRA_ST are European programs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CCAR|DFAST|ICAAP|ILAAP|EBA_ST|PRA_ST|INTERNAL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Rules; EBA Stress Testing Guidelines; PRA Supervisory Statement SS3/19

attributes.name: run_code
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this stress test execution, used in regulatory submissions and internal reporting (e.g., CCAR-2024-ADV-001). Unique within a submission cycle.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Instructions; Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing (DFAST) Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: run_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for qualitative commentary on this stress test run, including methodology overrides, data quality issues, management adjustments, or explanations of material deviations from prior runs.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Capital Plan Qualitative Requirements; BCBS Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: run_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the stress test execution. 'draft' indicates setup not finalized; 'in_progress' indicates computation running; 'completed' indicates results available; 'failed' indicates execution error; 'submitted' indicates filed with regulator; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a rerun.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Submission Guidelines; BCBS Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: run_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the stress test computation was initiated. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the scenario was applied to the portfolio.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Reporting; SAS Risk Management Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: run_type
attributes.description: Classification of the stress test run by its purpose. 'regulatory' is a mandated submission run; 'internal' is management-initiated; 'parallel' is a shadow run alongside regulatory; 'ad_hoc' is event-driven; 'restatement' corrects a prior submission.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Rules; BCBS Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: scenario_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the stress scenario applied (e.g., 'Fed Severely Adverse 2024', 'Internal Adverse Scenario Q3-2024', 'COVID-19 Replay'). Denormalized for reporting convenience.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Scenario Definitions; BCBS Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: scenario_type
attributes.description: Classification of the stress scenario by severity or origin. 'baseline' is the expected economic path; 'adverse' and 'severely_adverse' are Fed-prescribed CCAR/DFAST scenarios; 'internal' is bank-designed; 'reverse' identifies conditions that would cause failure; 'sensitivity' tests single-factor shocks.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Scenario Definitions; BCBS Stress Testing Principles (2018)

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record that generated this stress test run (e.g., 'SAS_RISK_MGR', 'MOODYS_RISK_AUTH', 'AXIOMSL'). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Basel III Data Quality and Aggregation Principles (BCBS 239); SOX Data Lineage Requirements

attributes.name: stress_capital_buffer_pct
attributes.description: The stress capital buffer (SCB) requirement derived from this stress test run, expressed as a percentage. Calculated as the maximum decline in CET1 ratio under the severely adverse scenario, subject to a 2.5% floor.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve Stress Capital Buffer Rule (Regulation Y, 12 CFR Part 225)

attributes.name: stress_horizon_quarters
attributes.description: The number of quarters over which the stress scenario is projected. Standard CCAR/DFAST horizon is 9 quarters; internal stress tests may use shorter or longer horizons.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Stress Testing Rules; BCBS Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: stressed_cet1_ratio
attributes.business_glossary_term: Stressed Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Capital Ratio
attributes.description: The minimum projected Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio under the stress scenario over the projection horizon, expressed as a percentage. Key regulatory output for CCAR/DFAST pass/fail determination. CET1 minimum regulatory threshold is 4.5% under Basel III.
attributes.references: Basel III CET1 Requirements (BCBS); Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Capital Adequacy Standards; OCC Capital Adequacy Rules

attributes.name: stressed_cva_amount
attributes.description: The projected Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) on OTC derivatives under the stress scenario, in reporting currency. Represents the market value of counterparty credit risk under stressed conditions.
attributes.references: Basel III CVA Framework (BCBS); ISDA CVA Standards; FRTB CVA Capital Charge

attributes.name: stressed_ecl_amount
attributes.description: Total Expected Credit Loss (ECL) projected under the stress scenario over the full horizon, in reporting currency. Represents cumulative credit impairment charges under CECL/IFRS 9 stressed conditions.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 326 CECL; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments (IASB); Federal Reserve CCAR Loan Loss Projection

attributes.name: stressed_lcr_ratio
attributes.description: The minimum projected Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) under the stress scenario, expressed as a percentage. LCR measures the bank's ability to survive a 30-day liquidity stress event. Regulatory minimum is 100% under Basel III.
attributes.references: Basel III LCR Framework (BCBS); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249); ILAAP Guidelines

attributes.name: stressed_leverage_ratio
attributes.description: The minimum projected Tier 1 leverage ratio under the stress scenario, expressed as a percentage. Calculated as Tier 1 capital divided by average total consolidated assets. Regulatory minimum is 4% for bank holding companies.
attributes.references: Basel III Leverage Ratio Framework (BCBS); Federal Reserve CCAR Capital Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: stressed_nii_impact_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Stressed Net Interest Income (NII) Impact Amount
attributes.description: The cumulative change in Net Interest Income (NII) projected under the stress scenario relative to the baseline over the horizon, in reporting currency. Negative values indicate NII compression under stress.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Pre-Provision Net Revenue (PPNR) Projections; ALCO NII Reporting Standards

attributes.name: stressed_nim_bps
attributes.business_glossary_term: Stressed Net Interest Margin (NIM) Impact (Basis Points)
attributes.description: The change in Net Interest Margin (NIM) under the stress scenario relative to baseline, expressed in basis points (BPS). Captures the spread compression effect of the stress scenario on the bank's interest-earning assets.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR PPNR Projections; ALCO ALM Reporting Standards

attributes.name: stressed_nsfr_ratio
attributes.description: The minimum projected Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) under the stress scenario, expressed as a percentage. NSFR measures the bank's stable funding relative to required stable funding over a one-year horizon. Regulatory minimum is 100% under Basel III.
attributes.references: Basel III NSFR Framework (BCBS); Federal Reserve NSFR Rule; ILAAP Guidelines

attributes.name: stressed_ppnr_amount
attributes.description: Cumulative Pre-Provision Net Revenue (PPNR) projected under the stress scenario over the full horizon, in reporting currency. PPNR is a key CCAR metric representing revenue before credit loss provisions.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST PPNR Projection Requirements

attributes.name: stressed_rwa_amount
attributes.description: Total Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) projected under the stress scenario at the end of the horizon, in reporting currency. Encompasses credit RWA, market RWA, and operational RWA under stressed conditions.
attributes.references: Basel III RWA Framework (BCBS); Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Reporting; OCC Capital Adequacy Rules

attributes.name: stressed_tier1_ratio
attributes.description: The minimum projected Tier 1 capital ratio under the stress scenario over the projection horizon, expressed as a percentage. Includes CET1 plus Additional Tier 1 instruments. Regulatory minimum is 6% under Basel III.
attributes.references: Basel III Tier 1 Capital Requirements (BCBS); Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Capital Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: stressed_total_capital_ratio
attributes.description: The minimum projected Total Capital ratio (Tier 1 + Tier 2) under the stress scenario over the projection horizon, expressed as a percentage. Regulatory minimum is 8% under Basel III.
attributes.references: Basel III Total Capital Requirements (BCBS); Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Capital Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: stressed_var_amount
attributes.description: The projected Value at Risk (VaR) for the trading book under the stress scenario, in reporting currency. Represents the maximum expected loss at a defined confidence level under stressed market conditions.
attributes.references: Basel III Market Risk Framework (BCBS); FRTB (Fundamental Review of the Trading Book); SEC Market Risk Disclosure

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The date on which this stress test run was submitted to the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., Federal Reserve for CCAR/DFAST). Null if not yet submitted or if this is an internal run.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Submission Deadlines; Dodd-Frank Act Section 165

attributes.name: submission_reference
attributes.description: The reference number or acknowledgement ID assigned by the regulatory authority upon receipt of the stress test submission (e.g., Federal Reserve submission tracking number). Null if not yet submitted.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Submission Portal; AxiomSL Regulatory Reporting Platform

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this stress test run record was last modified, including status changes, result updates, or metadata corrections.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Basel III Data Quality Standards

products.name: liquidity_metric
products.description: Daily liquidity risk measurement record capturing LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio), NSFR (Net Stable Funding Ratio), intraday liquidity positions, survival horizon, HQLA (High Quality Liquid Assets) buffer, net cash outflows, and available stable funding. Supports ALCO reporting, regulatory LCR/NSFR submissions to Fed/OCC/PRA, and internal liquidity stress testing.

attributes.name: liquidity_metric_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each daily liquidity risk measurement record. Primary key for the liquidity_metric data product in the risk domain.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) LCR/NSFR Framework

attributes.name: accounting_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.accounting_period. Business justification: LCR/NSFR liquidity metrics are calculated and reported for specific accounting periods, aligned with financial close cycles and regulatory reporting calendars. Essential for period-based liquidity ris

attributes.name: appetite_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.appetite. Business justification: Liquidity metrics (LCR, NSFR) are monitored against risk appetite statements that define the bank's tolerance for liquidity risk. The liquidity_metric table has regulatory minimums (lcr_regulatory_min

attributes.name: channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.channel. Business justification: Liquidity metrics measured at channel level for cash management (ATM network cash requirements, branch vault liquidity planning). Banks forecast channel-specific liquidity needs for operational effici

attributes.name: currency_id
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the liquidity metric amounts are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Supports multi-currency liquidity reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; BCBS LCR Standard

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Reference to the legal entity for which this liquidity metric record is calculated. Supports entity-level regulatory reporting to Fed, OCC, and PRA.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed); Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC); Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA)

attributes.name: liquidity_ratio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.liquidity_ratio. Business justification: Risk monitoring references treasury-calculated LCR/NSFR ratios for limit monitoring, breach detection, and regulatory reporting. Risk appetite framework requires tracking actual treasury-calculated ra

attributes.name: reporting_unit_legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal reporting unit or business line (e.g., retail banking, treasury, trading) for which the liquidity metric is computed. Supports ALCO sub-entity reporting.
attributes.references: Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO) Reporting Standards; Federal Reserve System (Fed)

attributes.name: risk_limit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_limit. Business justification: Liquidity metrics (LCR, NSFR) are monitored against regulatory and internal risk limits. The liquidity_metric table has is_breach and breach_severity flags but no reference to the specific limit being

attributes.name: stress_scenario_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.stress_scenario. Business justification: Liquidity metrics are calculated under various stress scenarios (baseline, adverse, severely adverse). The liquidity_metric table has stress_scenario_code field which should be replaced by FK to stres

attributes.name: alco_review_status
attributes.description: Status of the ALCO review process for this liquidity metric record. Tracks whether the metric has been reviewed, escalated for breach, or approved by the Asset-Liability Committee for regulatory submission.
attributes.references: Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO) Governance Framework; Federal Reserve SR 10-6

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the liquidity metric record was formally approved by the ALCO or risk officer for regulatory submission or internal reporting. Supports governance and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ALCO Governance Framework; Federal Reserve SR 10-6; SOX Section 302/906

attributes.name: available_stable_funding_amount
attributes.description: Total Available Stable Funding (ASF) representing the portion of capital and liabilities expected to be reliable over a one-year horizon. Numerator of the NSFR ratio.
attributes.references: BCBS NSFR Standard (October 2014); Federal Reserve NSFR Rule

attributes.name: breach_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of a regulatory liquidity breach based on the magnitude of the shortfall relative to the minimum threshold. Drives escalation level and remediation response timeframe per the institution's liquidity contingency plan.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 10-6; BCBS Sound Principles for Liquidity Risk Management; PRA Liquidity Standards

attributes.name: calculation_run_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the liquidity metric calculation was executed in the risk management platform. Supports audit trail, reprocessing identification, and T+1 regulatory submission deadlines.
attributes.references: SAS Risk Management; Moody's RiskAuthority; AxiomSL Regulatory Reporting Platform

attributes.name: calculation_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the liquidity metric record indicating whether the calculation is preliminary, final, restated, under review, or approved for regulatory submission.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed); Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC); AxiomSL / Wolters Kluwer OneSumX Regulatory Reporting Platform

attributes.name: central_bank_eligible_amount
attributes.description: Total value of assets eligible for central bank repo or discount window operations (e.g., Fed discount window, Bank of England repo). Represents the ultimate liquidity backstop available to the institution.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve Discount Window Policy; Bank of England Sterling Monetary Framework; BCBS Sound Principles for Liquidity Risk Management

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text commentary provided by the risk officer or ALCO analyst explaining material movements, breaches, restatements, or methodology changes for this liquidity metric record. Supports regulatory examination and internal audit.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 10-6; BCBS Sound Principles for Liquidity Risk Management; SOX

attributes.name: committed_facility_outflow_amount
attributes.description: Expected cash outflows from drawdowns on committed credit and liquidity facilities extended to customers and counterparties over the 30-day LCR stress horizon. Includes undrawn revolving credit facilities.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: consolidation_scope
attributes.description: Indicates whether the liquidity metric is calculated on a solo (single legal entity), consolidated (group-wide), or sub-consolidated basis. Determines the perimeter of assets and liabilities included in LCR/NSFR calculations.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; Federal Reserve LCR Rule; EBA LCR Delegated Act

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this liquidity metric record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX); BCBS Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation (BCBS 239)

attributes.name: encumbered_assets_amount
attributes.description: Total value of assets pledged as collateral or otherwise encumbered (e.g., repo, covered bonds, central bank pledges) and therefore excluded from the HQLA buffer. Critical for accurate HQLA calculation.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; EBA Asset Encumbrance Guidelines (EBA/GL/2014/03)

attributes.name: gross_cash_inflow_amount
attributes.description: Total expected gross cash inflows over the 30-day LCR stress horizon, capped at 75% of gross outflows per Basel III rules. Includes contractual loan repayments and securities maturities.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: gross_cash_outflow_amount
attributes.description: Total expected gross cash outflows over the 30-day LCR stress horizon before netting of inflows. Includes retail deposit runoff, wholesale funding outflows, and off-balance-sheet commitments.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: hqla_amount
attributes.description: Total stock of High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) after applicable haircuts, expressed in the reporting currency. Comprises Level 1, Level 2A, and Level 2B assets as defined under the Basel III LCR framework.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: hqla_level1_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) Level 1 Amount
attributes.description: Stock of Level 1 HQLA assets (e.g., central bank reserves, sovereign bonds with 0% risk weight) with no haircut applied. Highest quality component of the HQLA buffer.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: hqla_level2a_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) Level 2A Amount
attributes.description: Stock of Level 2A HQLA assets (e.g., agency MBS, covered bonds, sovereign bonds with 20% risk weight) subject to a 15% haircut. Capped at 40% of total HQLA.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: hqla_level2b_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) Level 2B Amount
attributes.description: Stock of Level 2B HQLA assets (e.g., non-agency RMBS, corporate bonds, equities) subject to haircuts of 25–50%. Capped at 15% of total HQLA.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: intraday_available_liquidity_amount
attributes.description: Total liquidity resources available intraday at the start of the business day, including central bank reserves, committed intraday credit facilities, and unencumbered liquid assets accessible within the day.
attributes.references: BCBS Monitoring Tools for Intraday Liquidity Management (April 2013); Federal Reserve Intraday Credit Policy

attributes.name: intraday_peak_liquidity_amount
attributes.description: Maximum intraday liquidity requirement observed during the reporting day, representing the peak net cumulative position across all payment systems (RTGS, ACH, SWIFT). Supports intraday liquidity monitoring per BCBS monitoring tools.
attributes.references: BCBS Monitoring Tools for Intraday Liquidity Management (April 2013); Federal Reserve Intraday Credit Policy

attributes.name: is_breach
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the liquidity metric breaches the applicable regulatory minimum threshold (LCR < 100% or NSFR < 100%). Triggers escalation to ALCO and regulatory notification procedures.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249); BCBS LCR Standard; PRA Liquidity Standards

attributes.name: lcr_buffer_amount
attributes.description: Excess HQLA above the regulatory minimum LCR requirement, representing the institution's liquidity cushion. Calculated as HQLA minus (net cash outflows × regulatory minimum LCR). Used in ALCO reporting and internal liquidity stress testing.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; Federal Reserve LCR Rule; ALCO Reporting Standards

attributes.name: lcr_ratio
attributes.description: The Liquidity Coverage Ratio expressed as a decimal (e.g., 1.25 = 125%). Calculated as HQLA divided by total net cash outflows over a 30-day stress period. Regulatory minimum is 100% (1.00) under Basel III / Fed LCR Rule.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249); OCC; PRA

attributes.name: lcr_regulatory_minimum
attributes.description: The applicable regulatory minimum LCR threshold for this entity as of the metric date (e.g., 1.00 for 100%). May vary by jurisdiction (Fed, OCC, PRA) and entity classification (GSIB, non-GSIB).
attributes.references: Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249); OCC; PRA; BCBS LCR Standard

attributes.name: liquidity_transfer_restriction
attributes.description: Indicates whether there are legal, regulatory, or operational restrictions on the transfer of liquidity between entities within the group (e.g., ring-fencing, local regulatory requirements). Affects consolidated vs. solo LCR/NSFR calculations.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; PRA Ring-Fencing Rules; Federal Reserve Regulation W

attributes.name: metric_date
attributes.description: The business date (as-of date) for which the liquidity metrics are calculated. Represents the daily snapshot date used for LCR, NSFR, and intraday liquidity reporting.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); BCBS NSFR Standard (October 2014)

attributes.name: metric_type
attributes.description: Classification of the liquidity metric record indicating which regulatory or internal liquidity measure is captured. Values: LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio), NSFR (Net Stable Funding Ratio), INTRADAY (intraday liquidity position), SURVIVAL_HORIZON, STRESS (internal stress test metric).
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; BCBS NSFR Standard; Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: net_cash_outflow_amount
attributes.description: Total net cash outflows over the 30-calendar-day stress period, calculated as total expected cash outflows minus the minimum of total expected cash inflows and 75% of total expected cash outflows. Denominator of the LCR ratio.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard (January 2013); Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

attributes.name: nsfr_ratio
attributes.description: The Net Stable Funding Ratio expressed as a decimal (e.g., 1.10 = 110%). Calculated as Available Stable Funding (ASF) divided by Required Stable Funding (RSF). Regulatory minimum is 100% (1.00) under Basel III.
attributes.references: BCBS NSFR Standard (October 2014); Federal Reserve NSFR Rule (12 CFR Part 249); EBA NSFR Guidelines

attributes.name: nsfr_regulatory_minimum
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) Regulatory Minimum
attributes.description: The applicable regulatory minimum NSFR threshold for this entity as of the metric date (e.g., 1.00 for 100%). Supports compliance monitoring against Fed/OCC/EBA NSFR rules.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve NSFR Rule (12 CFR Part 249); EBA NSFR Guidelines; BCBS NSFR Standard

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: The regulatory jurisdiction under which this liquidity metric is reported (e.g., US for Fed/OCC, UK for PRA, EU for EBA). Determines applicable minimum thresholds and reporting templates.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed); Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC); Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA); European Banking Authority (EBA)

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which this liquidity metric is calculated and reported. Daily for LCR/intraday; monthly or quarterly for NSFR and internal stress metrics. Drives scheduling in the regulatory reporting platform.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249); BCBS NSFR Standard; AxiomSL Regulatory Reporting Platform

attributes.name: required_stable_funding_amount
attributes.description: Total Required Stable Funding (RSF) representing the amount of stable funding required to support assets and off-balance-sheet exposures over a one-year horizon. Denominator of the NSFR ratio.
attributes.references: BCBS NSFR Standard (October 2014); Federal Reserve NSFR Rule

attributes.name: retail_deposit_outflow_amount
attributes.description: Expected cash outflows from retail deposits (stable and less stable) over the 30-day LCR stress horizon, applying Basel III run-off rates (3–10% for stable, 10–15% for less stable deposits).
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249); FDIC

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this liquidity metric data was sourced (e.g., SAS_RISK, MOODYS_RA, AXIOMSL, ONESUMX). Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: SAS Risk Management; Moody's RiskAuthority; AxiomSL; Wolters Kluwer OneSumX

attributes.name: survival_horizon_days
attributes.description: The number of calendar days the institution can survive under a combined idiosyncratic and market-wide stress scenario without accessing wholesale funding markets. Key internal liquidity risk metric reported to ALCO.
attributes.references: BCBS Sound Principles for Liquidity Risk Management (2008); Federal Reserve SR 10-6; PRA Liquidity Standards

attributes.name: unencumbered_assets_amount
attributes.description: Total value of assets that are free from legal, regulatory, or contractual restrictions and available to be monetized or pledged as collateral. Supports HQLA eligibility assessment.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; EBA Asset Encumbrance Guidelines; Federal Reserve LCR Rule

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this liquidity metric record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks restatements, corrections, and ALCO-driven adjustments to liquidity metric values.
attributes.references: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX); BCBS Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation (BCBS 239)

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of the liquidity metric record, incremented on each restatement or correction. Enables tracking of preliminary vs. final vs. restated submissions for regulatory audit purposes.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation (BCBS 239); AxiomSL Regulatory Reporting Platform

attributes.name: wholesale_funding_outflow_amount
attributes.description: Expected cash outflows from wholesale funding sources (e.g., interbank deposits, commercial paper, repo) over the 30-day LCR stress horizon. Key component of gross cash outflow calculation.
attributes.references: BCBS LCR Standard; Federal Reserve LCR Rule (12 CFR Part 249)

products.name: operational_risk_event
products.description: Operational risk loss event record capturing actual losses and near-miss incidents across the enterprise. Captures event date, discovery date, Basel event type category (internal fraud, external fraud, EPWS, CPBP, EDPM, BDSF, EFLF), affected business line, gross loss amount, recovery amount, net loss, root cause analysis, causal factors, control failure classification, insurance recovery, and legal/regulatory action status. Feeds SMA capital charge calculation and supports regulatory reporting to OCC/Fed/PRA. Sourced from GRC platform and internal loss database.
products.reference: Operational Risk Loss Event / Basel III SMA

attributes.name: operational_risk_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the operational risk loss event or near-miss incident record within the enterprise internal loss database. Primary key for the silver-layer data product.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) — Basel III Operational Risk Framework; OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk

attributes.name: affected_channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.channel. Business justification: Operational risk events (outages, fraud, process failures) must track the affected channel for root cause analysis, regulatory reporting, and remediation. Banks report operational losses by channel. R

attributes.name: approver_employee_id
attributes.description: Employee identifier of the risk manager or senior officer who reviewed and approved the operational risk event record, including the loss amount, root cause classification, and corrective action plan. Required for SOX and regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; OCC Supervisory Guidance; BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices

attributes.name: assessment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_assessment. Business justification: Operational risk events are often identified through RCSA (Risk and Control Self-Assessment) processes. The risk_assessment table captures RCSA records; operational_risk_event captures actual loss eve

attributes.name: compliance_breach_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.breach. Business justification: Operational losses often constitute compliance breaches (BSA/AML violations, Reg E failures). Linking supports MRA tracking, consent order remediation, and regulatory reporting where operational risk

attributes.name: country_id
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction where the operational risk event occurred. Used for geographic risk concentration analysis and cross-border regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3 Country Codes; BCBS Operational Risk Data Standards

attributes.name: currency_id
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the gross loss, recovery, and net loss amounts are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency consolidation and FX translation to reporting currency.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; BCBS Operational Risk Data Standards

attributes.name: deposit_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to account.deposit_account. Business justification: Operational loss events (fraud, processing errors, unauthorized transactions) are tracked by affected account for root cause analysis and loss attribution. Operational risk reporting requires account-

attributes.name: exam_finding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.exam_finding. Business justification: Regulatory exams identify operational risk events as findings requiring remediation. Banks track which operational losses were cited in exam findings to demonstrate remediation progress and prevent re

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.legal_entity. Business justification: Operational loss events are recorded against specific legal entities for Basel AMA/SMA capital calculations, regulatory loss data reporting, and financial statement loss provisions. Legal_entity_code

attributes.name: primary_operational_event_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Employee identifier of the risk event owner responsible for managing the investigation, root cause analysis, corrective action, and closure of the operational risk event. Sourced from the Human Capital Management System (Workday/SAP SuccessFactors).
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk; GRC Platform — Moodys RiskAuthority

attributes.name: accounting_date
attributes.description: The date on which the operational risk loss was recognized in the general ledger and financial statements. Used for IFRS 9 / CECL provisioning alignment and financial reporting reconciliation.
attributes.references: IFRS 9 — Financial Instruments; FASB ASC 450 Contingencies; BCBS Operational Risk Data Standards

attributes.name: affected_product_line
attributes.description: The specific banking product or service line affected by the operational risk event (e.g., Mortgage Lending, FX Trading, ACH Payments, Wealth Management, Trade Finance). Used for product-level risk attribution and LOB reporting.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Business Line Mapping; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the operational risk event record was formally reviewed and approved by the designated risk manager or senior officer. Supports audit trail and governance requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; OCC Supervisory Guidance; BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices

attributes.name: basel_event_type_category
attributes.description: Basel III Level 1 operational risk event type category classification. Values: 'internal_fraud' (Internal Fraud), 'external_fraud' (External Fraud), 'epws' (Employment Practices and Workplace Safety), 'cpbp' (Clients Products and Business Practices), 'edpm' (Execution Delivery and Process Management), 'bdsf' (Business Disruption and System Failures), 'eflf' (Damage to Physical Assets). Mandatory for SMA capital charge calculation and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: internal_fraud|external_fraud|epws|cpbp|edpm|bdsf|eflf — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Annex 9 Operational Risk Event Type Classification; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: basel_event_type_level2
attributes.description: Basel III Level 2 sub-category providing granular classification within the Level 1 event type (e.g., 'Unauthorized Activity' under Internal Fraud, 'Theft and Fraud' under External Fraud, 'Suitability Disclosure and Fiduciary' under CPBP). Supports detailed root cause analysis and trend reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product aligned with BCBS Annex 9 taxonomy]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Annex 9 Level 2 Event Type Sub-Categories

attributes.name: business_line_code
attributes.description: Basel III-defined business line classification code for the organizational unit where the operational risk event occurred. Standard Basel business lines include Corporate Finance, Trading and Sales, Retail Banking, Commercial Banking, Payment and Settlement, Agency Services, Asset Management, and Retail Brokerage. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: corporate_finance|trading_and_sales|retail_banking|commercial_banking|payment_and_settlement|agency_services|asset_management|retail_brokerage — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Operational Risk Business Line Mapping; BCBS 196

attributes.name: causal_factor_code
attributes.description: Standardized code from the enterprise causal factor taxonomy identifying the specific contributing factor(s) to the operational risk event (e.g., inadequate segregation of duties, system configuration error, third-party vendor failure, inadequate staff training). Used for trend analysis and KRI calibration.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; GRC Platform — Moodys RiskAuthority Causal Factor Taxonomy

attributes.name: ccar_dfast_applicable_indicator
attributes.business_glossary_term: Comprehensive Capital Analysis and Review / Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing (CCAR/DFAST) Applicable Indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this operational risk event is included in the operational risk loss scenario library used for CCAR and DFAST stress testing submissions to the Federal Reserve. Supports capital adequacy assessment under stressed conditions.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve CCAR Framework; Dodd-Frank Act Stress Testing (DFAST) Requirements; Federal Reserve SR 15-18

attributes.name: control_failure_type
attributes.description: Classification of the internal control failure that contributed to the operational risk event. 'design_failure' indicates the control was inadequately designed; 'operating_failure' indicates the control existed but did not operate effectively; 'no_control' indicates absence of a required control; 'override' indicates management override of controls; 'circumvention' indicates deliberate bypass of controls.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; COSO Internal Control Framework; OCC Supervisory Guidance; BCBS Operational Risk

attributes.name: corrective_action_due_date
attributes.description: Target completion date for the corrective action plan associated with this operational risk event. Used for management escalation tracking and regulatory examination readiness.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance; SOX Section 404; COSO Internal Control Framework

attributes.name: corrective_action_status
attributes.description: Status of the corrective action plan (CAP) initiated in response to the operational risk event to remediate the identified control failure. 'not_required' for near-miss events with no control gap; 'planned' for CAP defined but not started; 'in_progress' for active remediation; 'completed' for fully remediated; 'overdue' for past target completion date.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk; SOX Section 404; COSO Internal Control Framework

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the operational risk event record was first captured and persisted in the GRC platform or internal loss database. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS Operational Risk Data Standards

attributes.name: discovery_date
attributes.description: The date on which the operational risk event was first identified or discovered by the bank, which may differ significantly from the event date for latent losses. Used to measure detection lag and assess control effectiveness.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; Moodys RiskAuthority — Loss Event Capture

attributes.name: event_date
attributes.description: The date on which the operational risk loss event actually occurred or commenced. This is the principal real-world event date used for SMA capital charge period allocation and regulatory reporting. Distinct from discovery date and accounting date.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA); BCBS 196 Operational Risk Data Collection Exercise

attributes.name: event_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the operational risk event, including what happened, how it was identified, and the immediate impact. Supports root cause analysis, regulatory examination responses, and internal audit reviews.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk; PRA SS1/23; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: event_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to the operational risk event by the GRC platform or internal loss database (e.g., ORE-2024-00123). Used for cross-system reconciliation and regulatory reporting submissions to OCC/Fed/PRA.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; OCC Bulletin 2019-37; PRA SS1/23

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the operational risk event record. 'open' indicates active loss event under investigation; 'under_review' indicates root cause analysis in progress; 'closed' indicates fully resolved and signed off; 'near_miss' indicates no financial loss but control failure identified; 'pending_recovery' indicates awaiting insurance or third-party recovery.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; SAS Risk Management — Loss Event Workflow

attributes.name: event_title
attributes.description: Short, descriptive title summarizing the nature of the operational risk event (e.g., 'Unauthorized Wire Transfer — Treasury Operations', 'System Outage — Payment Processing Hub'). Used for management reporting and GRC dashboard display.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; GRC Platform — Moodys RiskAuthority

attributes.name: external_loss_database_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this internal loss event to a corresponding record in an external operational risk loss data consortium (e.g., ORX — Operational Riskdata eXchange Association). Supports benchmarking of internal loss experience against industry peers.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices — Use of External Data; ORX Loss Data Standards

attributes.name: gross_loss_amount
attributes.description: Total gross financial loss incurred from the operational risk event before any recoveries, expressed in the reporting currency. This is the primary input to the SMA capital charge calculation and must meet the BCBS minimum loss threshold for regulatory reporting (typically USD 20,000 for internal data collection).
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA Capital Charge; BCBS 196 Operational Risk Data Collection; OCC Reporting

attributes.name: insurance_recovery_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the total recovery amount attributable specifically to insurance policy payouts (e.g., fidelity bond, professional indemnity, cyber insurance). Tracked separately per BCBS guidance on insurance recognition in operational risk capital.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Insurance Recognition in Operational Risk; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: legal_action_status
attributes.description: Status of any legal proceedings or litigation associated with the operational risk event. 'none' indicates no legal action; 'threatened' indicates potential litigation notified; 'filed' indicates lawsuit filed; 'settled' indicates out-of-court settlement reached; 'judgment' indicates court judgment rendered; 'dismissed' indicates case dismissed.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 450 Contingencies; IFRS IAS 37 Provisions; OCC Supervisory Guidance; SOX

attributes.name: legal_provision_amount
attributes.description: Financial provision or reserve established in the general ledger for potential legal liability arising from the operational risk event. Recognized per IFRS IAS 37 or FASB ASC 450 when outflow is probable and estimable.
attributes.references: IFRS IAS 37 Provisions Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets; FASB ASC 450; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: loss_recovery_date
attributes.description: Date on which the recovery amount was received or recognized, whether from insurance, legal settlement, or third-party reimbursement. Used for cash flow timing analysis and SMA recovery component allocation.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA Recovery Component; BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices

attributes.name: loss_threshold_met_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the gross loss amount meets or exceeds the minimum loss data threshold (typically USD 20,000 per BCBS guidance) required for inclusion in the SMA Loss Component calculation and external loss data consortium submissions.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA; BCBS 196 Operational Risk Data Collection Exercise

attributes.name: near_miss_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this record represents a near-miss incident (potential loss that was averted) rather than an actual realized loss event. Near-miss events have zero gross loss but are captured for control environment assessment and KRI monitoring.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk

attributes.name: net_loss_amount
attributes.description: Net financial loss after deducting all recoveries from the gross loss amount (gross_loss_amount minus recovery_amount). This is the final economic impact figure used for P&L attribution, RAROC calculation, and management reporting.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA; IFRS 9; FASB ASC 450

attributes.name: recovery_amount
attributes.description: Total amount recovered from all sources (insurance, legal settlements, third-party reimbursements, collateral liquidation) following the operational risk loss event. Subtracted from gross loss to derive net loss.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — SMA; BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: regulatory_report_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the regulatory report or notification filed with the relevant supervisory authority (OCC, Fed, PRA) in connection with this operational risk event. Populated only when regulatory_reportable_indicator is true.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; PRA SS1/23

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this operational risk event meets the threshold or criteria requiring mandatory regulatory reporting to OCC, Federal Reserve, PRA, or other supervisory authorities (e.g., significant operational events, cyber incidents, large losses).
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; PRA SS1/23; BCBS Operational Risk

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: High-level root cause classification of the operational risk event following root cause analysis (RCA). Standard taxonomy: 'people' (human error, misconduct, inadequate training), 'process' (process failure, inadequate controls, procedural breach), 'system' (IT system failure, data quality, cybersecurity), 'external_event' (natural disaster, third-party failure, fraud by external party).
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Sound Practices; ISO 31000 Risk Management; OCC Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: root_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative of the root cause analysis findings, identifying the specific underlying cause(s) of the operational risk event. Supports corrective action planning, control remediation, and regulatory examination responses.
attributes.references: OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk; PRA SS1/23; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: sma_loss_component
attributes.description: Classification of how this event contributes to the SMA capital charge calculation under Basel III. 'loss_component' indicates the event feeds the Loss Component (LC) of the SMA formula; 'recovery_component' indicates a recovery adjustment; 'timing_adjustment' indicates a multi-year loss requiring temporal allocation per BCBS guidance.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) for Operational Risk; BCBS d355

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the originating operational system from which this loss event record was sourced (e.g., MOODYS_RISK_AUTHORITY, SAS_RISK_MGMT, GRC_PLATFORM, MANUAL_ENTRY). Used for data lineage tracking and ETL reconciliation in the Databricks lakehouse.
attributes.references: BCBS Operational Risk Data Standards; SOX Section 404 — Data Lineage

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the operational risk event record, including updates to loss amounts, recovery amounts, root cause classification, or status changes. Supports audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk

products.name: kri_measurement
products.description: Key Risk Indicator (KRI) master registry and periodic measurement record. Captures KRI definitions (name, risk category, calculation methodology, measurement frequency, data source, green/amber/red thresholds, owner, escalation path) and periodic readings (measurement date, actual value, threshold breach status, trend direction, owning business unit, escalation status). Links to risk appetite framework for threshold derivation. Provides the authoritative KRI taxonomy and monitoring data for enterprise risk dashboards, GRC reporting, and board risk committee oversight.

attributes.name: kri_measurement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each KRI measurement record in the enterprise risk monitoring registry. Primary key for the kri_measurement data product.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Principles for Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (BCBS 239)

attributes.name: appetite_id
attributes.description: Reference to the risk appetite statement from which the KRI thresholds (green/amber/red) were derived. Links this measurement to the governing risk appetite framework entry for threshold lineage and governance audit.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to channel.channel. Business justification: Key Risk Indicators are measured per channel (ATM downtime %, digital fraud rate, branch error rate). Channel-level KRI monitoring is standard in banking risk management for operational risk oversight

attributes.name: deposit_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to account.deposit_account. Business justification: KRIs track account-level risk metrics (dormancy rates, fraud incident rates, AML alert rates by account type). Risk dashboard reporting aggregates metrics by account segment for board reporting and ea

attributes.name: liquidity_position_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treasury.liquidity_position. Business justification: KRIs monitor specific liquidity position metrics for early warning indicators in risk appetite framework. Liquidity KRIs track intraday positions, tenor gaps, and scenario-based positions for breach d

attributes.name: risk_limit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_limit. Business justification: KRI measurements track against defined thresholds and limits. The kri_measurement table has green/amber/red thresholds and breach_status — these are operationally linked to risk_limit definitions for

attributes.name: actual_value
attributes.description: The observed or calculated numeric value of the KRI for the measurement period. Represents the raw measurement result before threshold comparison (e.g., NPL ratio of 0.0325, LCR of 1.42, VaR of 15000000). Unit of measure is defined in the unit_of_measure field.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: amber_threshold
attributes.description: The boundary defining the warning (amber) zone for the KRI. Values breaching this threshold trigger heightened monitoring and management attention but do not yet require board-level escalation. Derived from the risk appetite framework.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Workflow status of the KRI measurement record through the review and approval process. 'draft' indicates initial capture, 'submitted' indicates pending review, 'approved' indicates sign-off by risk governance, 'rejected' indicates the measurement requires correction and resubmission.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302/404

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the KRI measurement record was formally approved by the risk governance officer. Provides the audit timestamp for SOX and regulatory compliance purposes.
attributes.references: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302/404; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the risk governance officer who approved this KRI measurement record. Required for SOX and regulatory audit trail. Classified confidential as it identifies internal personnel.
attributes.references: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302/404; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: breach_status
attributes.description: The RAG (Red-Amber-Green) status of the KRI measurement relative to defined thresholds. 'green' indicates within appetite, 'amber' indicates warning zone, 'red' indicates limit breach. Drives escalation workflows and board risk committee reporting.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR Guidance

attributes.name: calculation_methodology
attributes.description: Description of the methodology or formula used to calculate the KRI value (e.g., 'HQLA / Net Cash Outflows over 30 days', 'NPL balance / Total Gross Loans', '99th percentile 10-day VaR using historical simulation'). Supports model governance and audit requirements.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7 Model Risk Management

attributes.name: commentary
attributes.description: Free-text narrative commentary provided by the KRI owner explaining the measurement result, contextualising any threshold breaches, or noting exceptional circumstances affecting the value (e.g., market dislocation, one-off events, methodology changes).
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this KRI measurement record was first created in the system. Provides the audit creation timestamp for data lineage, BCBS 239 compliance, and silver layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX)

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Categorical data quality assessment for this KRI measurement record. 'passed' indicates data meets quality standards, 'warning' indicates minor data issues that do not invalidate the measurement, 'failed' indicates the measurement should not be used, 'under_review' indicates quality assessment is pending.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: A numeric score (0.00 to 100.00) representing the assessed quality of the underlying data used to compute this KRI measurement. Supports BCBS 239 data quality attestation requirements and flags measurements with low data confidence for review.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239 Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which the KRI measurement data was sourced (e.g., 'SAS Risk Management', 'Moodys RiskAuthority', 'Murex', 'Core Banking T24', 'AxiomSL'). Critical for data lineage and BCBS 239 data quality attestation.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: escalation_authority
attributes.description: The governance body or individual to whom the KRI breach has been escalated (e.g., 'ALCO', 'Board Risk Committee', 'CRO', 'Risk Management Committee'). Defines the escalation path for each breach severity level.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Corporate Governance Principles for Banks

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the KRI breach was formally escalated to the designated escalation authority. Null if no escalation was required. Used to measure escalation timeliness against SLA targets.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: escalation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the escalation workflow triggered by a KRI breach. 'not_required' for green-status KRIs, 'pending' when escalation has been initiated but not yet actioned, 'in_progress' when remediation is underway, 'resolved' when breach is remediated, 'overdue' when SLA has been breached.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Governance Risk and Compliance (GRC) Framework

attributes.name: green_threshold
attributes.description: The upper or lower boundary defining the acceptable (green) zone for the KRI. Values within this threshold indicate normal operating conditions and no escalation is required. Derived from the risk appetite framework.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: is_board_reported
attributes.description: Indicates whether this KRI is included in board risk committee reporting packs (True) or is management-level only (False). Board-reported KRIs require higher data quality standards and formal sign-off per governance policy.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Corporate Governance Principles for Banks; Financial Stability Board (FSB)

attributes.name: is_regulatory_kri
attributes.description: Indicates whether this KRI is mandated by a regulatory body (True) or is an internally-defined management KRI (False). Regulatory KRIs (e.g., LCR, CET1, NSFR) require formal regulatory reporting and have prescribed minimum thresholds.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)

attributes.name: kri_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the KRI definition in the enterprise KRI taxonomy. Follows the format KRI-<CATEGORY>-<SEQUENCE> (e.g., KRI-CREDIT-0001). Links the measurement to the KRI master registry entry.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7 Model Risk Management

attributes.name: kri_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the KRI being measured (e.g., 'Non-Performing Loan Ratio', 'Liquidity Coverage Ratio', 'Value at Risk Utilisation'). Sourced from the KRI master registry.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: kri_owner_name
attributes.description: Full name of the individual accountable for the KRI measurement, remediation, and escalation. Typically a senior risk officer or business unit head. Classified confidential as it identifies internal accountability assignments.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) Risk Governance Guidelines

attributes.name: kri_owner_role
attributes.description: The job title or role designation of the KRI owner (e.g., 'Chief Risk Officer', 'Head of Credit Risk', 'Treasury Risk Manager'). Supports role-based escalation routing and governance reporting.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Corporate Governance Principles for Banks

attributes.name: legal_entity
attributes.description: The legal entity or subsidiary to which this KRI measurement applies. Supports legal-entity-level risk aggregation required for CCAR, DFAST, and regulatory reporting submissions (e.g., 'Banking Corp USA', 'Banking Corp UK Branch').
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST Requirements; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Resolution Planning

attributes.name: measurement_date
attributes.description: The business date on which the KRI value was observed or calculated. Represents the as-of date for the measurement, distinct from the record creation timestamp. Critical for time-series trend analysis and regulatory reporting periods.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: measurement_frequency
attributes.description: The prescribed frequency at which this KRI is measured and reported. Determines the cadence of data collection and dashboard refresh cycles (e.g., LCR is measured daily, NSFR monthly, ICAAP KRIs quarterly).
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III LCR/NSFR Standards; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR Annual Cycle

attributes.name: measurement_period_end
attributes.description: The end date of the measurement period over which the KRI value was calculated. For point-in-time KRIs this equals measurement_date; for flow-based KRIs this defines the close of the accumulation window.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) ASC 825

attributes.name: measurement_period_start
attributes.description: The start date of the measurement period over which the KRI value was calculated. For point-in-time KRIs this equals measurement_date; for flow-based KRIs (e.g., monthly loss events) this defines the beginning of the accumulation window.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) ASC 825

attributes.name: owning_business_unit
attributes.description: The line of business (LOB) or organisational unit responsible for managing and remediating this KRI (e.g., 'Commercial Lending', 'Treasury', 'Retail Banking', 'Trading'). Used for accountability assignment in GRC reporting and board risk committee packs.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) Risk Assessment System

attributes.name: prior_period_value
attributes.description: The KRI actual value from the immediately preceding measurement period. Stored on the record to support period-over-period variance analysis and trend computation without requiring a self-join. Expressed in the same unit_of_measure as actual_value.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST Reporting

attributes.name: red_threshold
attributes.description: The boundary defining the breach (red) zone for the KRI. Values exceeding this threshold indicate a material risk limit breach requiring immediate escalation to senior management or the board risk committee.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: The regulatory framework or standard to which this KRI is aligned (e.g., 'Basel III', 'CCAR', 'DFAST', 'IFRS 9', 'FRTB', 'Dodd-Frank'). Enables regulatory-specific filtering and reporting in AxiomSL / OneSumX submissions.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III; International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) IFRS 9

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Free-text description of the management action plan or remediation steps being taken to address a KRI breach or amber warning. Captured for audit trail and board risk committee reporting purposes.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) Risk Assessment System

attributes.name: remediation_due_date
attributes.description: The target date by which the remediation action for a KRI breach must be completed. Used to track SLA compliance and flag overdue escalations in GRC dashboards.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: risk_category
attributes.description: High-level risk taxonomy category to which this KRI belongs. Aligns with the enterprise risk taxonomy and Basel III risk classification framework. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: credit|market|liquidity|operational|compliance|reputational|strategic — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III Framework; Federal Reserve System (Fed) SR 11-7

attributes.name: risk_sub_category
attributes.description: Granular risk sub-classification within the risk category (e.g., 'counterparty credit risk', 'interest rate risk in the banking book', 'settlement risk', 'conduct risk'). Supports drill-down analysis in GRC reporting.
