attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Basel III Framework; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) Risk Assessment System

attributes.name: stress_scenario_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this measurement record represents a stress scenario value (True) rather than a base-case actual measurement (False). Stress scenario KRI readings are used in CCAR, DFAST, and ICAAP submissions.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST Stress Testing Requirements; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: stress_scenario_name
attributes.description: Name of the stress scenario applied when stress_scenario_flag is True (e.g., 'Fed Severely Adverse', 'Fed Adverse', 'Internal Baseline', 'COVID-19 Stress'). Null for base-case actual measurements.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve System (Fed) CCAR/DFAST Stress Testing Requirements; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) Stress Testing Principles

attributes.name: threshold_direction
attributes.description: Indicates the directionality of the KRI thresholds. 'higher_is_worse' means increasing values are adverse (e.g., NPL ratio, VaR). 'lower_is_worse' means decreasing values are adverse (e.g., LCR, CET1 ratio). 'range_bound' means both extremes are adverse.
attributes.references: Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance; Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239

attributes.name: trend_direction
attributes.description: The directional trend of the KRI value relative to the prior measurement period. 'improving' indicates movement toward lower risk, 'deteriorating' indicates movement toward higher risk, 'stable' indicates no material change. Used for forward-looking risk dashboard indicators.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Financial Stability Board (FSB) Risk Appetite Framework Guidance

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit in which the KRI actual value is expressed (e.g., 'percentage', 'basis_points', 'USD', 'ratio', 'count', 'days'). Ensures correct interpretation of the actual_value field across heterogeneous KRI types.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) Risk Metrics Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this KRI measurement record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, data lineage audits, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) BCBS 239; Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX)

products.name: model_validation
products.description: Independent model validation record for all risk models including IRB (PD/LGD/EAD), VaR, CVA, ECL, stress testing, and pricing models. Captures validation date, model under review, validation type (initial/periodic/triggered), scope, backtesting results (traffic light approach, Kupiec test), benchmarking outcomes, sensitivity analysis, identified model limitations, materiality assessment, MRA/MRIA findings, remediation requirements and deadlines, and regulatory approval status. Core artifact for SR 11-7 / SS1/23 model risk governance and OCC/Fed examination readiness.
products.reference: Model Validation / SR 11-7 Model Risk Management

attributes.name: model_validation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each model validation record in the risk domain. Primary key for the model_validation data product.
attributes.references: SR 11-7 Model Risk Management Guidance; OCC 2011-12

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the lead independent model validator (employee or third-party specialist) responsible for conducting and signing off the validation. Must be independent of model development per SR 11-7.

attributes.name: irb_model_id
attributes.description: Reference to the risk model under validation (e.g., IRB PD model, VaR model, ECL model, CVA model). Links to the model inventory record.

attributes.name: regulatory_exam_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_exam. Business justification: Model validations are reviewed during regulatory exams per SR 11-7 and OCC guidance. Examiners assess validation independence, frequency, and findings. Banks track which validations were reviewed in e

attributes.name: valuation_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.valuation_model. Business justification: Model validation applies to all risk models, including valuation models used for fair value measurement. Currently model_validation only links to irb_model, but valuation models also require independe

attributes.name: asset_class
attributes.description: Asset class to which the model under validation applies. Determines applicable regulatory capital framework and validation benchmarks. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: corporate|retail|sovereign|financial_institution|securitisation|equity|commodity|fx|rates|structured_credit|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III IRB; FRTB; IFRS 9

attributes.name: backtesting_exceptions_count
attributes.description: Number of days (for VaR) or observations (for IRB/ECL) where actual losses or outcomes exceeded model predictions during the backtesting observation window. Directly drives the traffic light classification.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Article 366; FRTB; SR 11-7

attributes.name: backtesting_result
attributes.description: Traffic light outcome of backtesting under the Basel/FRTB framework: green (0–4 exceptions, model acceptable), amber (5–9 exceptions, supervisory scrutiny), red (10+ exceptions, model presumed inadequate). Applicable primarily to VaR and IRB models.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Article 366 (Traffic Light Approach); FRTB Article 325bf; SR 11-7

attributes.name: benchmarking_outcome
attributes.description: Outcome of benchmarking the model's outputs against alternative models, industry benchmarks, or regulatory reference models. Indicates whether the model is consistent with, more conservative than, or more aggressive than benchmarks.
attributes.references: SR 11-7 Section III; OCC 2011-12; BCBS IRB Article 185

attributes.name: conceptual_soundness_rating
attributes.description: Rating for the conceptual soundness component of the validation, assessing whether the model's theoretical basis, assumptions, and mathematical framework are appropriate for its intended use.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this model validation record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under BCBS 239 and SOX.

attributes.name: data_quality_rating
attributes.description: Rating for the data quality and integrity component of the validation, assessing whether input data is accurate, complete, representative, and appropriate for the model's intended use.

attributes.name: is_regulatory_capital_model
attributes.description: Indicates whether the model is used in the calculation of regulatory capital requirements (RWA, CET1). Models flagged true are subject to heightened validation standards and mandatory regulatory approval under Basel III IRB.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III IRB; CRR Article 143; Fed SR 11-7

attributes.name: kupiec_test_result
attributes.business_glossary_term: Kupiec Proportion of Failures (POF) Test Result
attributes.description: Result of the Kupiec Proportion of Failures (POF) statistical test for VaR model accuracy. Tests whether the observed exception rate is statistically consistent with the model's confidence level (e.g., 99% VaR).
attributes.references: Kupiec (1995); BCBS Basel III Article 366; SR 11-7

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this model validation record. Used for change tracking, data lineage, and ensuring currency of validation status in regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: legal_entity
attributes.description: Legal entity within the banking group for which the model is approved and validated. Relevant for cross-border regulatory compliance (e.g., Fed approval for US entity, PRA approval for UK subsidiary).
attributes.references: SR 11-7; BCBS Basel III IRB; PRA SS1/23; EBA Guidelines on IRB

attributes.name: line_of_business
attributes.description: Line of Business (LOB) for which the model is used (e.g., 'Retail Mortgage', 'Corporate Lending', 'Trading — Rates', 'Wealth Management'). Supports LOB-level model risk aggregation and RAROC attribution.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; CCAR/DFAST LOB Segmentation; BCBS IRB

attributes.name: materiality_assessment
attributes.description: Assessment of whether identified model limitations and findings are material to the bank's financial position, capital adequacy, or regulatory compliance. Drives escalation to ALCO, Board Risk Committee, and regulators.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; BCBS Basel III IRB Article 185; IFRS 9; CCAR/DFAST

attributes.name: model_limitations_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of key model limitations identified during validation, including known weaknesses in assumptions, data gaps, out-of-sample performance concerns, and boundary conditions where the model should not be applied.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the model under validation at the time of this validation engagement (e.g., '3.2.1'). Critical for change management and ensuring validation findings are tied to the correct model version.

attributes.name: mra_count
attributes.description: Number of Matters Requiring Attention (MRAs) identified during the validation. MRAs are significant findings that require corrective action but do not immediately impair model use. Key metric for regulatory examination readiness.
attributes.references: OCC Examination Handbook; Fed SR 11-7; OCC 2011-12

attributes.name: mria_count
attributes.description: Number of Matters Requiring Immediate Attention (MRIAs) identified during the validation. MRIAs are critical findings that may require immediate suspension or restriction of model use pending remediation.
attributes.references: OCC Examination Handbook; Fed SR 11-7; PRA SS1/23

attributes.name: next_validation_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic validation of this model, determined by the model's risk tier, regulatory requirements, and any conditions imposed in this validation cycle.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; OCC 2011-12; BCBS Basel III IRB Article 185

attributes.name: observation_window_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the historical data observation window used for backtesting and performance testing. Defines the data cut-off for performance metrics reported in this validation.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Article 366; IRB Article 180; FRTB

attributes.name: observation_window_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the historical data observation window used for backtesting and performance testing in this validation. For VaR models, typically 250 trading days; for IRB models, minimum 5–7 years per Basel III.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Article 366; IRB Article 180; FRTB

attributes.name: overall_outcome
attributes.description: Final determination of the validation engagement: approved (model fit for purpose), approved_with_conditions (model usable subject to remediation), rejected (model not approved for use), or deferred (decision pending additional information).
attributes.references: SR 11-7; OCC Model Risk Examination Procedures; SS1/23

attributes.name: overall_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative rating assigned to the model following validation, reflecting aggregate assessment of conceptual soundness, data quality, and performance. Aligns with supervisory rating scales used in Fed/OCC examinations.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; OCC Model Risk Examination Procedures

attributes.name: performance_rating
attributes.description: Rating for the ongoing performance monitoring component, assessing whether the model produces accurate and stable outputs relative to observed outcomes (backtesting, benchmarking, sensitivity analysis).
attributes.references: SR 11-7; BCBS Basel III IRB Article 185; FRTB Article 325bf

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_status
attributes.description: Status of regulatory approval for models requiring supervisory sign-off (e.g., IRB models under Basel III, CCAR/DFAST models under Fed supervision). Tracks whether the regulator has approved, conditionally approved, or rejected the model.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III IRB Article 183; Fed CCAR Supervisory Guidance; OCC 2011-12

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Primary regulatory framework governing the model under validation. Determines mandatory validation requirements, documentation standards, and supervisory expectations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Basel_III_IRB|FRTB|IFRS9|CECL|CCAR|DFAST|SA_CCR|SMA|ICAAP|IRRBB|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS; Fed SR 11-7; OCC 2011-12; FASB ASC 326 (CECL); IFRS 9

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the model validation report or model approval application was submitted to the relevant regulator (Fed, OCC, PRA, EBA). Null if regulatory submission is not required.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III IRB; Fed CCAR; OCC IRB Approval Process

attributes.name: remediation_deadline
attributes.description: Agreed deadline by which all MRA/MRIA findings must be remediated and evidence of closure submitted to the independent validation function. Monitored by model risk governance and reported to the Board Risk Committee.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; OCC Examination Handbook; PRA SS1/23

attributes.name: remediation_status
attributes.description: Current status of remediation activities for findings identified in this validation. Overdue status triggers escalation to senior management and regulatory notification where required.

attributes.name: report_issued_date
attributes.description: Date the final model validation report was formally issued to model owners, senior management, and risk governance committees. May differ from validation_end_date if report drafting extends beyond fieldwork.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; OCC Model Risk Examination Procedures

attributes.name: scope_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the validation scope, including model components reviewed (conceptual soundness, data quality, performance testing, implementation), portfolios covered, and any explicit out-of-scope items.

attributes.name: sensitivity_analysis_outcome
attributes.description: Summary outcome of sensitivity and stress testing of model inputs and assumptions. Indicates whether model outputs are stable under parameter perturbations or exhibit material sensitivity to key assumptions.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; CCAR/DFAST Supervisory Guidance; IFRS 9 Sensitivity Disclosure

attributes.name: total_findings_count
attributes.description: Total number of findings (MRAs, MRIAs, observations, and recommendations) identified across all validation components. Used for trend analysis and model risk appetite monitoring.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; OCC Model Risk Examination Procedures

attributes.name: use_approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval status for model use following validation: approved (unrestricted use), restricted (use permitted within defined constraints), suspended (use temporarily halted pending remediation), prohibited (model must not be used).

attributes.name: use_restrictions
attributes.description: Narrative description of any restrictions placed on model use as a condition of approval (e.g., 'Apply conservative overlay of +15 bps to PD estimates', 'Limit use to portfolios with LTV < 80%', 'Not approved for CCAR submission without additional benchmarking').

attributes.name: validation_code
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the validation engagement, used in regulatory submissions, audit trails, and correspondence with examiners (e.g., MV-IRBPD-2024). Unique across all validation cycles.

attributes.name: validation_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the validation engagement was formally completed and the validation report issued. Null if still in progress.

attributes.name: validation_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the independent model validation engagement formally commenced. Used to measure validation cycle duration and SLA compliance.

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the validation engagement. Drives workflow routing, escalation, and regulatory reporting readiness.
attributes.references: SR 11-7; OCC Model Risk Examination Procedures

attributes.name: validation_team
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the independent model validation team or unit conducting the review (e.g., 'Model Risk Management — Credit Risk Team', 'External Validator: Moody's Analytics').

attributes.name: validation_type
attributes.description: Nature of the validation engagement: initial (first-time validation of a new model), periodic (scheduled annual/biennial review), triggered (event-driven review due to material change, performance deterioration, or regulatory finding), pre-implementation, or post-implementation.

products.name: assessment
products.description: Enterprise risk assessment and Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) record capturing periodic and event-driven evaluations across all risk categories. Assessment type (enterprise_risk_assessment, rcsa, thematic_review) distinguishes evaluation methodology. For enterprise assessments: captures assessment date, risk category, inherent risk rating, control effectiveness, residual risk rating, risk owner, methodology, findings, and action plan. For RCSAs: captures process name, risk event type, control description, control type (preventive/detective), control effectiveness rating, residual risk score, testing frequency, last test date, and remediation plan. Supports ICAAP, ORSA, board risk committee reporting, operational risk management framework, and GRC platform integration.

attributes.name: assessment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the risk assessment record. Primary key for the risk_assessment data product in the enterprise risk management lakehouse.
attributes.references: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) — Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk

attributes.name: appetite_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_appetite. Business justification: Risk assessments evaluate residual risk against the enterprise risk appetite framework. The risk_assessment table has residual_risk_rating and residual_risk_score — these are compared to risk_appetite

attributes.name: approver_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the senior risk officer or governance body representative who formally approved the risk assessment findings and ratings. Required for ICAAP, ORSA, and board risk committee reporting.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Handbook — Risk Assessment; BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk

attributes.name: assessment_assessor_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the individual who performed or facilitated the risk assessment. Supports accountability tracking, assessor independence validation, and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; OCC Handbook — Internal Controls

attributes.name: assessment_employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the individual or role designated as the accountable risk owner responsible for managing and monitoring the assessed risk. Supports escalation routing and risk ownership reporting to the board risk committee.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; Three Lines of Defence Model

attributes.name: exam_finding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.exam_finding. Business justification: Risk assessments are performed in response to exam findings to evaluate control effectiveness and residual risk. Banks document which risk assessments address specific exam findings to demonstrate rem

attributes.name: action_plan
attributes.description: Documented plan of remediation actions to address identified control gaps or elevated risk ratings. Includes action steps, responsible parties, and target completion dates. Tracked in the GRC platform for management information reporting.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; COSO ERM Framework; OCC Matters Requiring Attention (MRA) Guidance

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the risk assessment was formally approved by the designated approver. Marks the transition from 'under_review' to 'approved' status and triggers downstream reporting and action plan activation.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve SR 11-7; SOX Section 404; OCC Handbook — Risk Assessment

attributes.name: assessment_code
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the assessment, used in GRC platform references, board risk committee reports, and regulatory submissions. Format: RA-{CATEGORY}-{YEAR}-{SEQUENCE}.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; OCC Supervisory Guidance on Operational Risk

attributes.name: assessment_date
attributes.description: The principal business event date on which the risk assessment was conducted or formally initiated. Used as the reference date for inherent risk and control effectiveness ratings.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; IFRS 9 — Impairment; CCAR/DFAST Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: assessment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the risk assessment record within the GRC workflow. Drives escalation, approval routing, and reporting eligibility.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; Federal Reserve SR 11-7

attributes.name: assessment_type
attributes.description: Discriminator identifying the methodology and scope of the assessment. 'enterprise_risk_assessment' covers holistic enterprise-wide evaluations; 'rcsa' denotes Risk and Control Self-Assessment; 'thematic_review' covers targeted deep-dives; 'icaap' aligns with Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process; 'orsa' aligns with Own Risk and Solvency Assessment.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Handbook — Internal Controls

attributes.name: control_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the key control(s) in place to mitigate the identified risk. Captures control design, automation level, and frequency of operation. Used in RCSA documentation and internal audit evidence packages.
attributes.references: COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework; OCC Handbook — Internal Controls; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: control_effectiveness_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of how effectively the existing controls mitigate the identified inherent risk. Derived from control design adequacy and operating effectiveness testing. Drives residual risk calculation and remediation prioritization.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework; OCC Handbook — Internal Controls

attributes.name: control_type
attributes.description: Classification of the primary control mechanism associated with the assessed risk. 'preventive' controls stop risk events from occurring; 'detective' controls identify events after occurrence; 'corrective' controls remediate impact; 'directive' controls establish required behaviors.
attributes.references: COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework; OCC Handbook — Internal Controls; BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the risk assessment record was first captured in the GRC platform or risk management system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; BCBS BCBS239 — Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation

attributes.name: findings_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of key findings identified during the risk assessment, including control gaps, risk drivers, and significant observations. Used in board risk committee packs, ICAAP documentation, and regulatory examination responses.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; OCC Handbook — Risk Assessment; Federal Reserve SR 11-7

attributes.name: impact_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the severity of financial, operational, reputational, or regulatory impact if the risk event materializes. Combined with likelihood to derive the inherent risk score.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; COSO ERM Framework; OCC Handbook — Risk Assessment

attributes.name: inherent_risk_rating
attributes.description: Risk rating reflecting the gross level of risk before considering the effect of controls. Assessed based on likelihood and impact of the risk materializing in the absence of mitigating controls. Core input to the risk appetite framework and ICAAP capital assessment.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Handbook — Risk Assessment

attributes.name: is_material_risk
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the assessed risk has been classified as material under the enterprise risk appetite framework or ICAAP materiality assessment. Material risks receive enhanced monitoring, board-level reporting, and dedicated capital allocation consideration.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; EBA ICAAP Guidelines

attributes.name: is_regulatory_finding
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this risk assessment was initiated or escalated as a result of a regulatory examination finding, Matters Requiring Attention (MRA), or supervisory letter. Drives priority handling and regulatory response tracking.
attributes.references: OCC Matters Requiring Attention (MRA) Guidance; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; FDIC Examination Guidance

attributes.name: kri_code
attributes.description: Code referencing the Key Risk Indicator (KRI) associated with this risk assessment. Links the assessment to the quantitative KRI monitoring framework for threshold breach tracking and early warning signal generation.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; Institute of Operational Risk — KRI Sound Practice Guidance

attributes.name: last_test_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent formal test of the associated control was completed. Used to assess control currency, identify overdue testing, and support internal audit scheduling.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework; OCC Handbook — Internal Controls

attributes.name: legal_entity_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the legal entity within the banking group to which this risk assessment applies. Supports legal entity-level risk aggregation, regulatory reporting (CCAR, DFAST, ICAAP), and resolution planning.
attributes.references: BCBS239 — Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation; Federal Reserve LFI Supervisory Guidance; FSB Resolution Planning

attributes.name: likelihood_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the probability that the identified risk event will materialize within the assessment horizon. Combined with impact rating to derive the inherent risk score on the risk heat map.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; COSO ERM Framework; OCC Handbook — Risk Assessment

attributes.name: line_of_business
attributes.description: The business line or division to which the assessed risk is attributed (e.g., 'retail_banking', 'commercial_lending', 'investment_banking', 'wealth_management', 'treasury'). Used for LOB-level risk aggregation and CCAR/DFAST capital allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: retail_banking|commercial_lending|investment_banking|wealth_management|treasury|asset_management|payments|corporate_trust — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — Business Line Mapping; Federal Reserve CCAR Supervisory Guidance

attributes.name: methodology
attributes.description: Methodology applied to conduct the risk assessment. 'qualitative' relies on expert judgment; 'quantitative' uses statistical models (e.g., VaR, ECL); 'hybrid' combines both; 'scenario_analysis' applies stress scenarios; 'loss_data_analysis' uses historical loss event data.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III — IRB Approach; BCBS SMA Framework; Federal Reserve SR 11-7

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review or reassessment of this risk assessment record. Ensures timely refresh of risk ratings and control effectiveness in line with the risk appetite framework review cycle.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Handbook — Risk Assessment

attributes.name: process_name
attributes.description: Name of the business process or activity being assessed, primarily used in RCSA assessments (e.g., 'Loan Origination', 'Trade Settlement', 'AML Transaction Monitoring'). Provides process-level granularity for operational risk management.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; OCC Handbook — Internal Controls

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Regulatory or supervisory framework under which this assessment is conducted or reported (e.g., 'Basel_III', 'CCAR', 'DFAST', 'ICAAP', 'ORSA', 'SOX', 'FATCA'). Enables regulatory-specific filtering and submission mapping. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Basel_III|CCAR|DFAST|ICAAP|ORSA|SOX|FATCA|CRS|FRTB|CECL — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Framework; Federal Reserve CCAR/DFAST Supervisory Guidance; SOX Section 404; FATCA

attributes.name: remediation_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which all remediation actions in the action plan must be completed. Used for tracking overdue items, escalation triggers, and regulatory commitment management.
attributes.references: OCC Matters Requiring Attention (MRA) Guidance; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk

attributes.name: remediation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the remediation action plan associated with this risk assessment. Drives escalation workflows, management reporting, and regulatory commitment tracking in the GRC platform.
attributes.references: OCC Matters Requiring Attention (MRA) Guidance; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk

attributes.name: residual_risk_rating
attributes.description: Net risk rating after accounting for the effectiveness of existing controls. Represents the remaining risk exposure and is the primary metric for risk appetite comparison and escalation decisions.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; COSO ERM Framework

attributes.name: residual_risk_score
attributes.description: Quantitative residual risk score (typically on a 1–25 or 1–100 scale) derived from the product of likelihood and impact ratings after control adjustment. Used for risk heat map positioning and quantitative risk aggregation in the GRC platform.
attributes.references: BCBS Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk; SAS Risk Management — RCSA Module

attributes.name: risk_category
attributes.description: Primary risk taxonomy classification for the assessment. Aligns with the enterprise risk appetite framework and Basel III/IV risk category definitions. Drives routing to the appropriate risk owner and regulatory capital treatment.
attributes.references: BCBS Basel III Framework; Federal Reserve SR 11-7; OCC Handbook — Risk Assessment

attributes.name: risk_event_type
attributes.description: Basel II/III operational risk event type classification applicable primarily to RCSA assessments. Maps to the seven Basel operational risk event categories used in Standardized Measurement Approach (SMA) capital calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: internal_fraud|external_fraud|employment_practices|clients_products_business|damage_physical_assets|business_disruption|execution_delivery — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BCBS Basel II — Operational Risk Event Type Classification; BCBS SMA Framework

attributes.name: risk_owner_name
attributes.description: Full name of the designated risk owner accountable for the assessed risk. Retained as a denormalized field for reporting and audit trail purposes independent of HR system changes.

products.name: stress_test_factor_result
products.description: This association product represents the decomposition of stress test results by individual risk factors. It captures the contribution of each risk factor to the overall stressed capital ratios, RWA, ECL, and other stress test outputs. Each record links one stress test run to one risk factor with quantitative attribution metrics required for regulatory reporting (FR Y-14 Schedule A), model validation, and risk factor sensitivity analysis.. Existence Justification: In regulatory stress testing, each stress test run applies shocks to hundreds or thousands of risk factors simultaneously, and each risk factor is used across multiple stress test runs (different scenarios, different time periods, different portfolios). The business actively manages and reports on the decomposition of stress test results by risk factor—this is not an analytical correlation but an operational requirement. Regulatory submissions (FR Y-14 Schedule A) explicitly require factor-level attribution showing how each risk factor contributed to the stressed capital ratios.

attributes.name: contribution_to_capital_impact
attributes.description: The marginal contribution of this risk factor to the overall change in capital ratios (CET1, Tier 1, Total Capital) under this stress scenario. Expressed in the same currency as the stress test run. Used for factor attribution analysis.

attributes.name: contribution_to_ecl_impact
attributes.description: The marginal contribution of this risk factor to the change in Expected Credit Loss (ECL) under this stress scenario. Expressed in the same currency as the stress test run. Critical for CECL and IFRS 9 stress testing.

attributes.name: contribution_to_rwa_impact
attributes.description: The marginal contribution of this risk factor to the change in Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA) under this stress scenario. Expressed in the same currency as the stress test run. Required for Basel III regulatory attribution.

attributes.name: factor_loading
attributes.description: The portfolio exposure or loading to this risk factor at the as-of date of the stress test. Represents the dollar exposure, duration, or beta depending on the risk factor type. Used to calculate the factor contribution from sensitivity and shock size.

attributes.name: model_version_used
attributes.business_glossary_term: Model Version Used for Factor Result
attributes.description: Version identifier of the risk model that produced this factor-level result. May differ from the overall stress test run model version if factor-level models are versioned independently. Required for model risk management and validation.

attributes.name: sensitivity_coefficient
attributes.description: The partial derivative or sensitivity coefficient measuring the rate of change in the stress test output (capital, RWA, ECL) with respect to a unit change in this risk factor. Used for marginal sensitivity analysis and model validation.

attributes.name: shock_direction
attributes.description: The direction of the shock applied to this risk factor in this stress scenario. Values: up (factor increased), down (factor decreased), neutral (no shock applied to this factor in this scenario).

attributes.name: shock_magnitude

attributes.name: stressed_value
attributes.description: The shocked or stressed value of this risk factor applied in this specific stress test run (e.g., shocked interest rate level, stressed credit spread, shocked equity index value). Unit depends on the risk factor type.

products.name: model_deployment
products.description: This association product represents the deployment of an IRB model to a specific legal entity within the banking group. It captures regulatory approval status, portfolio scope, validation outcomes, and override activity for each model-entity combination. Each record links one IRB model to one legal entity with attributes that exist only in the context of this deployment relationship. Essential for capital adequacy reporting, regulatory compliance tracking, and model governance across the consolidated banking group.. Existence Justification: IRB models in banking groups are deployed across multiple legal entities, and each legal entity uses multiple IRB models for different asset classes and portfolios. Banks actively manage these deployments as distinct operational records, tracking entity-specific regulatory approvals, portfolio scope, validation outcomes, override activity, and RWA impacts. Model deployment is a recognized business process in model governance and regulatory capital management.

products.name: collateral_margin_call
products.description: Transactional record of all margin activity — margin calls, initial margin (IM) requirements and balances, and variation margin (VM) daily settlements — under CSA, CCP, and bilateral margin arrangements. Captures call/settlement date, margin type (IM requirement, IM posted/received, VM call, VM settlement), call direction (issued, received), amount, currency, delivery deadline, IM calculation methodology (ISDA SIMM, schedule-based), IM segregation status and custodian details, VM settlement status, netting set reference, dispute flag, dispute reason, dispute resolution status, settlement confirmation, UMR phase compliance, and regulatory flags (UMR, EMIR, Dodd-Frank daily VM). Tracks the full margin lifecycle from requirement calculation through call issuance, delivery, dispute resolution, and settlement confirmation per BCBS/IOSCO margin rules. This is the SSOT for all margin activity including IM balances and VM settlements.

attributes.name: journal_entry_id

attributes.name: override_flag

attributes.name: previous_net_value

attributes.name: previous_valuation_date

attributes.name: purpose

attributes.name: valuation_method

attributes.name: valuation_source
attributes.description: The origin of the valuation data, indicating whether it came from an internal pricing model, third-party appraiser, exchange pricing feed, market data vendor, broker quote, or index provider.

attributes.name: valuation_status
attributes.description: The current status of the valuation record. Final indicates approved and active, preliminary for initial calculations, pending review for valuations awaiting approval, disputed for challenged valuations, overridden for manually adjusted values, stale for outdated valuations requiring refresh.

attributes.name: valuation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the valuation was calculated, supporting intraday MTM (Mark-to-Market) for derivatives and trading book positions.

attributes.name: value_change_amount

attributes.name: value_change_percentage

products.name: haircut_schedule
products.description: Reference table defining haircut percentages applied to collateral asset categories for margin and exposure calculations. Covers Basel III standardized approach supervisory haircuts, internal model-based haircuts (own-estimate approach), CCP-specific haircuts, and bilateral CSA-negotiated haircuts. Captures asset class, credit quality step (CQS), residual maturity bucket, currency mismatch add-on, liquidity category, volatility adjustment methodology, regulatory framework (Basel III, EMIR, Dodd-Frank), effective date, and expiry date. Governs the reduction in collateral value recognized for credit risk mitigation and regulatory capital purposes.
products.reference: Basel III Haircut Schedule / Supervisory Haircuts

attributes.name: haircut_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the haircut schedule entry. Primary key for this reference table.

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Haircut schedules implement regulatory obligations (Basel III capital rules, EMIR margin requirements, UMR initial margin). The obligation drives the schedule requirements and supervisory haircut floo

attributes.name: currency_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.currency. Business justification: Haircut schedules vary by currency due to FX volatility and liquidity. Central banks publish currency-specific haircut tables for regulatory capital and margin calculations. Creating new FK.

attributes.name: instrument_classification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.instrument_classification. Business justification: Asset class and subclass determine applicable haircut; requires classification reference for consistency with regulatory frameworks. Creating new instrument_classification_id FK.

attributes.name: regulatory_taxonomy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.regulatory_taxonomy. Business justification: Regulatory framework field should reference taxonomy master for consistent reporting across Basel, EMIR, UMR regimes. Creating new regulatory_taxonomy_id FK.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval state of this haircut schedule entry within the governance workflow. Only approved schedules are used in production calculations.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this haircut schedule entry was formally approved. Supports audit trail and regulatory examination requirements.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authorized individual who approved this haircut schedule entry. Required for regulatory audit and SOX compliance.

attributes.name: asset_class
attributes.description: The broad category of collateral asset to which this haircut applies. Aligns with Basel III asset classification for credit risk mitigation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equity|government_bond|corporate_bond|covered_bond|asset_backed_security|cash|gold — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), CRR Article 197

attributes.name: asset_subclass
attributes.description: Granular sub-category within the asset class (e.g., sovereign bond, municipal bond, investment-grade corporate bond, high-yield bond). Provides additional segmentation for haircut determination.

attributes.name: bilateral_csa_haircut_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Bilateral Credit Support Annex (CSA) Haircut Percentage
attributes.description: Negotiated haircut percentage specified in a bilateral Credit Support Annex under an ISDA Master Agreement. May differ from supervisory haircuts based on counterparty agreement.
attributes.references: ISDA Credit Support Annex (CSA), Basel III paragraph 147

attributes.name: ccp_haircut_pct
attributes.description: Haircut percentage applied by a qualifying central counterparty (QCCP) for cleared derivatives and securities financing transactions. Reflects CCP-specific margin methodology.

attributes.name: collateral_eligibility_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this asset class is eligible as collateral under the applicable regulatory framework and internal policy. True if eligible, False if ineligible.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), CRR Article 197

attributes.name: concentration_limit_pct
attributes.description: Maximum percentage of total collateral pool that can be composed of this asset class. Prevents over-concentration in single asset types.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), CRR Article 208

attributes.name: confidence_level_pct
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level used in VaR-based haircut calculations. Basel III requires 99% confidence level for own-estimate haircuts.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), paragraph 149

attributes.name: credit_quality_step
attributes.description: The credit quality step assigned to the collateral asset under the standardized approach, mapping external credit ratings to regulatory risk buckets. CQS 1 represents highest credit quality (e.g., AAA to AA-), CQS 6 represents lowest investment grade. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CQS_1|CQS_2|CQS_3|CQS_4|CQS_5|CQS_6|unrated — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CRR Article 136, EBA Guidelines on Credit Quality Steps

attributes.name: currency_mismatch_addon_pct
attributes.description: Additional haircut percentage applied when collateral and exposure currencies differ. Typically 8% under Basel III standardized approach for major currency pairs.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), paragraph 151

attributes.name: currency_mismatch_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the collateral currency differs from the exposure currency. True if mismatch exists, requiring an additional haircut add-on per Basel III.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), paragraph 151

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this haircut schedule entry becomes active and applicable to collateral valuations and margin calculations.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which this haircut schedule entry ceases to be valid. Null indicates an open-ended schedule with no defined expiration.

attributes.name: holding_period_days
attributes.description: Assumed liquidation period for the collateral asset, used to scale haircuts. Longer holding periods require higher haircuts. Basel III specifies minimum holding periods by transaction type.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), paragraph 150

attributes.name: initial_margin_haircut_pct
attributes.description: Haircut applied to collateral posted as initial margin for non-cleared derivatives under the BCBS-IOSCO margin framework. Protects against potential future exposure.
attributes.references: BCBS-IOSCO Margin Requirements for Non-Centrally Cleared Derivatives (2015)

attributes.name: internal_model_haircut_pct
attributes.description: Haircut percentage derived from the bank's own internal Value-at-Risk (VaR) model under the own-estimate approach, subject to regulatory approval and minimum floors.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), paragraph 147-150, CRR Article 283

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: The legal jurisdiction or regulatory authority under which this haircut schedule applies (e.g., USA, GBR, EUR, CHE). Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent periodic review of this haircut schedule entry. Basel III and internal policy require regular review of haircut parameters.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), Internal Risk Policy

attributes.name: liquidity_category
attributes.description: Classification of the collateral asset based on market depth, trading volume, and ease of liquidation. Highly liquid assets (e.g., G7 sovereign bonds) receive lower haircuts.
attributes.references: Basel III: Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR), BCBS 238

attributes.name: lookback_period_days
attributes.description: Number of historical days used to calculate volatility and haircut estimates under internal models. Basel III requires minimum 1-year lookback for own-estimate approach.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), paragraph 149

attributes.name: minimum_haircut_floor_pct
attributes.description: Regulatory minimum haircut percentage that must be applied regardless of internal model estimates. Ensures prudent collateral valuation under all circumstances.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), FSB Haircut Framework

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next mandatory review of this haircut schedule entry. Ensures ongoing appropriateness of haircut parameters.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, rationale, or special instructions related to this haircut schedule entry. Supports operational transparency and knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: The primary regulatory regime under which this haircut schedule is defined. Different frameworks may prescribe different haircut methodologies and floors.
attributes.references: Basel III, EMIR, Dodd-Frank Act, MiFID II, SFTR

attributes.name: residual_maturity_bucket
attributes.description: The time-to-maturity band of the collateral instrument. Longer maturities typically attract higher haircuts due to increased interest rate and market risk.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), Annex 4

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The upstream system or platform from which this haircut schedule was sourced (e.g., SAS Risk Management, Murex, internal risk engine). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: supervisory_haircut_pct
attributes.description: The standardized haircut percentage prescribed by the Basel III supervisory framework for this asset class, credit quality, and maturity combination. Used under the standardized approach for credit risk mitigation.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), Annex 4

attributes.name: transaction_type
attributes.description: The type of collateralized transaction to which this haircut applies. Different transaction types may have different haircut requirements under Basel III.

attributes.name: variation_margin_haircut_pct
attributes.description: Haircut applied to collateral posted as variation margin for non-cleared derivatives. Typically lower than initial margin haircuts as VM covers current exposure.
attributes.references: BCBS-IOSCO Margin Requirements for Non-Centrally Cleared Derivatives (2015)

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version identifier for this haircut schedule entry. Increments with each revision to support audit trail and historical analysis.

attributes.name: volatility_adjustment_method
attributes.description: The statistical or econometric method used to calculate volatility-based haircut adjustments. Relevant for internal model approaches and dynamic haircut schedules.
attributes.references: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms (BIS, 2017), paragraph 148

products.name: eligibility_rule
products.description: Business rules, eligibility criteria, and concentration limits defining what collateral is acceptable and how diversified collateral portfolios must be across all arrangements (CSA, repo, secured lending, CCP).
